[Prop contraction  wrp to sup norm of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $\lambda>0$ and $\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$.
    Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a family of graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ that is closed under taking induced subgraphs and satisfies VSSM with rate $\alpha\in [0,1)$ and constant $C'>0$ for the hard-core model at fugacity $\lambda$. 
    Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the family of self avoiding walk trees of graphs in $\mathcal{G}$.
    Then there exists $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and $\eta_0>0$ such that for each $0<\eta_1<\eta_0$ there is an $\eta_2>0$ such that for any $(T,v)\in \mathcal{T}$, $r\in [\ell_\Delta(\lambda),r_\Delta(\lambda)]^{S^*_T(v,n)}$, $r'\in B_{\ell_\infty}(r,\eta_1)$ and  $\vec{\lambda}=(\lambda_u)_{u\in V(T)}$ with $\lambda_u\in B(\lambda,\eta_2)$ for each $u$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        | {F}_{T,n,\Vec{\lambda}}(r') -{F}_{T,n}(r)|\leq \eta_1.
    \end{equation}

[Lemma L:arc-original-grid of arXiv:2607.15966, 'Canonical Mandelbrot Cascades on Curves Are Rajchman'] Fix \(K\geq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).  
For every \(n\geq1\), there is a deterministic finite set
\[
        \Lambda_n(K,\varepsilon)
        \subset
        \{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^2:2^n\leq|\xi|<2^{n+1}\}
\]
such that
\[
        \#\Lambda_n(K,\varepsilon)
        \leq
        C_\gamma
        \bigl(1+K^2\varepsilon^{-2}\bigr)2^{2n}, 
\]
and, on \(\Omega_K\),
\[
        S_{\gamma,n}>\varepsilon
        \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
        \max_{\xi\in\Lambda_n(K,\varepsilon)}
        |\widehat{\mu_\gamma}(\xi)|
        >
        \frac{31}{32}\varepsilon.
\]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Let $\alpha>-1$, $\beta>0$ and   $0<p\leq q<\infty$. Suppose $\mu$ is a positive Borel measure on $[0,1)$. Then $\mathcal{C}_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}: A_{\alpha}^p(\mathbb{B}_n)\to A_{\alpha}^q(\mathbb{B}_n)$ is bounded if and only if $\mu$ is a $\lambda$-Carleson measure on $[0,1)$, where \[
    \lambda=\beta+(n+1+\alpha)\Big(\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}\Big).
\] That is
\[
    \sup_{r\in [0,1)}\frac{\hat{\mu}(r)}{(1-r)^{\lambda}}<\infty.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 14 of arXiv:2609.01889, 'Sufficiency of Hall's Condition for Graphic List Coloring'] Let $k\ge 4$ and let $C_k$ be the cycle 
$v_1–v_2–\cdots–v_{k}–v_1$.
Let $S=\{a,b,c\}$ and define a list assignment $L:V(C_k)\to 2^S$ by
\[
L(v_1)=\{c\},\qquad L(v_2)=\{a,c\},\qquad L(v_i)=\{a,b\}\,\,\text{ for all }3\le i\le k-1,
\]
and
\[
L(v_{k})=
\begin{cases}
\{b,c\}, & \text{if $k$ is even},\\[2mm]
\{a,c\}, & \text{if $k$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then $(C_k,L)$ satisfies Hall's condition, but $C_k$ is not $L$-colorable.

[Proposition prop:2 of arXiv:2410.23250, 'Strict inequalities for arm exponents in planar percolation'] Let $A, B$ be two increasing events such that $\mathrm P[A\circ B]>0$. For each $x,y\in \{0,1\}^n$, let $F(x,y)$ be the indicator  function that 
  $(A,B)$ occurs disjointly in $(x,y)$. Then we have
  \begin{equation}
    \mathrm P[A\circ B]=\mathrm P[A\cap \overline B] e^{-J},\quad\text{ where } J= \frac12 \int_0^{1} \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\mathbb E[D_iF(\omega,\omega_t)]}{\mathbb E[F(\omega,\omega_t)]} \; dt.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 45 (Point separation by scalar triangular responses) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $z=(x,A,q)$ and $\widetilde z=(\widetilde x,\widetilde A,\widetilde q)$ be
distinct elements of
$\mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathcal S_2,1}(H)$.  Then there is a scalar restarted
coefficient-defined triangular It\^o system of the form
\eqref{eq:finite-dimensional-triangular-test} whose complete response separates
$z$ and $\widetilde z$.  More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item a first-level difference is detected by a rank-one map
$C\in\mathcal L(H,\mathbb R)$ and $B=0$;
\item if the first levels agree but the area fields differ, a finite-rank skew
$K$ and
$B_K(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(K^*\operatorname{Anti}T)$ detect the difference;
\item if the first level and area agree but the covariance fields differ, a
finite-rank self-adjoint $S$ and
$B_S(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(S\operatorname{Sym}T)$ detect the difference.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the scalar triangular response class is point separating, although
\Cref{cor:no-finite-scalar-lossless-test} shows that no fixed finite subfamily
is globally lossless in infinite dimension.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.30155, 'Gradient Estimates Near the Natural Exponent for Very Weak Solutions to $A_p$-Weighted Qua'] Assume \eqref{struc} and \eqref{unidegen}. Suppose that $\omega \in A_{p}$ for some $p>1$. Then there exists
		$ \delta_0 = \delta_0(n,p,\nu,L,\Lambda,[\omega]_{A_{p}})>0$
		such that the following holds: Let $u \in W^{1,p-\delta_{0}}_{\omega,\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a very weak solution of \eqref{maineq}. If $ \mathbf{f} \in L^\gamma_{\omega, \mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for $\gamma \in [p-\delta_0,p+\delta_0]$, then $Du \in L^\gamma_{\omega, \mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for every ball $B_{2R} \Subset \Omega$ we have
		$$
		  \int_{B_{R}} | D u |^{\gamma} \, \omega\, dx
		\le C \left[ \omega(B_{2R})^{\frac{p-\delta_0-\gamma}{p-\delta_0}}
		\left( \int_{B_{2R}} | D u |^{p-\delta_0} \, \omega\, dx \right)^{\frac{\gamma}{p-\delta_0}}
		+ \int_{B_{2R}} | \mathbf{f} |^{\gamma} \, \omega\, dx
		\right],
		$$
		where $C$ depends only on $n,p, \nu,L,\Lambda$ and $[\omega]_{A_{p}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2608.31168, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality for surfaces in every codimension'] Let $J$ be a normal $1$-current in $\bR^2$.
Then, there exist non-negative measures $\lambda, \mu$; a family of injective arcs $\{ \gamma_{\sigma} \}_{\sigma \in \Sigma}$ of finite length; and a family of integral $1$-cycles $\{ \Gamma_{\xi} \}_{\xi \in \Xi}$, each of which is a countable union of finite-length loops, such that
\[
J = \int_{\Sigma} [\![ \gamma_{\sigma} ]\!] \, d \lambda(\sigma) + \int_{\Xi} \Gamma_{\xi} \, d \mu(\xi)
\]
with no cancellation of mass.

Moreover, the arc part has no boundary cancellation: for every open set $\Omega \subset \bR^2$, it holds that
\[
\mathbf{M}( \partial J ; \Omega) = \int \mathbf{M} ( \partial [\![ \gamma_{\sigma} ]\!] ; \Omega) \, d \lambda(\sigma)
\]
Consequently, if $\Sigma_{\Omega}$ denotes the collection of arcs having at least one endpoint in $\Omega$, we have
\[
\Sigma_{\Omega} := \{ \sigma : \gamma_{\sigma} \; \text{has an endpoint in } \Omega \}, \qquad \lambda(\Sigma_{\Omega}) \leq \mathbf{M} ( \partial J; \Omega).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2608.31168

body:
[Defn def:g2 of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] Let $\mathcal{F}_{c}$ denote the set of all measurable functions ${\boldsymbol f}=(f_1,\ldots,f_c):[0,1]\to [0,1]^c$ such that $\sum_{r=1}^c f_r(x)=1$ for all $x\in [0,1]$ (modulo almost everywhere equality).  For any $W\in \mathcal{W}_v$, define the functional ${G}_{W,\phi}(.): \mathcal{F}_c\to \mathbb{R}$ by 
\[
G_{W,\phi}({\boldsymbol f})
:=
\int_{[0,1]^v}
W(x_1,\ldots,x_v)\,\Phi_{\boldsymbol f}(x_1,\ldots,x_v)\,dx_1\cdots dx_v,
\]

\noindent where for ${\boldsymbol f}\in\mathcal F_c$,
\[
\Phi_{\boldsymbol f}(x_1,\ldots,x_v)
:=
\sum_{r_1,\ldots,r_v\in[c]}
\phi(r_1,\ldots,r_v)\prod_{a=1}^v f_{r_a}(x_a).
\]
title: Defn def:g2 of arXiv:2609.02682

body: In topology, a surface is a two-dimensional manifold. Some surfaces arise as the boundaries of three-dimensional solid figures; for example, the sphere is the boundary of the solid ball. Other surfaces arise as graphs of functions of two variables; see the figure at right. However, surfaces can also be defined abstractly, without reference to any ambient space. For example, the Klein bottle is a surface that cannot be embedded in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

[Prop PNT of arXiv:2605.13666, 'When Does the Dice Sum Become Prime?'] Let $\pi(x)$ denote the number of primes less than or equal to $x$. Then
\begin{alignat*}{2}
  \pi(x) &> \dfrac{x}{\ln{x}} &\qquad& (x \geq 17), \\
  \pi(x) &< 1.25506\dfrac{x}{\ln{x}} &\qquad& (x > 1). 
\end{alignat*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quantitative prime number theorem, Corollary~1 in~\cite{RS}

[Lem Whitney_McShane_noise_HP of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a metric space and equip $X\times\mathbb{R}$ with the
$\ell^1$-product metric $\overline{\rho}$.  Let
$\mu\in\mathcal{P}(X\times\mathbb{R})$ satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality with
constant $C>0$ with respect to $\overline{\rho}$.  Let
$Z_n\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} (X_n,\varepsilon_n)$, $n\in[N]_+$, be i.i.d.\ with law $\mu$, and
assume that $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_1]=0$.  For every
$f\in \operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho);1)$, define
$\mathbb{D}_N\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} ((X_n,\varepsilon_n))_{n=1}^N$ and
$\mathbb{D}_N^0\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} ((X_n,0))_{n=1}^N$.  Then, for every $\delta\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

        \mathbb{P}
        \Big(
            \Xi_N
            \le
            \sqrt{C\log(2N/\delta)}
        \Big)
    \ge
        1-\delta
.
\end{equation}

[Prop 4 of arXiv:2506.11358, 'Cardinalities in proofreading'] Let
$\overline{S}=((\overline{s}_1,\overline{u}_1),
(\overline{s}_1,\overline{u}_2),
\ds,\ds,(\overline{s}_M,\,\overline{u}_N))$
be the runs of two $(p,q,n)$-proofreaders. The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every set $I\sus[n]$ we have
$$
{\textstyle
\frac{1}{MN}\cdot\big|
\big\{
j\in[MN]\cc\;\text{$(\overline{s}_{v_j})_i=1$ for every $i\in I$}\big\}\big|=p^{|I|}\,.
}
$$
\item For every set $I\sus[n]$ we have
$$
{\textstyle
\frac{1}{MN}\cdot\big|
\big\{
j\in[MN]\cc\;\text{$(\overline{u}_{w_j})_i=1$  for every $i\in I$}\big\}\big|=q^{|I|}\,.
}
$$
\item For every set $I\sus[n]$ we have
$$
{\textstyle
\frac{1}{MN}\cdot\big|
\big\{
j\in[MN]\cc\;\text{$(\overline{s}_{v_j})_i=(\overline{u}_{w_j})_i=1$ for every $i\in I$}\big\}\big|
=(pq)^{|I|}\,.
}
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2609.01540, '2609.01540'] For every \(0<\beta<1/2\), the metric \(g\) may be approximated by a smooth
metric \(\check{g}\) on \(M\) such that
\[
 R_{\check{g}}\geq0,\qquad R_{\check{g}}\in L^1(M),\qquad
 |m(\check{g})-m(g)|<\beta,
\]
\[
 (1-\beta)g\leq\check{g}\leq(1+\beta)g.
\]
The distinguished end of \(\check{g}\) has harmonic asymptotics, and every
other end remains asymptotically flat after a constant dilation of its
coordinates.

body:
[Theorem 6 (Matrix Freedman) of arXiv:2604.27119, '\Large Applied Random Matrix Theory\relatedversion'] Consider a finite matrix martingale sequence $(\mtx{S}_0, \dots, \mtx{S}_n)$
consisting of $d_1 \times d_2$ matrices, real or complex.

Suppose that the elements of the difference sequence 
$(\mtx{X}_1, \dots, \mtx{X}_n)$ are uniformly bounded:
$\norm{ \mtx{X}_k } \leq B$.

Introduce the \term{conditional quadratic variation} sequence:
\[
V_k \coloneqq
	\lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j \mtx{X}_j^* \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\vee \lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j^* \mtx{X}_j \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\quad\text{for $k = 1, \dots, n$.}
\]
For parameters $v, t \geq 0$, we have the probability inequalities
\begin{align}

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq \sqrt{2 v t} + Bt/3 \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \, \econst^{-t}; \\

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq t \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \exp\left( \frac{-t^2/2}{v + Bt/3} \right).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matrix Freedman

[Lemma 29 (Refined ring lemma for \RCP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $(G,\Theta)$ be a tame ADT satisfying (Z1)--(Z4), and assume that (Z2) is strengthened to (Z2$'$). Let $r:V\to(0,\infty)$ denote the radius function of an embedding in the plane. Then there exists a constant $C=C(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1)$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the constant in (Z2$'$) and $\varepsilon_1$ is the tameness constant in the angle upper bound $\Theta(e)\leq \pi-\varepsilon_1$, such that for every edge $u\sim v$,
\[
\frac{r(v)}{r(u)} > e^{-C\cdot S(u)},
\]
where $S(u)=\sum_{v'\sim u}\deg(v')$ is the \emph{flower degree} of $u$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Refined ring lemma for \RCP

[Defn 83 (Product of diagrams) of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be two isomorphism classes of diagrams on the same set $A$. Define the product diagram $\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2$ by specifying the following data:
\begin{itemize}
\item $A_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}=A$
\item $I_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}=I_{\Gamma_1} \sqcup I_{\Gamma_2}$
\item $E_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}=E_{\Gamma_1} \sqcup E_{\Gamma_2}$ 
\item $s_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}|_{E_{\Gamma_i}}=s_{\Gamma_i}$
\item $t_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}|_{E_{\Gamma_i}}=t_{\Gamma_i}$
\item $W^V_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}|_{A}=W^V_{\Gamma_1} \cdot W^V_{\Gamma_2}$
\item $W^V_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}|_{I_{\Gamma_i}}=W^V_{\Gamma_i}$
\item $W^E_{\Gamma_1 \cdot \Gamma_2}|_{E_{\Gamma_i}}=W^E_{\Gamma_i}$
\end{itemize} 
Here we assume that the sets $I_{\Gamma_1}$ and $I_{\Gamma_2}$, and $E_{\Gamma_1}$ and
$E_{\Gamma_2}$ respectively, are disjoint. The orders on linearly ordered sets are extended to the disjoint union of by letting $x<y$ for $x$ in the first summand and $y$ in the second summand.
title: Product of diagrams

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be bounded and open with $C^1$ boundary, $T>0$, and let $u,\tilde u$ be smooth on $\overline{U_T}$ and solve $u_t=\Delta u$ and $\tilde u_t=\Delta\tilde u$ in $U_T$ with the same values on $\partial U\times[0,T]$. If $u(\cdot,T)=\tilde u(\cdot,T)$ in $U$, then $u\equiv\tilde u$ in $\overline{U_T}$: two solutions that agree at one later time agreed all along. (Regularity up to the boundary is load-bearing only through what the proof uses: the difference must lie in $H^1_0(U)$ at each time and the integrations by parts below must be legitimate; mere continuity on $\overline{U_T}$ with no regularity of $\partial U$ does not supply this.) Quantitatively, for the difference $w$ the function $t\mapsto\log\|w(t)\|_{L^2(U)}^2$ is convex on $[0,T]$, so $\|w(t)\|_{L^2}\le\|w(0)\|_{L^2}^{1-t/T}\,\|w(T)\|_{L^2}^{t/T}$ (conditional stability of Holder type for $0<t<T$). The abstract form: if $A$ is a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ and $v(t)=e^{-tA}v_0$, then $\|v(t)\|^2$ is log-convex and $v(T)=0$ forces $v_0=0$. Backward uniqueness must not be confused with backward stability or backward solvability, both of which fail.
U bounded open in R^n with C^1 boundary
u, tilde u smooth on the closure of U_T and solving the heat equation in U_T (enough regularity that the difference lies in H^1_0(U) at each time and the integrations by parts are valid)
u = tilde u on the lateral boundary partial U x [0,T]
u(.,T) = tilde u(.,T) on U
abstract version: A nonnegative self-adjoint on a Hilbert space, v(t) = e^{-tA} v_0

[Proposition 11 (Box eigenvalue bound) of arXiv:2609.02784, 'Maximizing the fundamental Laplace--Neumann \\ eigenvalue on quadrilaterals'] Let $\mathcal B \subset P_{\mathrm C}$ be a closed axis-aligned box on which $M(\p) \succ 0$, so that the generalized eigenvalues of the pencil are well-defined, and suppose a certified enclosure
\[
  \lambda_1(\p) \in \bigl[\underline\lambda_1(\mathcal B),\, \overline\lambda_1(\mathcal B)\bigr]
  \quad \text{for all } \p \in \mathcal B,
  \qquad \underline\lambda_1(\mathcal B) > 0,
\]
is available. Write $Q(\mathcal B) := \sup_{\p \in \mathcal B} |Q_\p|$. If
\[
  Q(\mathcal B)\, \overline\lambda_1(\mathcal B) \;<\; \pi^2,
\]
then $0 < |Q_\p|\,\lambda_1(\p) < \pi^2$ on $\mathcal B$.

[Theorem 8 (Distance to a random subspace) of arXiv:2608.30722, 'Intermediate Singular Values of Random Matrices\\ under Second-Moment and Anti-Concentrati'] There exist constants $c, C, \lambda > 0$ depending only on $a$ and $b$ such
that the following holds for all $1 \le d \le \lambda n/\log n$. Let
$X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be a random vector with independent entries satisfying
\textnormal{(A1)--(A2)}, and let
$M \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n-d)}$ be an independent random matrix whose
columns satisfy \textnormal{(A1)--(A2)}. Let $H$ denote the column span of
$M$. Then, for every $t\ge0$,
\[
  \mathcal{L}(P_{H^\perp}X,\, t\sqrt{d})
  \;\le\; (Ct)^d + e^{-cn}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 (Automatic prior-score energy lower bound) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Assume $\Tr\Cov(X_0)<\infty$ and let $\mu_t=\E X_t$.  For every $t>0$,
\begin{equation}

\frac1d\E\|s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)\|^2
\ge
\frac{d}{\Tr\Cov(X_t)}
=
\frac{d}{a_t^2\Tr\Cov(X_0)+d\Delta_t}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $d^{-1}\Tr\Cov(X_0)\le C_0$, then
\begin{equation}

\frac1d\E\|s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)\|^2
\ge
\frac1{a_t^2C_0+\Delta_t}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Automatic prior-score energy lower bound

Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: In the spatially constant reduction with globally Lipschitz reaction noise, total mass S=sum_i U_i is nonnegative and its drift is at most K0+K1*S. On the positive orthant, |U|<=S, so the total diffusion coefficient satisfies ||sum_i g_i(U)||<=C*(1+S). Ito applied to S^2, stopping at levelN, gives E S_(t wedge tauN)^2 <= C_T*(1+S0^2). The standard stopped maximal estimate gives a uniform bound on E sup_(s<=T) S_(s wedge tauN)^2, hence the finite-dimensional system does not explode. Check: The diffusion bound follows from global Lipschitz continuity of each g_i and positivity, rather than from cancellation between its noises. Markov inequality at the exit time then makes P(tauN<=T) tend to zero. Obstruction: For spatially varying solutions, an L1 mass bound is not an L-infinity or high-Lp bound. Different species have different transport fields, so their sum does not satisfy a closed scalar advection-diffusion equation. The deterministic triangular duality argument has not been transferred in this generality. The2026 entropy-dissipation paper treats specially chosen regularizing noise, not every source-admissible coefficient.

A function holomorphic on an open set U equals its Taylor series locally: around any z0 in U it has a power series expansion converging on every disk centered at z0 contained in U. In particular holomorphic functions are infinitely differentiable.

body: Let (gamma_h, gamma_h^d): I -> Delta_1 be a spacelike Legendre curve with curvature (m_h, n_h), i.e. gamma_h^s = gamma_h wedge gamma_h^d and gamma_h' = m_h gamma_h^s, (gamma_h^d)' = n_h gamma_h^s, (gamma_h^s)' = m_h gamma_h - n_h gamma_h^d. If there is a smooth phi: I -> R with m_h(t) cosh phi(t) + n_h(t) sinh phi(t) = 0 for all t, the hyperbolic evolute is HE(gamma_h, gamma_h^d)(t) = cosh phi(t) gamma_h(t) + sinh phi(t) gamma_h^d(t); phi is unique when {t : n_h(t) != 0} is dense in I. Where n_h != 0 the condition reads tanh phi = -m_h/n_h, so it requires |m_h| < |n_h|.

[Lem multiplication of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Let $s\ge 0$, $s_1\geq s$, and $s_2\ge s$
be real numbers satisfying
\[
s_1+s_2 >s+ \frac{d}2.
\]
Then, the pointwise multiplication of functions extends uniquely to a continuous bilinear map 
\[
H^{s_1}(\mathcal O) \times H^{s_2}(\mathcal O) \rightarrow H^{s}(\mathcal O),
\]
namely there exists a constant $C$, depending on 
$s, s_1, s_2, d$ such that, for every $f_1\in H^{s_1}(\mathcal O)$ and $f_2\in H^{s_2}(\mathcal O)$ it holds that 
$f_1f_2\in H^{s}(\mathcal O)$ and
\[
\norm{f_1f_2}_{H^{s}(\mathcal O)}\leq C
\norm{f_1}_{H^{s_1}(\mathcal O)}\norm{f_2}_{H^{s_2}(\mathcal O)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Assuming one-way functions, the GPX posterior-hard family admits positive smooth polynomial-LSI regularizations with bounded covariance, polynomial-time generative descriptions and polynomially accurate computable forward-score networks. Their actual LSI constants lie between D^100/96 and O(D^206(log D)^2); norm-one selector observations with noise Theta((log D)^-2) put their ratios between Omega(D^100(log D)^4) and O(D^206(log D)^6). A polynomial-time posterior sampler achieving TV 10^-6 for at least 1-10^-6 of observations would contradict GPX hardness. The computational interface is polynomial-accuracy score networks, not a unit-cost exact-score oracle. No novelty or independent-check claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:869d142b2cb0ffd730879486ba8359ad49b02ade4d4afdfee77a95ce06c53e74","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/86/869d142b2cb0ffd730879486ba8359ad49b02ade4d4afdfee77a95ce06c53e74.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3ae8d2385a1800d70b615980f17dcc27d6ab151acb3a095b1b92bed95d074599","bundle_entry_key":"draft-posterior-hardness-polynomial-lsi-regularization","bundle_id":"population.w740-t411-c007-v2-reviewed-supersede","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"posterior sampling and functional inequalities","draft":"w740/bundle_003_r1.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.sampling:draft-posterior-hardness-polynomial-lsi-regularization","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Posterior-sampling hardness with polynomial log-Sobolev priors — C007 v2

Status: proof (unaudited). Source/interface inspection, the 31 original checks, and constructive lemma C008 with 38 additional exact coefficient checks recorded; independent review remains required. This is a proposed proof of T411 Target 2. It makes no novelty claim. Target 1 remains open.

## Computational scope and statement

Use the computational model of Gupta, Jalal, Parulekar, Price and Xun, arXiv:2402.12727v2: a diffusion prior is supplied through polynomial-size, polynomially bounded, effectively constructible approximate forward-score networks. Gaussian sampling primitives and polynomial-precision computations are understood as in that source. This is not a lower bound against a unit-cost oracle for exact prior scores.

Assume one-way functions exist. For all sufficiently large ambient dimensions D in the source's hard family, there are positive smooth priors M_D, coordinate-selector matrices A_D of norm one, and Gaussian observation standard deviations sigma_D=Theta((log D)^(-2)), with the following properties.

* The priors have explicit polynomial-time generative descriptions, bounded covariance operator, and polynomially accurate forward scores witnessed by polynomial-size ReLU networks (specifically 8-well-modeled in Definition 1.1).
* Their actual optimal LSI constants satisfy

  D^100/96 <= C_LS(M_D) <= C D^206 (log D)^2.

* Therefore their actual observation ratios satisfy

  c D^100 (log D)^4 <= ||A_D||^2 C_LS(M_D)/sigma_D^2
       <= C' D^206 (log D)^6.

* There is no polynomial-time sampler which, with probability at least 1-10^(-6) over observations, outputs a law within TV 10^(-6) of the posterior, using the stated computable score interface and the generative description. Such a sampler would invert a one-way function.

Constants may depend on the fixed source construction, not on D. The polynomial exponents are chosen to keep the approximation budget explicit; no optimal exponent or matching boundary is asserted.

The LSI convention is Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E||grad f||^2. The final priors contain nondegenerate Gaussian noise: the finite-coin approximation below is of the center sampler, not a claim that a discrete finite-grid output approximates a continuous law in TV.

## 1. Primary-source input

Take the hard family P_D from Theorem 1.8 / Lemma 3.5 of Gupta et al. The construction is Definition 3.2, scaled in Definition 3.3; its well-modeled score networks are Corollary 3.6, with their construction completed in Appendix C.8. It has these properties:

1. A_D selects the encoded last coordinates, so A_D A_D^T=I and ||A_D||=1. Observation noise is beta_D=Theta((log D)^(-2)). A (1/10,1/10) posterior sampler, in Definitions 1.2 and 1.5, would contradict one-way-function hardness. The success probability is over the observation.
2. P_D is 10-well-modeled: at every D^(-10)<=v<=D^10 its smoothed score has squared L2 approximation error less than D^(-10)/v^2, by a polynomial-size network with polynomially bounded weights. These are the source's effective constructions from the forward one-way-function circuit; no preimage is supplied.
3. Each seed is uniform fair bits. Given the seed, the first coordinates are independent N(seed_i,1/R_D^2). Each remaining coordinate is an independent phase-0 or phase-half discretized centered Gaussian, divided by R_D, where R_D=Theta(log D), and its phase is specified by the forward function of the seed. The unscaled grid spacing and its reciprocal are polynomially bounded.

C008 supplies an explicit polynomial-time construction for the scalar phase-lattice score networks. Its exact assumptions, normalized summation algorithm, truncation bounds, finite-precision error budget, rational ReLU interpolation and Gaussian tail proof are in proofs/C008_uniform_phase_lattice_scores.md. This replaces the sketch of effective scalar-network generation in C007 v1; it does not assume that network existence alone implies an algorithm.

Choose a fixed K large enough to include the source scalar grid spacings, smoothing scales and rescalings by R_D. C008 gives squared scalar score error at most 3D^(-2q), and output magnitude O((q+K)log D/u), for any fixed sufficiently large q. Taking q>K+1 gives precisely the bounded-output form needed by the source's scalar primitive construction in Lemma C.11. The source's polynomial-size, constant-depth network compositions have polynomial sensitivity to inverse-polynomial coefficient rounding; enlarge q by that fixed sensitivity exponent and by the coordinate-summation budget. The construction constant in the source can be fixed sufficiently large once to accommodate these error budgets. All exponents are fixed before D varies.

Lemma C.15 (PDF p.32) explicitly composes a vertex decoder, the forward circuit, these scalar score primitives, and ReLU switches. At large scales Lemmas C.19/C.20 (PDF p.38) use product two-Gaussian-mixture scores; those are finite Gaussian sums with explicitly evaluable coefficients and the same polynomial-window interpolation argument. Ordinary conditional Gaussian scores are linear. Consequently the forward networks used below are generated with polynomial work and polynomial precision. No conditional seed probability or circuit inverse is computed. The model remains polynomial-accuracy Gaussian primitives, not an exact-real score oracle.

Both phase lattices are symmetric about zero. Therefore E P_D=0; its raw second-moment operator is bounded by an absolute constant, also stated in the well-modeled condition. The first coordinate is exactly

(1/2)N(1,1/R_D^2)+(1/2)N(-1,1/R_D^2).

The conditional lattice Gaussian has uniform Gaussian-type tails for the source spacings <=1: its normalizer is bounded below by c/epsilon, and its tail sums are bounded above by C exp(-T^2/4)/epsilon. These bounds follow by counting grid points in [-1,1] and comparing the tails with the Gaussian integral. In particular all coordinate fourth moments are uniformly bounded and E||X||^4=O(D^2). No independence between the different encoded phase choices is needed for this fourth-moment conclusion.

## 2. A finite-coin center sampler

There is a polynomial-coin deterministic map S_D:{-1,1}^k->R^D, k=O(D log D), such that

W2(P_D,Law(S_D)) <= D^(-130),
||S_D(b)|| <= B_D:=4D^2 for all b,
E[S_D S_D^T] <= K I

for an absolute K and all sufficiently large D. Here is a finite algorithmic construction, not an enumeration of the exponentially many seeds.

Sample the seed with its exact fair bits and evaluate its forward circuit. For each scalar Gaussian or phase-lattice Gaussian primitive, truncate the unscaled variable at absolute value D. The tail second-moment contribution is exponentially small in D^2, uniformly in the two lattice phases; this uses the preceding elementary tail-sum comparison. For a continuous Gaussian, quantize its truncated value to mesh D^(-300). For a lattice primitive retain the actual grid points in [-D,D]. There are polynomially many points because the grid reciprocal is polynomially bounded.

For each of the Gaussian and two lattice-phase tables, approximate its finite probabilities by nonnegative dyadic probabilities, of common denominator 2^b, with total mass one and total variation error at most D^(-1000). One can round all but one weight down and assign the remaining mass to the last cell; use b large enough that the number of cells times 2^(-b) is below the requested error, and compute each weight to a further fixed number of guard bits. Thus b=O(log D), with a sufficiently large fixed constant. The Gaussian bin probabilities and lattice weights are computable to this precision in polynomial time, for example by Taylor approximation and integration on the bounded interval; their arguments have polynomial size. Standard elementary series likewise approximate R_D and the grid spacing to the finer mesh precision. No inversion of the forward circuit occurs.

Use b fresh fair bits and the dyadic CDF to choose a cell exactly, independently for each primitive. Couple this with the ideal primitive by a common-part coupling on the finite cells. On a table mismatch the squared unscaled error is at most O(D^2); the total mismatch probability over O(D) coordinates is O(D^(-999)). On a match, continuous quantization contributes at most D^(-300) per coordinate, and parameter rounding can be made smaller. Gaussian and lattice tail second moments contribute exp(-cD^2) times a polynomial. Summing the squared errors proves the stated global W2 bound for sufficiently large D. All values after division by R_D>=1 have absolute value at most 3D, so the norm bound 4D^2 is valid. The tables and the circuit have polynomial descriptions and are built in polynomial time. The number of random bits is O(D log D), even if a deliberately inefficient polynomial-size table is used.

Finally, for each unit vector v, this coupling gives

E(v.S_D)^2 <=2E(v.X)^2+2E||S_D-X||^2 <=K.

Thus bounded covariance is preserved without multiplying a tiny TV error by the square of an unnecessarily enormous output cutoff.

## 3. Regularize to polynomial LSI

Put r=D^(-20), a=D^(-100), h=a/k. Apply C006 to S_D, using fresh standard Gaussians Z in R^k and W in R^D:

c(z)=min(1,min_i |z_i|/h),
F(z)=c(z)S_D(sign z),
M_D=Law(F(Z)+rW).

It has a positive smooth density, bounded covariance operator, and

C_LS(M_D)<=B_D^2 k^2/a^2+r^2
 <=16 k^2 D^204+r^2 <=C D^206(log D)^2.

It is explicitly samplable using the given forward circuit and Gaussian randomness.

Let P_r=P_D*N(0,r^2 I). Gaussian translation gives

TV(Law(S_D+rW),P_r) <=W2(P_D,Law(S_D))/r <=D^(-110).

For clarity, the translation estimate follows by integrating the absolute directional derivative of the Gaussian density: TV(N(x,r^2I),N(x',r^2I))<=||x-x'||/r. Integrate this over the displayed coupling and use Cauchy--Schwarz. No density of the unsmoothed P_D is required.

C006 and the triangle inequality therefore give TV(M_D,P_r)<=a+D^(-110)<=2a.

The prior score is also globally Lipschitz with a polynomial bound: if V=F(Z), then ||V||<=B_D, and Gaussian convolution gives Hess log p(x)=-I/r^2+Cov(V|V+rW=x)/r^4. Its operator norm is at most r^(-2)+B_D^2 r^(-4)=poly(D). This is a regularity statement, not a polynomial exact-score evaluation algorithm.

## 4. Preserve effective forward-score networks

For D^(-8)<=u<=D^8 put v=sqrt(u^2+r^2). For large D, D^(-10)<=v<=D^10. The u-smoothed score of P_r equals the v-smoothed score of P_D. Use its source network and clip each output to [-D/u,D/u]. The clipping is an explicit ReLU operation with coefficients polynomially bounded on the scale interval.

Apply C005 with P=P_r, Q=M_D, L=D and TV distance at most 2a. The squared score error under (M_D)_u is at most

[2D^(-10)+12D exp(-D^2/2)+16aD(D^2+1)]/u^2 <=D^(-8)/u^2

for all sufficiently large D. This estimate is uniform over the full scale interval. For an explicit eventual bound, the degree-nine Taylor term gives exp(D^2/2)>12D^11 once D>=32; the remaining polynomial terms are smaller than D^(-10) for sufficiently large D. Hence the numerator is at most 4D^(-10), below D^(-8).

Together with bounded covariance, these clipped networks witness 8-well-modeledness. Their descriptions are computed by taking the source network at v and adding the clipping layer. The construction uses only the forward circuit and polynomial-precision scalar parameters. It does not approximate exact prior scores to arbitrarily requested accuracy and does not furnish unit-cost exact-score access.

## 5. The actual optimal LSI lies in a polynomial regime

The first marginal of P_r is the symmetric mixture of N(+1,t^2) and N(-1,t^2), where t^2=R_D^(-2)+r^2. Its probability in [-1/4,1/4] is at most 2 exp(-9/(32t^2)). Since R_D=Theta(log D) and r=D^(-20), this is at most a=D^(-100) for sufficiently large D. The symmetry makes each outside plateau have mass at least (1-a)/2.

The TV bound to M_D gives belt mass at most 3a and each outside plateau mass at least (1-5a)/2>=2/5. Let f be zero for x_1<=-1/4, one for x_1>=1/4, and linear between. Its squared gradient is 4 in the belt and zero outside, so its energy is at most 12a. Two independent copies show Var(f)>=4/25>1/8. Therefore

C_P(M_D)>=1/(96a)=D^100/96,
C_LS(M_D)>=C_P(M_D).

This is a lower bound on the actual optimal LSI constant. No irrelevant dummy coordinate or inflated LSI certificate is used to obtain a large observation ratio.

## 6. Transfer a posterior sampler back to the hard source

Write beta=beta_D, A=A_D, and choose sigma=sqrt(beta^2-r^2)>0. Positivity and sigma=Theta(beta) hold for sufficiently large D. Under the common coupling

X~P_D,  X_r=X+rW,  Y=A X_r+sigma E,

the joint law of (X,Y) is exactly the source model with noise beta: A A^T=I, so rAW+sigma E is N(0,beta^2 I), independent of X. The marginal law of (X_r,Y) is the P_r prior with independent observation noise sigma. This equality is before conditioning; W need not be independent of Y afterward.

For tau=1/100 let e_y be the conditional probability that ||X_r-X||>tau in this coupling. Since E||rW||^2=D^(-39),

E_Y e_y <=10^4 D^(-39).

Markov's inequality implies e_y<=1/100 outside an observation set of probability at most 10^6 D^(-39).

Suppose a polynomial-time M_D posterior sampler has TV error <=epsilon_0=10^(-6) with probability at least 1-epsilon_0 over its observations. Denote its output law at y by Q_y and let q(y)=TV(Q_y,M_D(.|y)). Since TV is at most one, E_{(M_D)_Y}q<=2epsilon_0. Observation marginalization contracts TV, so changing the Y law to that of P_r costs at most 2a. The conditional-TV averaging inequality proved in C002 gives

E_{(P_r)_Y} TV(M_D(.|Y),P_r(.|Y)) <=2TV(M_D,P_r)<=4a.

Consequently

E_{(P_r)_Y} TV(Q_Y,P_r(.|Y)) <=2epsilon_0+6a.

Markov at 1/100 makes the bad-observation probability at most 200epsilon_0+600a=0.0002+600a. On the remaining observations, couple Q_y to P_r(.|y) with failure at most 1/100, and then use the conditional coupling of X_r to X, with norm error at most 1/100 except on probability 1/100. The gluing lemma for couplings and a union bound give (1/100,2/100)-closeness to P_D(.|y).

The total bad-observation probability is at most

0.0002+600D^(-100)+10^6 D^(-39),

which is below 1/10 for sufficiently large D. This is stronger than the forbidden (1/10,1/10) source posterior guarantee. All wrapper computations, forward-score network calls and generative descriptions are polynomial, so the hypothetical sampler contradicts the source's one-way-function lower bound.

## 7. Observation ratio and conclusion

The same selector A has norm one and sigma^2=Theta((log D)^(-4)). Combining the two-sided prior LSI bounds with this noise scale gives exactly the two-sided polynomial bounds in the statement. Thus the construction lies in the polynomial-LSI class and the polynomial observation-ratio regime of Target 2, in the stated approximate-score interface.

This proof neither resolves Target 1 nor establishes a sharp transition. Its cryptographic assumption and hardness source are Gupta et al.; the proposed extension consists of the explicit polynomial-LSI regularization and preservation of their computable score interface. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02093, 'An analytic approach to the finite $R$-transform'] Let $\epsilon > 0$.
Assume that $p_N \in \calP_N((-\infty, -\epsilon])$ is a sequence of polynomials whose empirical root distributions $\meas{p_N}$ converge weakly to a probability measure $\mu \in \calM((-\infty, -\epsilon])$, and set $\alpha:= G_\mu(0)$.
Then, for each $s \in (0, \alpha)$, we have
\[
  R_{p_N}^{(N)}(s) - R_{\meas{p_N}}(s) = O(N^{-1}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:kpz-red-dressing of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We say that $K\colon\mathcal V\to\mathrm{End}(H)$ is
\emph{dressing compatible} with $(\Psi,\Phi)$ if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item For all $(t,x,a) \in \mathcal V$,
\begin{align}
K_a
  &= -\Psi\Phi,

body: [Lemma lem:analyt of arXiv:2512.17808, 'Zeros of polynomial powers under the heat flow'] The saddle points $(z,t)\mapsto u_t^j(z)$, $j=1,\dots,d+1$, are analytic within any simply connected domain of $\{(z,t)\in\mathbb{C}^2: z\notin B\}$. Moreover, fix $t\in\mathbb{C}$, $z_0\in B$, and let $V=B_r(z_0)\setminus[z_0,\infty)$ be some slit neighborhood of $z_0$ that contains no other branch points and on which, for some $k\le d+1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, we have $|u_t^k(z)-u_t^j(z)|>\varepsilon$ for all $j\neq k$. Then $u_t^k(z)$ can be analytically extended to $z_0$.

body: The union-closed sets conjecture, also known as Frankl’s conjecture, is an open problem in combinatorics posed by Péter Frankl in 1979. A family of sets is said to be union-closed if the union of any two sets from the family belongs to the family. The conjecture states: For every finite union-closed family of sets, other than the empty family, there exists an element that belongs to at least half of the sets in the family.
title: Union-closed sets conjecture

In a finite square-lattice FK random-cluster Dobrushin domain at the critical self-dual parameter, for 0<q<4 define the medial-edge parafermionic observable F(e)=E[exp(i sigma W_gamma(e,e_b)) 1_{e in gamma}], where sin(pi sigma/2)=sqrt(q)/2 and sigma is in (0,1). At every interior medial vertex with incident edges NW,SE,NE,SW, F(NW)-F(SE)=i(F(NE)-F(SW)). At q=1, sigma=1/3. This one local relation alone does not identify a holomorphic continuum limit.

body:
[Lemma Analogue of lemma 3.9 of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $u_0\in L^\infty(M)\cap L^r(M)$, $1\leq r\leq +\infty$.
    Let $b=b(r)=\frac{(n-1)^2}{2\max(2,r)}K_1$ (it is 0 if $r=+\infty$). There exist three functions $F_1,F_2,F_3:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ such that for every $t>0$, $x\in M$, the following holds for $\alpha>\frac{n-2}{4}$ and $\rho >0$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $\frac{n-2}{4}<\alpha<\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_1(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha=\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_2(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha>\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_3(\rho)^k.$$
    \end{enumerate}
    Here $C>0$ depends on $\alpha,K_1,n,$ and $r$. 
    The functions $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to \mathbb{R}_+$ are differentiable and satisfy the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For $i\in \set{1,2,3}$, and $K_1>0$ we have  
        \[ \dv{F_i}{\rho}<0,\quad\sup_{\rho\in\mathbb{R}_+}F_i(\rho)=F_i(0)<\infty,\text{ and }\lim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty}F_i(\rho)=0.\]
        
        Note that this implies $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to (0,F_i(0)]$ is invertible.
        \item For $K_1>0$, we have the asymptotics \begin{equation}
        F_i(\rho)\sim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty} \begin{cases}
            \left(\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^{2\alpha-\frac{n}{2}+1}& i=1,\\
                \frac{(\ln \rho)^2}{\rho}& i=2,\\
                \frac{1}{\rho}& i=3.
            \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}
title: Lemma Analogue of lemma 3.9 of arXiv:2411.09614

[Defn of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. The \textbf{box-closure of $S$}, denoted by $[S]$, is defined as
    $$[S] \coloneqq \left\{ \bm{s} \in \mathbb{R}^n \ \vert \ \exists \bm{s}^\pm \in S, \ \bm{s}^- \leq \bm{s} \leq \bm{s}^+\right\}.$$
    It is the smallest box-convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ containing $S$.

[Theorem thm:cycle of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Let $\a_2, \ldots, \a_K : {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be differentiable functions with bounded derivatives, where $K \geq 2$ is an integer independent of $N$, and fix $y_0 > 0$. Let $\phi : {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be the test function
	\[ \phi(x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y)\, f_k^N(x)\,, \]
and let $\varphi(x,y) \coloneqq \phi(x, y/a_N)$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $. Then with $T = N \lfloor y_0 a_N \rfloor$,
	\[ \frac{1}{N} \langle \! \langle D_T,\, \varphi \rangle \! \rangle
	\Rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal N}\!\left( 0\,, \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y_0)^2\, \frac{1 - e^{-2\g_k y_0}}{2 \g_k} \right) \]
as $N \to \infty$, where $\g_k = \sqrt{2}\,\pi\,\lfloor k/2 \rfloor$.

body: Let (X, ||.||) be a normed vector space over R or C. There exists an inner product <.,.> on X with ||x||^2 = <x,x> for every x in X if and only if the norm satisfies the parallelogram law: ||x+y||^2 + ||x-y||^2 = 2||x||^2 + 2||y||^2 for all x, y in X. When this holds, the inner product is recovered from the norm by the polarization identity. [Jordan and von Neumann (1935); see Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Parallelogram-Law Characterization of Inner-Product Norms

[Lemma 37 (Ergodicity of the Palm version) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Let $\mathbf Y$ be a Poisson point process on $X$ with intensity $c \, {\rm vol}$ for some $c>0$ and with iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$-marks. Let $\mathbf Y_0=\mathbf Y \cup \{\mathbf o\}$, where $\mathbf o$ is equipped with an independent ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$-mark. Then the following hold:
\begin{itemize} 
\item[{\rm(1)}] Let $A$ be a $G$-invariant event and let $A_0$ be the restriction of $A$ to configurations containing the origin. Then $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in A_0)=\mathbb P(\mathbf Y\in A)\in \{0,1\}$.
\item[{\rm(2)}] Let $B_0$ be an event such that $B_0=B'$, where $B'$ is the restriction of the event $B:=GB_0$ to configurations that contain the origin.
Then $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in B_0)=\mathbb P(\mathbf Y\in B)$. In particular, $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in B_0)\in\{0,1\}$.
\end{itemize}
The same conclusions hold when $\mathbf Y$ is replaced with the unmarked Poisson point process $Y$ and $\mathbf Y_0$ is replaced with $Y_0=Y\cup\{o\}$.

[Lemma 76 (Exponential boundary layers) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $0<\alpha<\beta<1$, and suppose
$\norm{x}_{\beta\text{-H\"ol}}\le R$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \norm{Y^\eps(x)}_{\beta\text{-H\"ol}}&\le R,
 &\norm{D^\eps(x)}_\infty&\le C_\beta R\eps^\beta,
 \notag\\
 \norm{D^\eps(x)}_{\alpha\text{-H\"ol}}
 &\le C_{\alpha,\beta}R\eps^{\beta-\alpha},
 &\sup_{v\le T}|\mathcal A_v^\eps(x)|
 &\le C_\beta R\eps^\beta.
 
\end{align}
Let
\[
 B_t=\one_{\{t>a\}}(1-e^{-(t-a)/\eps})u,
 \qquad |u|\le U\eps^\beta,
\]
and let $W$ be a bounded-variation path with
$\norm{W}_{\beta\text{-H\"ol}}\le M$.  If
$1/3<\alpha<\beta<1/2$, then
\begin{equation}
 \rho_\alpha(S_2(W+B),S_2(W))
 \le C U(1+M+U)\eps^{\beta-\alpha}.
\end{equation}
For a fixed finite sum of layers, the same estimate holds with the total
amplitude and a constant depending on their number.

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the combinatorial identities (layer = second-largest branch height, maximum layer = floor(diam/2) <= height) were verified by brute-force leaf stripping on 40 random recursive trees of sizes 6 to 120 (480 vertices), with the 5-vertex path as a control] This is the layer part of the campaign answer to Conjecture 2 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. For each integer n>=3, let T_n be a random recursive tree on vertices 1,...,n, in which each vertex j>=2 chooses its parent independently and uniformly from 1,...,j-1. Repeatedly remove all vertices of degree at most one, assigning layer zero to the first removed set and successively increasing the layer. Let L_n be the maximum layer. As n tends to infinity, L_n=e log n-(3/2)log log n+O_P(1), where logarithms are natural and O_P(1) means that the centered sequence is bounded in probability. Under this removal rule, L_n=floor(diameter(T_n)/2); other conventions for the last vertex left standing change the maximum by at most one. The proof uses the recursive-tree height estimate of Addario-Berry and Ford (Corollary 1.3) and the fact that the root's normalized subtree sizes have a stick-breaking limit whose second-largest term is positive almost surely. The maximum-rank part of Conjecture 2 is not addressed. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

body:
[Proposition prop:existence_measure_initial of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] There exist a filtered probability space, a space-time white noise $\widetilde\xi$, a nonnegative random Radon measure $\widetilde\mu_0$, a coefficient field $(\widetilde a,\widetilde b,\widetilde c) $ satisfying Assumption~(asp:coefficients of the paper), and a nonnegative process 
\[ 
\ u\in C((0,T];C_{\mathrm{tem}}) 
\] 
such that $L(\widetilde\mu_0,\widetilde a,\widetilde b,\widetilde c) = L(\mu_0,a,b,c) $ and $u$ is a solution of 
\[ 
\partial_t u = \widetilde L u + \sigma( u)\widetilde\xi, \qquad  u(0,\cdot)=\widetilde\mu_0, 
\] 
where $\widetilde L = \widetilde a\,\partial_x^2 + \widetilde b\,\partial_x + \widetilde c$. More precisely, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ and every $t\in(0,T]$,
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
    (u(t),\varphi)
    &=
    (\widetilde\mu_0,\varphi)
    +
    \int_0^t (u(s),\widetilde L^*\varphi(s))\,\mathrm{d} s  +
    \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{R}}
        \sigma(u(s,x))\varphi(x)\,\widetilde\xi(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} x)
    \qquad\text{a.s.}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $\mathbb{E} W_q(\mu_0)<\infty$, then for every
$\alpha\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\left[
        \sup_{0<t\le T} W_q(u(t))^\alpha
    \right]
    <\infty .
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
    W_q(u(t))<\infty
    \qquad\text{for every }t\in(0,T]\text{ a.s.}
\]

body:
[Proposition prop:seven of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] For fixed atoms $(t_i,z_i)$, the admissible weight vectors $p$ form a
polytope cut out by at most $7$ linear equalities, and the worst weight
vector (minimizing $E$) may be taken at a basic feasible solution, of support
at most $7$. Consequently each inequality of Conjecture~(conj:CE of the paper) holds
for all finite systems if and only if it holds for all systems with at most
seven atoms; and, since atoms may be split into identically placed copies
without changing anything, it suffices to treat systems with \emph{exactly}
seven labelled atoms.

[Thm exchangeable of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] Let $(Y,Y')$ be an exchangeable pair of random vectors in $\setr^d$.  Suppose that
there is an invertible matrix $\Lambda$ such that $\sete\bracmid{Y'-Y}{Y} =-\Lambda Y$ and a 
random matrix $E$ such that $\sete\bracmid{E}{Y} =\sete\bracmid{(Y'-Y)(Y'-Y)^T-2\Lambda}{Y}$.
Then for $g\in C^3(\setr^d)$,
\[
\abs[\big]{\sete[g(Y)] - \sete[g(Z)]} \leq \Abs{\Lambda^{-1}}_\mathrm{op} \paren*{\frac{\sqrt{d}}{4}M_2(g) \sete\brac[\big]{\Abs{E}_\mathrm{HS}} + \frac{1}{9}M_3(g)\sete\brac[\big]{\abs{Y'-Y}^3}},
\]
where $Z$ is a standard multivariate normal on $\setr^d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let F(x)=Qx+b be a Euclidean isometry preserving a bounded connected smooth domain D. Suppose normal reflected Brownian motion X in D almost surely visits every nonempty interior open set infinitely often. Then Y=F(X) is a reflected-Brownian coupling, and it is shy if and only if min_{closure D}|x-F(x)|>0. A bounded convex preserving domain has a fixed centroid and therefore no shy isometry coupling. A planar annulus with inner radius R>0 and nontrivial rotation theta has separation at least 2R*|sin(theta/2)|. No claim about arbitrary nondeterministic shy couplings is made.

Then the deterministic isometry coupling is shy exactly when

    min_{x in closure D} |x-F(x)| > 0.

If the minimum is positive the distance stays uniformly positive. If it is zero, for every epsilon>0 the set {x in D: |x-F(x)|<epsilon} is nonempty and open by continuity and density of D in its closure. Recurrence forces visits to it. Applying this to epsilon=1/k shows inf_t |X_t-F(X_t)|=0 almost surely, ruling out shyness.

If D is convex, its volume centroid c lies in D. Any preserving Euclidean isometry fixes c: change variables in its centroid integral to obtain Qc+b=c. Therefore this regular deterministic class has no shy coupling on a bounded convex smooth domain. This is not a claim about all nondeterministic couplings on such a domain.

[Corollary 41 of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Let \(m,L>0\), and suppose that \(V\in C^3(\mathbb R^d)\) satisfies
\[
  m I_d \preceq \nabla^2 V(x) \preceq L I_d,
  \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
Let
\[
  k(x,y)=\Psi(x-y),
\]
where \(\Psi\in C_b^4(\mathbb R^d)\) is even and \(k\) is positive
definite. Let \(\mu_0\) have a smooth positive density satisfying
\[
  \KL(\mu_0\Vert\pi)<\infty.
\]
Then Assumptions~\ref{ass:core-target} and~\ref{ass:ksd-kernel} hold,
with target log-Sobolev constant \(\alpha=m\). The kernel regularity
and diagonal-correction conditions in Assumption~\ref{ass:W2} also
hold. Consequently, Proposition~\ref{prop:wellposed} and the
target-convergence and uniform-second-moment results of
Sections~\ref{sec:target-KSD} and~\ref{sec:target-W2} apply.

If, in addition,
\[
  \int_{\mathbb R^d} e^{a_0\|x\|^2}\,\mu_0(dx)<\infty
\]
for some \(a_0>0\), then Assumption~\ref{ass:concentration} holds.  The
synchronous coupling and moving-product entropy bounds, and consequently the finite-time and uniform-in-time PoC results for the empirical measure in KSD, $W_2$, and finite-marginal PoC, therefore apply. If one further assumes
\(\mu_0\in T_2(C_0)\), the alternative entropy-derived Wasserstein bounds in
Section~\ref{app:entropy-W2} apply as well.

[Proposition 17 (\cite{AgrestiVeraarNonLinParab}) of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let $\mathcal B_1\hookrightarrow \mathcal B$ be Banach spaces. Set $\mathcal B_{1-\theta}=[\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1]_{1-\theta}$ or $\mathcal B_{1-\theta} = (\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\theta,r}$, where the latter denotes real interpolation for $r\in [1, \infty]$. Assume that $p\in (1,\infty)$, $\beta\in [0,p-1)$, $\theta\in (0,1)$ and $T\in (0,\infty]$. Then the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $\theta>\frac{1+\beta}{p}$, then
$$
H^{\theta,p}([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_{1-\theta})\cap L^p([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_1)
\hookrightarrow C\left([0,T];(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\frac{1+\beta}{p},p}\right)_0
$$
\item If $\theta>\frac{1}{p}$, then for any $0<\varepsilon<T$
$$
H^{\theta,p}([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_{1-\theta})\cap L^p([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_1)\hookrightarrow
 C\left([\varepsilon,T];(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\frac{1}{p},p}\right)_0.
$$
\end{enumerate}
Here, if $T$ ranges over $ (\eta,\infty]$ for some $\eta > 0$, then the constants in \eqref{item:trace_with_weights_Xap} and \eqref{item:trace_without_weights_Xp} depend only on $\eta$.
Furthermore, if we replace $H^{\theta,p}$ by ${_0H}^{\theta,p}$ in \eqref{item:trace_with_weights_Xap} and \eqref{item:trace_without_weights_Xp}, the constants in the embeddings can be chosen independent of $T>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 7 of arXiv:2511.01245, 'A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain'] The transition matrix $K(x, y)$ satisfies
\[
    K(x, y) = K(x, \overline{y}) = K(\overline{x}, \overline{y}) = K(\sigma(x), \sigma(y)),
\]  
where $\overline{x}$ is the binary $n$-tuple obtained from $x$ by flipping all bits and $\sigma \in S_n$ is any permutation.

body: Let X be a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space and let K be a nonempty compact convex subset of X. Then K equals the closed convex hull of its extreme points, ext(K), where x in K is an extreme point if it cannot be written as t y + (1 - t) z for distinct y, z in K and t in (0,1); that is, x = ty + (1-t)z with t in (0,1) forces y = z = x. In particular ext(K) is nonempty whenever K is nonempty, compact, and convex, and every such K is recovered as the closure of the convex hull of ext(K).

body: Method (campaign status: proved): Take a maximum matching $P_1,\dots,P_N$ in $\Gamma$. Greedily choose a remaining pair, a witness row $E_s$ containing it, and remove the batch $B_s$ of all remaining matching pairs meeting $E_s$; put $a_s=|B_s|$. Batches partition the matching. With $V_s$ the endpoints of $B_s$ and $U_s=E_s\cap V_s$: $|U_s|\ge a_s+1$ (tag 14), the $U_s$ are disjoint, and $E_s$ avoids every later $U_t$. Condition outside $\bigcup_s U_s$ and peel $U_k,\dots,U_1$ in reverse exposure order. Notes: Key independence bookkeeping: earlier selected row indicators are independent of the set being peeled, and variables in earlier $U_t$'s are held as arbitrary parameters. This is exactly why the Littlewood-Offord input must be TARGET-UNIFORM (two-point form).

[Proposition prop:tailrl-threshold-reparameterization of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Define
\begin{equation}
F_w(t)
:=
\int_0^t w(s)\,ds,
\qquad
\widetilde r(x,z):=F_w\!\left(r(x,z)\right).

\end{equation}
Then $F_w$ is a strictly increasing map from $[0,1]$ to $[0,1]$, and
\begin{equation}
J_w(\theta;x)
=
\int_0^1
\log
\Pr_{z\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)}
\!\left(\widetilde r(x,z)>u\right)
\,du.

\end{equation}
Thus, weighted TailRL on $r$ is exactly uniform TailRL on the monotone rescaling $\widetilde r=F_w(r)$.

[Lem backprop of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $d$ be a positive integer and $D,\varepsilon$ be positive reals.
    There exists a positive integer $\ell$ depending only on
    $d,D,\varepsilon,C,V,\delta,t$ such that for all $k<t/\delta$ and
    polynomials $P:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d$ with
    $\|P\|_1\le DN$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
 \left|\mathbb{E}[ P(\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k+1)}) ] - \mathbb{E}\left[ P\left( \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -
 \beta\delta \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -\delta
 \text{\boldmath $P$}_\ell(\text{\boldmath $h$},\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)}) + \sqrt{2\delta}\text{\boldmath $\eta$}^{(k)} \right) \right]
 \right| \le \varepsilon N.
\end{align*}

    for all $\text{\boldmath $h$}$ with $\|\text{\boldmath $h$}\|_\infty\le C$. Furthermore, there exist
    a positive integer $d'$ and a positive real $D'$ depending only
    $d,D,\varepsilon,C,V,\delta,t$ such that for all polynomials
     $P:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d$ with
    $\|P\|_1\le DN$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
 \mathbb{E}\left[ P\left( \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} - \beta\delta\text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -
 \delta\text{\boldmath $P$}_\ell(\text{\boldmath $h$},\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)}) + \sqrt{2\delta}\text{\boldmath $\eta$}^{(k)}
 \right) \Big| \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} \right] = Q(\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)})
\end{align*}

    for some polynomial $Q:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d'$

[Thm thm5 of arXiv:2412.05521, 'Random attractors for the stochastic Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes system with multiplicativ'] Let $v^\varepsilon(0)$ $\in$  $H^1$ and $c_i(0) \in H^1$ be nonnegative with $c_i(0) \geq 0 $. Let $T > 0$. Then, there exists a unique solution $(v^\varepsilon,c_1,c_2)$ satisfying $v^\varepsilon \in 
		L^{\infty}(0,T;H^1) \cap L^2(0,T;H^2)$ and $c_i \in L^{\infty}(0,T;H^1) \cap L^2(0,T;H^2) $. Moreover $c_i(t) \geq 0$ holds on $[0,T]$. 
		\begin{proof}
			 By the local existence theorem (Theorem (thm2 of the paper)), there exists $T_0 \geq 0$ depending only on the norms of initial data in $H^1$ such that the solution exists and belongs to $H^1$. By Remark (Remark 1 of the paper), we find $c_i(t) \geq 0$. Moreover, the inequality (equation b33 of the paper) holds on $[0,T_0]$. It follows from Theorem (thm4 of the paper) that the solution is bounded in $H^1$. Applying the local existence theorem again and starting from $T_0$, we deduce that the solution can be extended for $T_1$ $\geq T_0$. The inequality (equation b33 of the paper) holds on $[0,T_1]$. Since the inequality holds as long as $c_i$ $\geq 0$, reasoning by contradiction we conclude that the solution can extend to the whole interval $[0,T]$.
		\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 40 ($W_2$--Lipschitz continuity) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Assume \hyperref[ass:OSL]{\textup{(A3)}}. Let \((X_t)_{t\ge0}\) and \((Y_t)_{t\ge0}\) be
solutions of \eqref{eq:SDE} driven by the same Brownian motion, with initial conditions
\(X_0=x\) and \(Y_0=y\).
Then for all \(t\ge0\),
\[
  \|X_t-Y_t\|_{L^2}\le e^{K' t}\,\|x-y\|.
\]
In particular, for \(t\in[0,\lambda]\), setting \(L := e^{K'\lambda}\) yields
\[
  \|X_t-Y_t\|_{L^2}\le L\,\|x-y\|.
\]
For \(\lambda\le \frac{\ln 2}{|K'|}\), then \(L\in[\tfrac12,2]\).

body:
[Thm 8 of arXiv:2609.03061, '2609.03061'] Let $K :U(n) \subset Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ be the inclusion $X+ i \ Y \mapsto
\left( \begin{array}{cc} X & -Y \\ Y & X \end{array} \right)$. Here $X^t Y = Y^tX$ and  $X^tX+Y^tY=Id[n], \ i \mapsto -J_n$.

\begin{itemize}
\item[1.] For $M \in Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ as above; the $n \times n$ \textbf{complex matrix}
$$
G[M] = ( a + i \ c) \cdot D[M]^{-1/2}
$$
is unitary.

Note that for $(X+i \ Y) \in U(n)$, $G[ K(X+i \ Y)]=(X + i \ Y)$. Hence, $M \mapsto G[M]$ is a retraction of
$Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ onto $U(n)$.

\item[2.] Let $L_0 = \mathbb{R}^n \oplus 0$ be the reference Lagrangian and
$M \cdot L_0$ be the result of the action of $M$ on $L_0$. That is,
$M \cdot L_0$ is the real span of the first $n$ columns of $M$.
Then
$$
M \cdot L_0 = K(G[M]) \cdot L_0.
$$
That is, the span of the first $n$ columns of $M$, $=\left( \begin{array}{c|c} a  & b \\ c &d \end{array} \right)$,
 equals the span of the first $n$ columns of $K(G[M])$,
$ =\left( \begin{array}{c|c} a \cdot D[M]^{-1/2} & - c \cdot D[M]^{-1/2}\\ c \cdot D[M]^{-1/2} &  a \cdot D[M]^{-1/2} \end{array} \right)$.

For example, for any continuous path $M: [a,b] \rightarrow Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$
there is the equality
$$
\{M(t) \cdot L_0 = K(G[M(t)]) \cdot L_0, \ a \le t \le b\}:
$$
a reduction from symplectic to unitary geometry.

\item[3.] The symplectic matrix $M $ equals a product of
of symplectic matrices
$$
M = K(G[M]) \cdot \left( \begin{array}{cc} D[M]^{+1/2} & 0 \\ 0 & D[M]^{-1/2} \end{array} \right)
\cdot \left( \begin{array}{cc} Id[n] & \alpha \\ 0 & Id[n] \end{array} \right)
$$
with $\alpha = D[M]^{-1} \cdot (a^t b + c^td)$. Moreover, $\alpha$ is symmetric; i.e.,
$$
 D[M]^{-1} \cdot (a^t b + c^td)  =( b^ta +d^t c) \cdot D[M]^{-1}.
 $$

 \item[4.] There is a natural deformation retraction of $Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ onto $U(n)$
 defined for $M \in Sp(2n,\mathbb{R})$ and $0 \le u \le 1$ by :
 $$
 H(M,u) =K(G[M]) \cdot \left( \begin{array}{cc} D[M]^{+1/2} & 0 \\ 0 & D[M]^{-1/2} \end{array} \right)^{(1-u)}
\cdot \left( \begin{array}{cc} Id[n] & \alpha \\ 0 & Id[n] \end{array} \right)^{(1-u)}
 $$

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 8 of arXiv:2609.03061

[Proposition 19 (A nontrivial Pauli family) of arXiv:2606.21137, 'A Sudakov--Fernique proof of Lehner-type edge bounds for matrix-valued GUE sums'] For $t>0$, consider the signed family
	\[
		\mathfrak F_t=(\sigma_x,\sigma_z,tI_2).
	\]
	Its covariance map admits a positive semidefinite Kraus decomposition if and
	only if $t\ge\sqrt2$.  When $t\ge\sqrt2$, one may use the four matrices
	\[
		\widetilde A_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}
		=
		\frac12\bigl(\varepsilon_1\sigma_x+\varepsilon_2\sigma_z\bigr)
		+\frac t2I_2,
		\qquad
		(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\in\{\pm1\}^2.
	\]
	At $t=\sqrt2$, these are rank-one positive semidefinite matrices with
	eigenvalues $0$ and $\sqrt2$.

[Proposition lem:discrete_antitrap_from_CT of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a filtration, and let $(G_n)_{n\ge0}$ be an
$\mathbb R^d$-valued adapted process satisfying
$$
G_{n+1}-G_n=\upsilon_{n+1}F_n+c_{n+1}(\varepsilon_{n+1}+r_{n+1}),
\quad n\ge0,
$$
where $(\upsilon_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(c_n)_{n\ge1}$ are deterministic nonnegative
sequences such that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n^2<\infty$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\upsilon_n=\infty$; for each $n\ge 0$, $F_n$, $\varepsilon_{n+1}$ and $r_{n+1}$ are $\mathcal F_n$-measurable, and
$$
\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0, \quad \mathbb{E}\|\varepsilon_n\|^2<\infty.
$$

Let $\Gamma\in\mathcal F_\infty$ be an event, where
$\mathcal F_\infty:=\sigma\bigl(\bigcup_{n\ge0}\mathcal F_n\bigr)$.
Assume that there exist a deterministic constant $\rho>0$, a finite random
integer $T_0$, a deterministic nonincreasing sequence $(b_n)_{n\ge0}$, and an
event $\Omega_*\in\mathcal F_\infty$ with $\mathbb P(\Omega_*)=1$ such that the
following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On $\Gamma\cap\Omega_*$, for all $n\ge T_0$,
$$
\langle G_n, F_n\rangle\ge0
\text{ whenever }\|G_n\|<2\rho; \quad \text{and}\quad
\upsilon_{n+1}\|F_n\|<\rho.
$$

\item[(b)] There exist deterministic constants $a_0,a_1>0$ such that on $\Gamma$,
$$
0<a_0\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon_{n+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_n]
\le

body: Lebesgue measure on R^n is the complete translation-invariant measure obtained by applying Caratheodory's construction to the outer measure m*(A) = inf of sum of volumes of countable covers of A by open boxes. Non-measurable sets exist (Vitali) assuming the axiom of choice.

For every integer n >= 1 there is a prime p with n < p <= 2n. Conjectured by Bertrand (1845, verified to 3 million), proved by Chebyshev (1852); the proof below is Erdos's (1932), from the prime factorisation of the central binomial coefficient. Refinements: for n >= 25 there is a prime in (n, 6n/5) (Nagura); the prime number theorem gives a prime in (n, (1 + eps) n) for every eps > 0 and n large; Ramanujan primes generalise the statement to k primes in (n/2, n].

In addition, for every integer n > 3 there is a prime p satisfying n < p < 2n-2. This sharpened form complements, and does not replace, the original assertion for all integers n >= 1.
n a positive integer
the elementary product bound prod_{p <= x} p < 4^x is used for real x >= 2 (Erdos)

[Theorem thm:main ESD of arXiv:2605.19894, 'Sharp Spectral Thresholds for Multi-View Spiked Wigner Models'] Suppose that Assumptions~(assump:Gaussian Wigner of the paper)--(assump:irreducible-normalized-B of the paper)
    hold. There exists a compactly supported probability measure $\mu$ on
    $\RR$ such that, if
    \[
        \hat\mu_H:=\frac{1}{nL}\sum_{j=1}^{nL}\delta_{\sigma_j(H)}
    \]
    is the empirical spectral measure of $H$, then $\hat\mu_H$ converges
    weakly to $\mu$ in probability. Let
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma_+:=\max\supp(\mu)
    \end{equation}
    denote the upper edge of this limiting bulk spectrum. Then, for every
    fixed $\epsilon>0$,
    \[
        \PP(
        \#\cbr{j\in[nL]:\sigma_j(H)>\sigma_++\epsilon}\le L
        )
        \to 1.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defi construction of nu of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Suppose $t\in\mathbb{Z}$. Set $t':=t-\lfloor\frac{n\log n}{2}\rfloor$, and $\gamma_t:=\exp(-2t'/n)$. Let $\nu_n^t$ denote the measure on $\mathfrak{S}_n$ defined by the following sampling process: first, sample $M_t\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ according to the distribution 
$$\mathbf{P}[M_t=k]=\mathbf{P}(\Pois(\gamma_t)=k)/\mathbf{P}(\Pois(\gamma_t)\le n),$$ 
then sample a uniformly random subset $S_t$ of size $M_t$ in $[n]$. Finally, sample a uniformly random element of $\mathfrak{S}_{[n]\backslash S_t}$ and view it as an element of $\mathfrak{S}_n$ by fixing all of the elements in $S_t$.

body:
[Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'] Given an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ and a set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Lim}(\kappa)$, a\linebreak \emph{$(\kappa, S)$-quagmire} is a quadruple $(T, {<}, {\lhd}, Q)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(Q\arabic*)},  start=0]
\item 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(T, <)$ is a $\kappa$-Kurepa tree,
\item $\lhd$ is a binary relation on $T$ whose restriction to each level of $T$ is a strict linear order; nodes of distinct heights are $\lhd$-incomparable,
\item the function $Q$ is a partial function from $T^2$ to $T$ whose domain consists of the pairs $(x, y) \in T^2$ such that $\mathrm{ht}(x) < \mathrm{ht}(y)$ and $x \lhd \pi_{\mathrm{ht}(x)}(y)$,
\end{enumerate}

\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$, then $x < Q(x, y) \lhd y$,
\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $y < z$, then $Q(Q(x, y), z) = Q(x,z)$,
\item if $(y, z) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $x \lhd y$, then $Q(x, Q(y, z)) = Q(x, z)$,
\item if $x \lhd y$ and $\mathrm{ht}(x) \in S \cup \{\kappa\}$, then there exists $\alpha < \mathrm{ht}(x)$ such that $\pi_\alpha(x) \lhd \pi_\alpha(y)$ and $x = Q(\pi_\alpha(x), y)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505

body:
[Lem 28 (\cite{spencer2007birth}*{Theorem~3.1(2)}) of arXiv:2509.09589, 'Geometry of critical discrete structures: long-range percolation on the hierarchical latti'] Suppose $c_0, c_1, c_2$, and $t$ are positive numbers with $t c_0>1$.
Let $H_n$, $n\geq 1$, be graphs (we view $H_n$ as the seed graph) with $|H_n| = n$ satisfying the following for all $n$:
\begin{enumeratei}
\item 
$n^{-1}\sum |\cC|^2 \geq c_0$, where the sum is over all connected components $\cC$ of $H_n$, and
\item 
$n^{-1}\#\big\{
v\in V(H_n)\, :\, | \cC( v; H_n ) | \geq s 
\big\}
\leq 
c_1 \exp(-c_2 s)$
for all $s\in\bZ_{>0}$.
\end{enumeratei}
Place edges with probability $t/n$ independently between all $u\neq v\in V(H_n)$ such that $\{u, v\}\notin E(H_n)$;
let $E_n^+$ denote the set of edges thus created.
Let $\cC_{\max}^+$ denote the largest component of the graph $(V(H_n), E(H_n)\cup E_n^+)$.
Then there exists $a_0>0$ depending only on $c_0, c_1, c_2$, and $t$ such that 
$ | \cC_{\max}^+ | \geq a_0 n $ whp. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{spencer2007birth}*{Theorem~3.1(2)}

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $\alpha\colon G\to G'$ be any homomorphism of compact Lie groups. Then $\alpha^*\colon\cat{$\bm{G'}$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ sends $G'$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalences to $G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
        In light of Lemma~(lemma:restr-right-Quillen of the paper), it suffices to consider the case of $G'$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalences $f\colon X\to Y$ of \emph{closed} orthogonal $G'$-spaces. But indeed, if $H\in{\mathcal{F}}$ and ${\mathcal{U}}_H$ is any complete $H$-universe, then $\alpha^*f({\mathcal{U}}_H)$ is a $\mathcal G_{H,G}$-weak equivalence by Example~(ex:graph-restr-rQ of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: An arithmetic function f (defined on positive integers) is multiplicative if f(1) = 1 and f(mn) = f(m) f(n) whenever gcd(m, n) = 1; completely multiplicative drops the coprimality condition. Multiplicative functions are determined by their values on prime powers. Examples: Euler's phi, the divisor count and divisor sum, the Mobius function mu. The Dirichlet convolution of two multiplicative functions is multiplicative, and Mobius inversion recovers f from its summatory function.
title: Multiplicative Arithmetic Function

body:
[Theorem 20 (Uniqueness for the distributional Duhamel system) of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Let $T>0$. Let
$(\mu_t^i)_{t\in[0,T],\,i\in\mathcal I}$ and
$(\widetilde\mu_t^i)_{t\in[0,T],\,i\in\mathcal I}$
be two families of finite nonnegative Borel measures on $\mathbb R^d$.
Assume that both families satisfy the distributional Duhamel formula~\eqref{eq:component-mild-form} with the same initial data, namely
\[
\mu_0^i=\widetilde\mu_0^i,
\qquad i\in\mathcal I.
\]
Assume moreover that
\[
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\left(
\mu_t^i(\mathbb R^d)
+
\widetilde\mu_t^i(\mathbb R^d)
\right)
<\infty .
\]
Then, for every $t\in[0,T]$ and every $i\in\mathcal I$,
\[
\mu_t^i=\widetilde\mu_t^i .
\]
In particular, the distributional Duhamel system admits at most one solution
in this class.

[Definition defi_solution_approx of arXiv:2603.26307, '\LARGE The incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with thermal noise'] A  \emph{weak martingale solution 
		to (equation Eq_approx of the paper)} 
	consists of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathfrak{A},\mathbb{P})$, a filtration $\mathscr{F}$ satisfying the usual conditions, independent $3$-dimensional standard $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(W_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ and $3\times 3$-matrix valued $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(B_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ with covariance structure (equation Eq_noise_matrix_covariation of the paper), a weakly continuous and adapted  $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$-valued process
	$u_{\delta,\epsilon}$, and $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3)$-valued  $\psi_{\delta,\epsilon}$, such that the following holds:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item  We have the additional regularity  $ u_{\delta,\epsilon}\in L^{2}(0,T;H^2( \mathbb{T}^3 ;\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ and $\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} \in  L^{2}(0,T;H^2( \mathbb{T}^3))$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  For every divergence-free $\varphi\in C^{{\infty}}(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				& \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}  u_{\delta,\epsilon}(t)\cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x \,-\, 
				\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_0 \cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,+\,\epsilon\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_{\delta,\epsilon}\Delta^2 \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} -  \Bigl(\frac{1}{2}+ \frac{F_1}{4}\Bigr) \nabla u_{\delta,\epsilon}: \nabla  \varphi \,+\, u_{\delta,\epsilon}\otimes u_{\delta,\epsilon}:\nabla \varphi \,\mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} s \,+\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} f_n \nabla \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x :\mathrm{d} B_{n,s},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
		and $\nabla \cdot u_t = 0$ for all $t\in [0,T]$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  
		For every $\zeta\in C_c^{{\infty}}([0,T) \times \mathbb{T}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				&-\,
				\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}  \partial_t \zeta  \, \mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} t \,-\, \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}
				\psi_0 \zeta
				\,\mathrm{d} x+\,\epsilon\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi_{\delta,\epsilon}\Delta^2\zeta\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s 
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} - \bigl(1+ {F_1}/2 +G_1/2\bigr) \nabla \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}\cdot \nabla  \zeta \,+\,\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} u_{\delta,\epsilon}\cdot \nabla \zeta   \,-\, (F_2/2+G_2/8) \psi_{\delta,\epsilon} \zeta \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t \\
				&\qquad+\, \int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \zeta\, h_\delta(\psi_{\delta,\epsilon})\bigl(
				|\nabla \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}|^2 \,+\, |\nabla_\mathrm{sym} u_{\delta,\epsilon}|^2 + \epsilon
				\bigr)\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t
				\\&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3
				\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon} g_n \partial_i \zeta  + \frac{1}{2} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}  \zeta \partial_ig_n \,\mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} W_{n,t}^i
				\, +\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j =1}^3\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}u_{\delta,\epsilon,j}\partial_i (\zeta f_n) \,\mathrm{d} x \,\mathrm{d} B_{n,t}^{ji},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}  $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.	
	\end{enumerate}
title: Weak martingale solution to \eqref{Eq_approx}

body: [Corollary 3.8 (Recovery of Hoeffding’s Inequality) of arXiv:2603.10190, 'Hoeffding-Type Concentration Bounds for Exchangeable Random Variable'] Let $(X_{m})_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of $[0,1]$ -valued random variables, and set $\mu\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[X_{1}]$. Then, for every $M\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(\bar{X}_{M}-\mu\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}},\qquad\mathbb{P}\left(\mu-\bar{X}_{M}\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}}.$

[Proposition prop:mean of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold and consider
additive functionals of density-type $\overline{\rho}_t$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and current-type $\overline{J}_t$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)).
For every $t>0$ the stationary (time-independent) means
are given by  
\begin{align}
\E^\mu\bigl[\overline{\rho}_t(V)\bigr] &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V \mathrm{d} \mu = \E^\mu[V],
\\
\E^\mu\bigl[\overline{J}_t(U)\bigr] &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} v_{\textrm{s}} \cdot U \mathrm{d}\mu = \E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}} \cdot U ] =\E^\mu[W],
\end{align}
with local mean velocity $v_{\textrm{s}}$ from Eq.~(equation eq:drift_split of the paper)
and $W\equiv v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U$.
title: Stationary expectation values

body:
[Definition def:genPotuple of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] .
For every $j$-tuple $\overline{z}$, we use the notation $\overline{z},\overline{z}$ to denote a tuple of length $2j$ where the first $j$ entries are the entries of $\overline{z}$ and similarly the last $j$ entries are the entries of $\overline{z}$. Thus, if $A$ and $B$ are random variables with support $(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^j$ then $\mathrm{dist}(A,B) \gtrsim \mathsf{Po}(\overline{z},\overline{z})$ indicates that the distribution of the pair $(A,B)$ is dominated below by an independent product of $2j$ Poisson distributions, where, for $k\in [j]$,  the $k$'th and $(j+k)$th Poisson distributions have mean~$z_k$.
title: Definition def:genPotuple of arXiv:2602.21315

[Definition 6 ($T^h$ and $h$-good) of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Let $T$ be a tree rooted at $r$, and $h,D>0$ be integers. Let $T^h$ be the subtree induced by the vertices of $T$ at depth $\leq h$. Moreover,
\begin{itemize}

\item All vertices at depth exactly~$h$ are $h$-good.
\item A vertex at depth less than $h$ is $h$-good if
it has at least~$D$  children that are $h$-good.
\end{itemize}
When   $T$ is fixed, we use
$ V^h_\mathrm{good}$ to denote the set of $h$-good vertices in~$V(T)$.

[Lemma 50 (Controlled-shift operator endpoint) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $c_1,\ldots,c_m\in\ell^2(\Gamma)$ be finitely supported, and let
$\widetilde K_{\mathbf c}^{L,Q}$ be the ordered kernel with coefficients
\[
 \bigl(\widetilde K_{\mathbf c}^{L,Q}\bigr)_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}
 :=\left(\prod_{j=1}^m c_{j,x_j}\right)
 P_L\lambda_{x_1\cdots x_m}P_Q.
\]
Then, for every $S\subset[m]$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm{\Flat_S(\widetilde K_{\mathbf c}^{L,Q})}_{\cL}
 \le\prod_{j=1}^m\norm{c_j}_{\ell^2}.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
 \Prof_{m,\infty}(\widetilde K_{\mathbf c}^{L,Q})
 \le\prod_{j=1}^m\norm{c_j}_{\ell^2}.
\]

body:
[Lemma ac excursions of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] Given $S\in\mathcal{S}_{n}$, on the event $V_{\delta}^{\mathrm{PTP}}(S)$, the followings hold.
\par
(1) The joint law of $W^{1},\ldots,W^{5}$ is uniformly equivalent to the joint law of five independent Brownian excursions in $\mathcal{A}(S,2^{-n},\delta/2)$.
\par
(2) Conditioned on $X^{i}$, $i=0,1,\ldots,5$, $W^{1},\ldots,W^{5}$ are conditionally independent and are distributed as Brownian excursions with fixed starting and ending points (i.e.\ the normalized boundary-to-boundary measure in $\mathcal{A}(S,2^{-n},\delta/2)$).
\par
(3) Conditioned on $W(s_{i}),W(t_{i})$, $i=1,\ldots,5$, $X^{j}$ are conditionally independent of each other, and further conditionally independent of $W^{j}$. Moreover, if $i=1,3$ (resp.\ $2,4$), $X^{i}$ is distributed as a Brownian bridge in $\mathcal{B}(S,\delta-2^{-n-1/2})$ (resp.\ $\mathbb D\setminus S$) conditioned to hit $S$ (resp.\ $\partial\mathcal{B}(S,\delta-2^{-n-1/2})$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma ac excursions of arXiv:2507.20324

[Theorem thm:REA of arXiv:2604.23981, 'Accelerating sampling via asymptotic relaxation enhancing flows'] Consider a given flow $v$. Let
$\sigma:=\liminf_{A\to\infty}\Psi_A$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $v$ is relaxation enhancing (or $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)=\emptyset$)
if and only if $\sigma=\infty$, and also if and only if $\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=\infty$.

\item  If $\sigma<\infty$, then $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)$
is nonempty and 
\begin{gather}
\sigma=\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=r(v).
\end{gather}
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, suppose $\sigma<\infty$ and $q_0$ satisfies Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper) with $q_0-1\in \mathcal{Y}$. Then, for any $\delta>0$, there is some $A_0$ such that whenever $A>A_0$, one has
\[
\mathcal{H}(\rho(t)| \pi)=\int q \log q \pi dx \le C\int |h|^2\pi \,dx \le C_1\exp(-(\sigma-\delta) t),
\]
where $C_1$ depends only on the two constants in Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper).
