body:
For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph G with p_c(G)<1, the historical Benjamini-Schramm question asks whether at p=p_c(G) there is almost surely no infinite open cluster. The p_c<1 hypothesis is essential: on the two-sided line p_c=1 and all edges are open at that parameter. This card records the precise question, not a present-day open-status verdict.
Independent Bernoulli bond percolation
G infinite, connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive
p_c(G)<1 in the question
title: Critical nonpercolation on quasi-transitive graphs: exact scope

[Corollary cor:P_t-bounded of arXiv:2511.22162, 'Landau Hamiltonian with Gaussian white noise potential and the asymptotics of its bottom o'] For $\bA \in \ccA$ and $q = (h, \zeta) \in \ccM$, $(P_t^B(\bA, q))_{t \ge 0}$ defines a strongly continuous semigroup satisfying the bound
	\begin{equ}
		\left\| P_t \right\|_{\cL(L^2(B))} \leq M_h^B e^{\omega^B(\bA, q) t},
	\end{equ}
	for all $t \ge 0$, where $M_h^B$ is given by (equation eq:C-and-M of the paper) and $\omega^B(\bA, q)$ is some positive constant bounded by
	\[\omega^B(\bA, q) \lesssim (\log M_h^B) (1 + \left\| \bA \right\|_{\ccA(B)} + \left\| q \right\|_{\ccM(B)})^a,\]
	for some power $a > 0$.
title: Corollary cor:P_t-bounded of arXiv:2511.22162

[Lemma 21 (Localized martingale property) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] For each fixed $\delta\ge2$, $\eps\in(0,1)$ and $n\ge1$, define
\[
M_t^{W,n}:=\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}u'_{\delta,\eps}(Y_s)
\bigl(a(s,X_s)-\wt a(s,\wt X_s)\bigr)\dd W_s
\]
and
\[
M_t^{Z,n}:=\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}\int_{\R\setminus\{0\}}
\{u_{\delta,\eps}(Y_{s-}+\gamma_s z)-u_{\delta,\eps}(Y_{s-})\}\,\wt N(\md s,\md z),
\]
where $\gamma_s:=\sigma(s,X_{s-})-\wt\sigma(s,\wt X_{s-})$. Then $M^{W,n}$ and $M^{Z,n}$ are true martingales.

[Corollary 10 (Turning-angle range and sharpness) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] For a non-orthogonal discrete general helix with acute helix angle $\alpha$,
\[
\boxed{\theta_i\le 2\alpha\qquad(1\le i\le n-1).}
\]
Equality holds exactly when $y_i=0$, equivalently $\psi_i=0$.
Conversely, given arbitrary turning angles $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_{n-1}\in(0,\pi)$, every
\[
\alpha\in\left[\frac12\max_i\theta_i,\frac\pi2\right)
\]
occurs as the acute helix angle of some non-orthogonal discrete general helix with those turning angles and suitable torsion angles. Thus the turning-angle sequence alone imposes no further compatibility condition; the right panel of Figure~\ref{fig:phase-parametrisation} displays the bound and its equality case. If the lower endpoint $\alpha=\frac12\max_i\theta_i$ is chosen and all turning angles are equal, then all $\psi_i=0$, hence all $\phi_i=\pi$; this is exactly the alternating planar overlap described in Remark~\ref{rem:branch-overlap}.

[Theorem thm:flowinguts of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(M\) be a closed 3-manifold and \(\varphi\) be a pseudo-Anosov flow without perfect fits on \(M\).
Let \(\mathcal{C}_{2}(\varphi)\) be the carried cone of \(\varphi\) in \(H_{2}(M)\), where the negative Euler class and the Thurston norm match.
For any primitive element \(z\) in \(\mathcal{C}_{2}(\varphi)\), there is a well-defined tight semiflow on the homology guts \(\operatorname{Guts}(M,z)\) associated to \(z\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma improved-one-step of arXiv:2607.05054, 'Root Dynamics of Differentiated Polynomials with Rotationally Invariant Structure'] Let $(r_j)_{1 \le j \le n}$ be an increasing sequence of positive real numbers, and let  
\[
\alpha \ge \max_{1 \le j \le n-1} \frac{r_j}{r_{j+1}} .
\]  
Suppose the $j$-th smallest root of $Q$ is exactly $r_j$ for $1 \le j \le n$. Define  
\begin{align}
y = \frac{2 + \log_{-}(\log(\alpha^{-1}))}{\log(\alpha^{-1})}, \qquad \log_{-}(x) = \max(0, -\log x).
\end{align}

Then, for integers $m \ge 1$ and $1 \le q \le m-1$, the $j$-th smallest root $z_j$ of  
\[
S(z) = q Q(z) + m z Q'(z), \qquad 2 \le j \le n,
\]  
satisfies  

\[
\left(1 - \frac{1}{\max(1,\, j-1 - y)}\right) r_j \;\le\; z_j \;\le\; \left(1 - \frac{\alpha}{j+1+2y}\right) r_j .
\]

For $q = 0$ and $3 \le j \le n$, the $(j-1)$-th smallest root of $Q'$ satisfies the same upper bound, and for $2 \le j \le n$ the same lower bound.
title: Lemma improved-one-step of arXiv:2607.05054

[Dfs df0 of arXiv:2604.24061, 'A characterization of ruin-inducing probability measures in a renewal risk model'] \normalfont
		Let $Q$ be a probability measure on $(\varOmega,\varSigma)$.   \smallskip
		
		\noindent\textbf{(a)} If $\mathcal G{\,\subseteq\,}\varSigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra of subsets of $\varOmega$, then  $Q$ is \textit{absolutely continuous}  with respect to $P$ on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$) if
		\[
		\forall\; A\in\mathcal G\quad  \Big( P(A)=0\Rightarrow Q(A)=0 \Big).
		\] 
		In addition, if $P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,} Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{equivalent} on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\sim\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$). For $\mathcal G{\,=\,}\varSigma$ simply write $Q{\,\ll\,} P$ and $Q{\sim}P$.  
		\smallskip
		
		\noindent  	\textbf{(b)} If $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$ is a filtration for $\varSigma$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{progressively equivalent} on $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, if $Q$ and $P$   are equivalent on each  $\mathcal G_t$ (i.e., $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t{\,\sim\,} P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t$). If $P$ and $Q$  are progressively equivalent with respect to $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, we write
		\[
		\frac{dQ}{dP}{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t:=\frac{d(Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)}{d(P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)} \,\,\text{ for all }  t\in\mathbb R_+
		\]
		for simplicity.

[Definition def:rod_subsegments of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] For \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(j=1,\ldots,K\), define the time intervals
\begin{align*}
R^-_{ij} &:= \bigl\{ u \in \mathbb{Z} : (2j-1)L_E \le \rho_i-u \le 2jL_E \bigr\}, \\
R^+_{ij} &:= \bigl\{ u \in \mathbb{Z} : (2j-1)L_E \le u-\rho_i \le 2jL_E \bigr\}.
\end{align*}
The corresponding path segments are
\[
S(R^-_{ij}) := (S_u:\ u\in R^-_{ij}),
\qquad
S(R^+_{ij}) := (S_u:\ u\in R^+_{ij}).
\]
We refer to these path segments as the \textit{rod sub-segments}. See Figure~(fig:rod_subsegments of the paper) for an illustration.

body:
[Prop 4 of arXiv:2609.03791, 'Canonical Bochner--K\"{a}hler potentials via the Sasaki--K\"{a}hler correspondence'] The moduli space of (local) Bochner--K\"{a}hler manifolds is the quotient space of $\mathcal H_n\oplus \mathbb C^n \oplus\mathbb R$ modulo the $\operatorname{U}(n)$ action described above, with $(X,a,r)$ regarded as general elements in $\mathcal H_n\oplus \mathbb C^n \oplus\mathbb R$. Here $\mathcal H_n$ is the space of hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. By means of the $\operatorname{U}(n)$ action one can normalise $(X,a,r)$ such that
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $X$ is diagonal with entries ordered such that $X_{j,j}\geq X_{j+1,j+1}$, and
        \item $a_{j+1}=0$ whenever  $X_{j,j}=X_{j+1,j+1}$,
    \end{itemize}
which identifies the moduli space with a subset in $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^n\times \mathbb R$ containing a dense open subset. 

If the eigenvalues of $X$ are distinct then the subgroup of $\operatorname{U}(n)$ that keeps $X$ diagonal is $\operatorname{U}(1)^n$, which can be used to make all entries of $a$ real and non-negative. Such cases cover an open and dense piece of the moduli space. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def-quantum-cone of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $W > 0$ and let $\alpha = Q - \frac{W}{2\gamma}$. Sample independent standard Brownian motions $(B_t)_{t \geq 0}, (\tilde B_t)_{t \geq 0}$ conditioned on $\tilde B_{t} - (Q-\alpha) < 0$ for all $t>0$. Let
	\[Y_t := \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} 
				B_{t}+(Q-\alpha) t & \mbox{for} & t\ge 0\\
				\tilde{B}_{-t} -(Q-\alpha) |t| & \mbox{for} & t<0
			\end{array} 
			\right. \]
	Let $\hat \psi = \psi_1 + \psi_2$ where $\psi_1$ is the distribution on $\mathcal{C}$ which is constant on each line segment $\{t\} \times [0,2\pi]$ satisfying $\psi_1(z) = Y_{\mathrm{Re}(z)}$, and $\psi_2$ is an independent copy of $h_\mathcal{C}^2$. The \emph{weight $W$ quantum cone} is $(\mathcal{C}, \hat \psi, -\infty, +\infty)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and we define the probability measure $\mathcal{M}^\mathrm{cone}(W)$ to be its law.
title: Definition def-quantum-cone of arXiv:2411.19810

[Theorem thm-ccmt of arXiv:2607.25567, 'Random Trees in Hyperbolic FPP'] Let $L$ be a non-amenable hyperbolic locally compact group. If $L$ contains
	a cocompact amenable closed subgroup, then there exists a unique maximal compact normal
	subgroup $W \subset L$, such that 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Either $L/W \subset Isom (X)$ where $X$ is a rank one symmetric space of noncompact type, and $L/W$ acts transitively on $X$.
		\item Or $L/W \subset Isom ({\mathcal T})$, where ${\mathcal T}$ is a locally finite
		non-elementary tree. Further, 
		\begin{itemize}
			\item $L/W$ acts faithfully and properly discontinuously by simplicial automorphisms without inversions on ${\mathcal T}$ with exactly two orbits of vertices,
			\item The $L$ action on the boundary $\partial {\mathcal T}$ is 2-transitive, i.e.\ it is transitive on $\partial^2 T$. 
		\end{itemize}
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-ccmt of arXiv:2607.25567

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] Let $Z\subset\Sn^1$ be the two singular parameter values of the closed profile
curve constructed above.  The quantity
\[
 \chi=\cos^{k-1}\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{ds}
\]
has a continuous extension through every $s_0\in Z$, with
\begin{equation}
 \chi(s_0)=\frac{r(s_0)^{k-1}x(s_0)\sin\theta_0}{A}.
\end{equation}
Consequently the formula
\begin{equation}
 d\mathcal K_k[X]
 =
 \left[
 -A r^{n-k}\chi+B r^{n-k-1}\cos^k\theta
 \right]\,ds\,d\omega
\end{equation}
defines a finite signed Radon measure on the fixed parameter manifold
$M=\Sn^1\times\Sn^{n-1}$, where $d\omega$ is the standard volume measure on
$\Sn^{n-1}$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}
 =
 -A\frac{\chi}{r^{k-1}}
 +B\left(\frac{\cos\theta}{r}\right)^k
\end{equation}
is continuous on $M$ and satisfies
\[
 \sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}=-\langle X,\nu\rangle,
 \qquad
 \mathcal K_k[X]=\sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}\,d\mu_X.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \mathcal K_k[X](\{s_0\}\times\Sn^{n-1})=0
 \qquad (s_0\in Z).
\]

    \end{align} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Proposition x0weakly of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Consider a sequence of random variables $X^n_0$ on $\mathbb{Z}^{+}$, whose distribution is defined by
\[
\mathbf{P}\left(X^n_0=k\right)=\frac{\left(q_n;q_n\right)_\infty}{\left(q_n;q_n\right)_k}q_n^k,\qquad k=0,1,2,\dots

Then, as $n\to\infty$
\begin{equation}
    \frac{X^n_0-\tfrac{1}{\gamma}\sqrt{n}\log\left(\sqrt{n}\right)}{\sqrt{n}} \overset{d}{\Rightarrow} X,
\end{equation}
where $X$ has density
\[
f_X\left(x\right)=e^{-\gamma x}\exp\Big(-\tfrac{1}{\gamma} e^{-\gamma x}\Big),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn 38 (Markov operator, canonical process, and canonical measure) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $\br \in \Ek$ be an SRI chain with base measure $\nu$ and decay function $F$. Define the associated \textbf{Markov operator} $P_{\br}$ to act on functions $f$ by the formula $$(P_{\br} f)(\mathbf x) := \int_{I^k} f(\y) \br ( \mathbf x,\dr \y),$$ defined for all Borel-measurable functions $f:I^k\to\mathbb R$ for which the integral converges absolutely for all $\x\in I^k.$

    We also denote by $(\mathbf R_r)_{r\ge 0} = (   R^1_r,...,   R^k_r)_{r\ge 0}$ the \textbf{canonical coordinate process} on $(I^k)^{\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}},$ and we denote by $\Pbb$ the \textbf{canonical probability measure} on $(I^k)^{\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}}$ under which the canonical coordinate process is distributed as the Markov chain with transition kernel $\br$ started from initial state $\x$. We also denote by $\Ebb$ the associated \textbf{expectation operator.}
title: Markov operator, canonical process, and canonical measure

body:
Let Omega be a bounded domain in R^n with C^1 boundary and outward unit normal nu, and let u be a sufficiently regular solution of -Laplacian u = f(u) in Omega with u = 0 on the boundary. Write F for the primitive of f with F(0) = 0. Then n times the integral over Omega of F(u) minus ((n-2)/2) times the integral over Omega of u f(u) equals (1/2) times the boundary integral of (x dotted with nu) times |partial u / partial nu|^2. Taking f(u) = |u|^{p-1} u with the critical exponent p = (n+2)/(n-2) makes the left side vanish identically, so on a STAR-SHAPED domain, where x dotted with nu >= 0 with strict positivity somewhere, the boundary term forces the normal derivative to vanish and hence u = 0: the critical Dirichlet problem has no nontrivial regular solution on a star-shaped domain.
Enough regularity to justify the integrations by parts (u in C^2 up to the boundary, or in H^2 with the boundary terms interpreted by trace theory), the Dirichlet condition, and C^1 boundary.
The non-existence conclusion needs star-shapedness;
on an annulus the identity holds but proves nothing, and indeed nontrivial critical solutions exist there.

[Proposition 9 (Transforms and moments) of arXiv:2607.20680, 'Exact Scale--Shape Factorization of the Typical Poisson--Voronoi Cell Volume in Arbitrary '] For every $s\geq0$,
  \begin{equation}
    
    \E[e^{-sY_d}]
    =
    \sum_{k=d+1}^\infty
    p_{d,k}\,
    \E\bigl[(1+sA_k)^{-k}\bigr],
  \end{equation}
with the convention that terms with $p_{d,k}=0$ contribute zero. Moreover, for every integer $r\geq1$,
  \begin{equation}
    
    \E[Y_d^r]
    =
    \sum_{k=d+1}^\infty
    p_{d,k}\,
    (k)_r\,\E[A_k^r],
  \end{equation}
where the identity is understood in \([0,\infty]\), and \((k)_r=\Gamma(k+r)/\Gamma(k)\) denotes the rising factorial, also called the Pochhammer symbol.
title: Transforms and moments

[Definition 1 (Homogeneity and population) of arXiv:2605.28677, 'Weak universality for stochastic reaction-diffusion models\\ with long-range correlated no'] The \emph{homogeneity} of a multiindex is defined by 
\begin{equation}
| \beta|
\coloneqq
 \alpha \Big(1+ (\kk-1) \sum_{k\geq\kk} \beta (k) - \sum_{ \bf{n}} \beta ( {\bf{n}} ) \Big)
+
2 \sum_{k\geq\kk} \beta (k)
+
\sum_{\bf{n}}|{\bf{n}}| \beta ({ \bf{ n}})\,,
\end{equation}

where 

\begin{equation}
|\n|\coloneqq 2n_0+n_1+\dots+n_d \, .
\end{equation}

Here and in the following, all sums and products over $\n$ are indexed by $\n=(n_0,\dots,n_d)\in\NN^{1+d}$.

A multiindex $\beta$ is called \emph{populated} if 

\begin{equation}
\beta = \delta_\n
\quad\textnormal{or}\quad
\beta=\delta_{\kk}+\delta_{\n_1}+\dots+\delta_{\n_{\kk}}
\quad\textnormal{or}\quad
[\beta]\coloneqq\sum_{k\geq\kk}(k-1)\beta(k)-\sum_\n\beta(\n)
\geq0\,.
\end{equation}

If $\beta=\delta_\n$, we say that $ \beta$ is \emph{purely polynomial}.
title: Homogeneity and population

body:
[Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let $\chi$ be a Navier--Stokes potential on an open fiber domain  \(\mathscr F\subset\mathscr E\) (containing its zero section) of a relaxation bundle \(\mathscr E\subseteq\Sym^2T^*\Mcal\). Then, a \textbf{relaxation rate map} consists of a smooth fiberwise map $\mathscr B=\mathscr B(\beta,\zeta)\in\mathscr E^*$ defined for all future timelike $\beta$ and all $\zeta \in \mathscr F$, satisfying the following conditions.

\bei 

\item \emph{Stable equilibrium property:}
\bel{eq:pot-relax-map}
\mathscr B(\beta,0)=0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)\geq0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\zeta=0.
\ee

\item \emph{Positivity property:}  Its linearization along the equilibrium manifold $\mathbb M$ given by 
\bel{eq:pot-relax-linearization}
\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)
\coloneqq
\frac{\del\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}}{\del\zeta_{\gamma\delta}}(\beta,0)
\ee
must be symmetric under interchange of the two index pairs and positive definite on~$\mathscr E$, namely
\be
\eta_{\alpha\beta}\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)\eta_{\gamma\delta}>0
\qquad
\text{for every nonzero }\eta\in\mathscr E.
\ee
\eei
Furthermore, the associated \textbf{production term} is
\bel{production-term-value}
\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}
\coloneqq
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}
\geq0.
\ee
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.31171

\]

Let n>=1, L_n=beta_n=n and M_n=2^(n^2). Take M_n distinct singleton paths, each with deterministic zero Gaussian field and positive weight exp(n), and one long path of M_n independent N(0,n) coordinates, each of weight 1/M_n. The covariance is PSD and its maximum diagonal is n. Put S_n(xi)=M_n^(-1) sum_i exp(xi X_i), H_n(xi)=min(n,log S_n(xi)), and F_n(xi)=-(1/n)log(exp[-n^2(1-log 2)]+exp[-n log S_n(xi)]). Then E[H_n(2)-H_n(0)]/n -> 1 whereas E[F_n(2)-F_n(0)]/n -> 1-log 2. Hard-min median exponents converge, beta_n->infinity and maximum variance is O(L_n), but normalized integrated soft-min response has the wrong endpoint limit when uniform smoothing error is omitted. This is a finite Gaussian counterexample, not planar LFPP.

[Proposition 43 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{2},1)$, $\delta>0$, and $V^{N,\delta,y}(t,z)$ defined by~\eqref{eq:V delta N def}. If for some $K >0$ and all $j \in \N, n \in \{0,1,2\}$, we have the almost sure bound
\[\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_{x}} \leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j},\]
then there exists $C(d,\alpha,K,\delta) >0$ such that for all $N, p\geq 1, y\in \T^d$, there exists a splitting
\[\iop^{N,\delta,y} V^{N,\delta,y} = \sum_{j=0}^N I^{j,N,\delta}\]
such that
\begin{align}

    \|I^{j,N,\delta}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_a L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^{1/2 + (2\alpha-1)/64}_t \mathcal{C}^1_z} \leq C p^{1/2} 2^{- C^{-1}j},\\
    
      \|\nabla_a I^{j,N,\delta}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_a L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^{1}_t \mathcal{C}^1_z} \leq C 2^{2j}\|\nabla \Psi^{N,\delta,y}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_a L^p_\omega\mathcal{C}^0_t}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    Then equation~\eqref{eq:mainELD} holds if and only if

         \left|\int_{-\eps}^\eps\left(e^{-itN}-e^{-it(N+g(n))}\right)\psi_Y(t)\,\frac{\Psi(t)^n-n\Psi(t)}{it}\, dt\right|
            =O\left(\frac{n}{N^{2-2/a}}\right)

[Lemma 9 (Correlation bound in the large increment case) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] Assume that \(\rho\) satisfies the regular variation assumption
    \(\abs{\rho(k)} = \abs{k}^{-\alpha}\slowVar(k)\) for a slowly varying
    function. Then for all
    \(\epsilon \in (0, \frac1{\hermRank} - \alpha)\) there exists \(n_0 =
    n_0(\slowVar, \epsilon) \in \nat\) and \(A=A(n_0, \slowVar)>0\) such that for all
    \(n\ge n_0\) and \(\frac1n \le t-s\)
    \[
        \frac{n^{-2\hurst}}{\slowVar(n)^\hermRank} \sum_{i, j = 0}^{\floor{n t}-\floor{n s}} \abs{\rho(i-j)}^\hermRank
        \le C (t-s)^{2\hurst - \epsilon \hermRank}.
   \]
    with \(C=\bigl(
            \tfrac{A^\hermRank \max\set{T^{2\epsilon\hermRank},1}}{(2\hurst-\epsilon \hermRank)(2\hurst - 1-\epsilon\hermRank)}
            + 15\bigl(\tfrac{A}{\slowVar(n_0)n_0^\epsilon}\bigr)^\hermRank
        \bigr) > 0
    \).

Consider the bias-free scalar-output ReLU network f(x)=W_(ell+1) ReLU(W_ell ... ReLU(W_1 x)), with d_0=d, d_1=...=d_ell=k, d_(ell+1)=1; all entries and layers are independent and W_i entries have law N(0,1/d_(i-1)). There is a universal constant C such that with probability at least0.9, f is nonzero on the whole unit sphere and simultaneously for every x,y in S^(d-1), |f(x)-f(y)|/|f(x)| <= C*sqrt(log(d)/d). For sufficiently large d this implies a single common nonzero sign on the whole sphere. The statement concerns this depth and width window, with a linear final readout and no biases.

    -\rho(1-\eta\lambda_j)h_{k-1}^{\nesterov}(j),
    \quad
    h_0^{\nesterov}(j)=1,\ 
    h_1^{\nesterov}(j)=1-\eta\lambda_j.
\]
The roots are
\[
    y_{j,+},y_{j,-}
    =
    \frac{(1+\rho)(1-\eta\lambda_j)
    \pm
    \sqrt{(1+\rho)^2(1-\eta\lambda_j)^2-4\rho(1-\eta\lambda_j)}}{2}.
\]
The discriminant is negative precisely when
\[
    \eta\lambda_j>\frac{(1-\rho)^2}{(1+\rho)^2}.
\]
Thus the comparison between $\eta$ and $(1-\rho)^2$ determines whether a coordinate is overdamped or underdamped. body:
[Defn Irreducibility criterion of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] The standard module $V_{n,p}$ is irreducible if and only if the Gram matrix is non-degenerate, i.e.,
\[
\det G_{n,p} \ne 0.
\]
If $\det G_{n,p} = 0$, then $V_{n,p}$ is reducible, and its radical
\[
R_{n,p} := \{x \in V_{n,p} \mid \langle x, y \rangle = 0, \forall y \in V_{n,p}\}
\]
is a nonzero proper submodule.
title: Irreducibility criterion

body:
[Corollary 13 (Empirical $W_2$ floors) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Let $\rho$ be a probability measure on $\R^d$ with a finite $q$th
moment for some $q>4$, and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_N$ be i.i.d.\ with law
$\rho$. Then
\[
    \E W_2^2\left(\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{Y_i},\rho\right)
    \le C_\rho
    \begin{cases}
      N^{-1/2}, & d<4,\\
      N^{-1/2}\log(1+N), & d=4,\\
      N^{-2/d}, & d>4.
    \end{cases}
\]
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:concentration}, this holds for $\rho = \pi$. Moreover, under the assumptions made in Proposition~\ref{prop:subgaussian}, the constant can be
chosen uniformly in $t$ such that the above holds for $\rho=\mu_t$, $t\ge0$.

[Definition 23 of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] We define the linear map $\Delta^\partial : \langle \mcT \rangle \to \langle \mcT \rangle \otimes \langle \mcT_1 \rangle$ recursively via
	\begin{align*}
		& \Delta^\partial \Xi_\mfl^j = \sum_{|k|_\mfs < o({\Xi_\mfl^j})} \frac{X^k}{k!} \otimes \Xi_{(\mfl, \partial)}^{k+j}, \qquad \Delta^\partial X_i = 0
		\\
		& \Delta^\partial \mcI_\mfl^k \tau = (\mcI_\mfl^k \otimes \id) \Delta^\partial \tau + \sum_{|j|_\mfs < o(\mcI_\mfl^k \tau) } \frac{X^j}{j!} \otimes \mcI_{(\mfl, \partial)}^{k+j} \tau
		\\
		& \Delta^\partial (\tau \sigma) = (\Delta^\partial \tau) (\Delta \sigma) + (\Delta^\partial \sigma) (\Delta \tau)
	\end{align*}

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.12142, 'Nonlinear filtering with stochastic discontinuities'] Let $\Gamma=\Gamma(\omega;t,y)$ be an $\bbF^Y$-predictable function such that $E[(e^\Gamma*\nu)_t]< \infty$
    and 
\begin{align}
    e^{\Gamma(t, y)} - \Delta \tilde B_t > 0, \qquad t \ge 0, 
\end{align}
where
    $ \tilde B := (e^\Gamma -1)*\nu. $
Furthermore, define 
    $
        M:= (e^\Gamma-1)*\tilde \mu.
    $
    Then $Z:=\ccE(M)$ is a strictly positive $(\bbF^Y,P)$-martingale 
     whenever $E[Z_t] = 1$ for all $t \ge 0$.
    Moreover, there exists a locally equivalent measure $P'$, such that
    $$
    dP'_t  = Z_t \, dP_t, \quad t \geq 0,
    $$
    and under $P'$, the compensator of  $\mu$ is given by
    \begin{align}
    \nu'(dt, dy) = (e^{\Gamma(t, y)}-\Delta \tilde B_t) \nu(dt, dy).
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.12142

[Definition 82 (The Levi-Civita connection $\nullangD$ of $\gnulltori$ and related differential operators) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill

\begin{enumerate}
\item We denote the Levi-Civita connection of $\gnulltori$ by $\nullangD$.
	In particular,
	for $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent tensorfields $\upxi$, 
	we have $\nullangD \upxi = \nulltorusproject \Dfour \upxi$.
\item If $\Xi$ is an $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent one-form, 
	then we define its $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-divergence 
	to be the scalar function
	$\nullangDiv \Xi \eqdef \gnulltori^{-1} \cdot \nullangD \Xi$. 
	Similarly, if $V$ is an $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent vectorfield, 
	then we define its $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-divergence to be the scalar function 
	$\nullangDiv V \eqdef \gnulltori^{-1} \cdot \nullangD V_{\flat}$,
	where $V_{\flat}$ is the one-form that is $\gfour$-dual to $V$.
\item If $\Xi$ is an $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent one-form, we define its curl to be the scalar function given by $\nullangcurl \eqdef \breve{\in}^{AB} \nullangD_A \Xi_B$, where $\breve{\in}$ is the area element of the Riemannian manifold $(\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u},\gnulltori)$ with respect to an arbitrary frame $f_A, A = 2,3$.
\item If $\upxi$ is a symmetric type $\binom{0}{2}$ $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent tensorfield, 
	then we define its $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-divergence $\nullangDiv \upxi$ 
	to be the $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent one-form with the following 
	$\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-components for $A=2,3$:
	\begin{align} 
	[\nullangDiv \upxi]\left(\nullgeop{x^A} \right) 
	\eqdef 
	(\gnulltori^{-1})(\rmd x^B,\rmd x^C) 
	\left[\nullangD_{\nullgeop{x^B}} \upxi \right]\left(\nullgeop{x^C},\nullgeop{x^A} \right).
	\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
title: The Levi-Civita connection $\nullangD$ of $\gnulltori$ and related differential operators

[Lemma lem:fixed-interrupted-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a spatial ribbon map $\Gamma$, one labelled residual
component $\mathcal C$ with $r_{\mathcal C}\le L\log n$ nonconstant
slots, one physical anchor, and its complete packet/root channel.
A hard ordinary supernode is one fused physical time containing either a
nonsingleton packet resource or the time-indexed linear Jacobi child
$-2N^{-1}W_i$.  The coupled pure-Weyl root is a special hard symbol; the
total number of special root symbols is bounded by an absolute constant
$B_0$.  Aggregate Ricci is not present in this ported theorem and is
treated separately in the aggregate-Ricci synthesis below.

For every fixed $L$ there are $A_L<\infty$ and a numerical exponent
$B<\infty$ for which the estimate below holds.

Suppose $\mathcal C$ contains a hard resource and reserve its
chronologically earliest resource-bearing hard supernode as the endpoint,
breaking a same-node tie by the fixed ribbon-slot order.  Let
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{surplus ordinary hard supernodes}\},\\
 o_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{all }\mathsf S^\pm
                         \text{ singleton supernodes}\},\\
 v_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{all }\mathsf V
                         \text{ singleton supernodes}\},\\
 t_{\mathcal C}&=b_{\mathcal C}+o_{\mathcal C}+v_{\mathcal C}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.4.1x}
\]
If $\mathfrak e_{\mathcal C}$ is the selected endpoint resource and
$\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}$ is the remaining normalized terminal
amplitude, then, for $\delta=1/16$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{\text{weak orders, equality blocks, finite gaps,}\\
                  \text{and typed states on }\mathcal C}}
 |\operatorname{Contr}_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}|
 \le A_L^{r_{\mathcal C}}(r_{\mathcal C}+1)^B
 \mathfrak e_{\mathcal C}\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}
 n^{-\delta t_{\mathcal C}}.}
\tag{3.4.1x$_1$}
\]
The estimate holds at the application horizon $m=cN$ for each fixed
$c\ge1$, uniformly in every finite remaining-time constraint; its
constant is independent of $c$, while the threshold in $n$ may depend on
$c$.  Summing the one anchor costs at most $m$.

[Prop 18 of arXiv:2604.03206, 'The extreme statistics of some noncolliding Brownian processes'] Let $H_0$ be a $n \times n$ Hermitian matrix with eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n$, and
    $H(t)$ be a Brownian motion in the space of $n \times n$ Hermitian matrices started from zero as in \eqref{eqn:hbm}.
    Suppose $0 < t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_k$. Then
    $$ \mathbf{Pr}(\lambda_{max}(H(t_i)+H_0) \leq a_i, 1 \leq i \leq k) = \det(I - K)_{L^2(\{1, \cdots, k\} \times [0,\infty))}.$$
    The kernel $K$ takes the form
    $$K(i,x;j,y) = - e^{(t_j^{-1} - t_i^{-1})\partial^2/2}\left(x + \frac{a_i}{t_i}, y + \frac{a_j}{t_j}\right) \ind{t_j < t_i} 
    + K_{nw}\left (t_i^{-1}, x + \frac{a_i}{t_i}; t_j^{-1}, y + \frac{a_j}{t_j}\right)$$
    where $K_{nw}$ is the kernel from \eqref{eqn:Knw} with $\mu_i = \lambda_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 18 of arXiv:2604.03206

[Cor lemma: ballisticity of arXiv:2605.26869, 'Law of Large Numbers for a random walk on dynamic environments with drift'] Let $\rho\in J$. 
    For any $v_\star \in (0, v^-(\rho))$, there exists $c>0$ such that for all $K \in \mathbb{N}$ large enough, we have that 
    \begin{equation} 
        \mathbb{P}^\rho \left( \exists n \in \mathbb{N} : X_n < n v_\star - K \right) \leq 2 \exp\left( -c K^{1/1000} \right).
    \end{equation}
    For any  $v_\star \in (v^+(\rho),1)$, we obtain the same bound for 
    $\mathbb{P}^\rho \left( \exists n \in \mathbb{N} : X_n > n v_\star + K \right)$.
title: Cor lemma: ballisticity of arXiv:2605.26869

DRAFT: proof (unaudited), w726-T332-C2 v1. Let n>=1 and 0<=c<=n. Let G be G(n,c/n), with independent edges and iid standard-Borel vertex marks independent of its edges, with numerical labels forgotten; let T be an identically marked Poisson(c) Galton-Watson tree. Root G at a fixed vertex independently of graph and marks. For these graph and tree laws, let states lie in a bounded Borel subset K of a separable Banach space, diameter D, invariant under all updates on locally finite graphs and induced subgraphs. Initial states depend only on own iid marks. Each measurable isomorphism-invariant layer rule depends only on the mark, own state and the unordered neighbor-state list, is the same on graph and tree independently of graph size, and is rho-Lipschitz in the maximum norm of the entire input list, uniformly over degrees, marks and layers, with 0<rho<1. Define delta_1(r)=min(1,4(1+c)^(2r+2)/(3n)). For every depth L and radius r>=0, root-law W1 is at most 2D rho^r+D delta_1(r). For a scalar 1-Lipschitz readout bounded by B, pooled variance is at most 34 B^2 (1+c)^(2r+2)/n+2D^2 rho^(2r), uniformly in L. Optimizing r gives polynomial n-rates for fixed c and rho. This does not assert a depth-uniform TV bound or an expected empirical bounded-Lipschitz supremum. Independent review is pending.

body:
[Lemma l.non-recursive of arXiv:2505.15283, 'Quantization of Probability Distributions via Divide-and-Conquer: Convergence and Error Pr'] Let $n\in {\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}$ and let $\alpha \in \{\pm\}^n$.
    Define $\Omega_\pm,\mu_\pm$ as above and for $\alpha \in \{\pm\}^{n}, n\geq 1$ define $\Omega_{\alpha\pm}$ recursively by
    \[
    \Omega_{\alpha-} = \{x \in \Omega_\alpha : x \leq f(\mu_\alpha)\},\ \Omega_{\alpha+} = \{x \in \Omega_\alpha : x > f(\mu_\alpha)\}    
    \]
    and (assuming that $\mu(\Omega_{\alpha})>0$ for all $\alpha \in \{\pm\}^j, j = 1,2,...,n-1$)
    \[
        \mu_{\alpha\pm}(A) =    
        \frac{ \mu(A \cap \Omega_{\alpha \pm})  }{\mu(\Omega_{\alpha \pm})},\ A \in {\mathcal{B}}({\mathbb{R}})   
    .
    \]
    Then
    \begin{equation}
    \mu^{(n),f} = T^f(\mu,n)=
    \sum_{\alpha \in \{\pm\}^n} 
        \mu(\Omega_{\alpha}) \delta_{f(\mu_\alpha)},\  n \geq 0,
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation}
    F^{(n),f}(x) := \sum_{ \substack{ \alpha \in \{\pm\}^n : \\ f(\mu_\alpha) \leq x  } }   \mu(\Omega_{\alpha}).
\end{equation}
title: Lemma l.non-recursive of arXiv:2505.15283

[Lemma 6 (Dyadic Green estimate) of arXiv:2605.09641, 'The Ballot Event for Two-Player Coupon Collection: A Renewal--Catalan Asymptotic'] Fix $g_0\ge0$, and let $s_0=s_0(d)$ be an integer sequence satisfying $0\le s_0<d-g_0$ and $s_0=o(d)$.  Then, for all sufficiently large $d$,
\begin{equation}
        \E_{s_0,g_0}\sum_{n<\tau}\Delta(S_n,G_n)
        \le
        C_{g_0}H(s_0,g_0)
        \left(\frac{s_0}{d}+\frac{\log d}{\sqrt d}\right),
\end{equation}
where $C_{g_0}$ depends only on $g_0$.
Consequently,
\[
        \E_{s_0,g_0}\sum_{n<\tau}\Delta(S_n,G_n)=o(H(s_0,g_0)).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Dyadic Green estimate

body: [Proposition 5 of arXiv:2605.04867, 'First server's effect on the expected number of games in Tennis'] Let $T$ denote the total number of games in a best-of-three sets match between $A$ and $B$. Assume $\G_A + \G_B > 1$. Then, writing $T^\text{match}_A= \E(T\mid S_1=A)$ and $T^\text{match}_B = \E(T\mid S_1=B)$, we have $T^\text{match}_A<T^\text{match}_B$ if $\G_A>\G_B$.

body:
Let n_1, ..., n_k be pairwise coprime positive integers and N = n_1 n_2 ... n_k. For any integers a_1, ..., a_k there exists an integer x with x = a_i (mod n_i) for every i, and x is unique modulo N. Equivalently, the ring map Z/NZ -> Z/n_1Z x ... x Z/n_kZ, x -> (x mod n_1, ..., x mod n_k), is an isomorphism of rings. The same holds in any commutative ring for pairwise comaximal ideals I_1, ..., I_k: R/(I_1 ... I_k) is isomorphic to the product of the R/I_j.
moduli pairwise coprime (pairwise comaximal ideals in the ring form)

For j != i the term a_j M_j N_j is divisible by n_i because n_i divides N_j, while a_i M_i N_i = a_i (mod n_i); hence x = a_i (mod n_i) for every i. The map Z/NZ -> prod Z/n_iZ is a ring homomorphism, injective by uniqueness, and both sides have N elements, so it is an isomorphism. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \textup{(Algebraic $L^2$-content, unconditional.)} $v_h$ is the unique element of minimal $H_W$-norm in $L^2(\Omega; H_W)$ satisfying the covering condition~(equation eq:covering-condition of the paper); equivalently, $v_h \in \operatorname{Ran}(\mathcal{T}^{*}) \subset L^2(\Omega; H_W)$ with $\mathcal{T}v_h = h$ a.s.
 \item \textup{(Skorokhod-domain membership, conditional.)} Under any one of the cases of Theorem~(thm:covering-regularity of the paper) below, $v_h$ further satisfies $v_h \in \operatorname{Dom}(\delta_U)$.
\end{enumerate}
Part~\textup{(i)} is the SPDE-side specialisation of the algebraic content of Theorem~(thm:pseudoinverse-covering of the paper) and requires no additional hypothesis; only the Skorokhod-integrability of $v_h$ in part~\textup{(ii)} requires the additional input of Theorem~(thm:covering-regularity of the paper).

[Definition def2_1 of arXiv:2607.26169, 'Scaling and partial universality of the height zero probability in the 2D Abelian sandpile'] Let $U\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an open connected region with boundary \(\partial U\). A continuous function \(f : U\cup\partial U \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) is said to be \it{harmonic} in \(U\) if it is twice continuously differentiable and satisfies 
    \[
        \Delta^{(c)} f = 0 \; \text{ in } U.
    \]
    For a given continuous function \(g : \partial U \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\), \(f\) is said to be the solution to Laplace's equation with Dirichlet boundary condition \(g\) if, in addition, it satisfies
    \[
        f = g \; \text{ on } \partial U.
    \]
title: Definition def2_1 of arXiv:2607.26169

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The probability for a needle of length $1$, when trown on a grid of parallel $1$-spaced lines, to intersect one line, is:
$$P=\frac{2}{\pi}$$
Moreover, we have generalizations of this result, with needles of arbitrary length, thrown over a grid of parallel lines, with arbitrary spacing.

[Theo 6 of arXiv:2608.00811, 'Comparison of Dirichlet forms for stable-like random walks on groups of polynomial volume '] Referring to the above setting and notation, given a symmetric stable-like probability measure $\nu$, we have
$$\mathcal E_\nu\asymp \mathcal E_{\rho_{S,\mathbf{v}}}\asymp \mathcal E_{\mu_{S,\bm{\alpha}}},$$
that is, the Dirichlet forms of $\nu$, of the radial measure $\rho_{S,\mathbf{v}}$ and of the $1d$-singular stable-like measure $\mu_{S,\bm{\alpha}}$, are all equivalent.
Moreover, if $\tilde{\nu}$ is another symmetric stable-like probability measure in our collection, form the tuple
$(\tilde{S}, \tilde{\mathbf{v}})$ by concatenating the tuples arising from its components, as before.
The following are equivalent 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\|\cdot\|_{\nu}\asymp \|\cdot \|_{\tilde{\nu}}$
     \item $\mathfrak w_{S,\mathbf{v}}(s)=\mathfrak w_{\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}}}(s)$ for all $
s \in \mbox{\em core}(S,\mathbf{v}) \cup \mbox{\em core}(\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}})$ 
    \item $\mathfrak w_{S,\mathbf{v}}(c)=\mathfrak w_{\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}}}(c)$ for all $
 c\in\mathcal{C}(\mbox{\em core}(S,\mathbf{v})) \cup \mathcal{C}(\mbox{\em core}(\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}}))$ 
\item  $\mbox{\em Red}(\mathcal{N}_{S,\mathbf{v}}) = \mbox{\em Red}(\mathcal{N}_{\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}}})$  and $\mathbf{w}_{S,\mathbf{v}} = \mathbf{w}_{\tilde{S},\tilde{\mathbf{v}}} $
\end{enumerate}
If any of the equivalent conditions above holds, then  $\mathcal E_{\tilde{\nu}}\asymp\mathcal E_\nu$.

Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be real numbers which are CONVEX, meaning the second differences D2 a_n := a_n - 2 a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are >= 0 for every n >= 0, and which tend to 0. (These two hypotheses already force a_n >= 0 and a_n nonincreasing: the first differences a_{n+1} - a_n are nondecreasing, so if one of them were positive the sequence would tend to +infinity. They also force n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, since the differences are monotone.) THEOREM (Young; Zygmund, Trigonometric Series, Ch. V). Put S(x) = a_0/2 + sum_{n >= 1} a_n cos(nx). Then: (1) the series converges for every x not in 2 pi Z, uniformly on every compact subset of (0, 2 pi); (2) S(x) >= 0 for all such x; (3) S is Lebesgue integrable on (-pi, pi), with (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of S over (-pi,pi) equal to a_0/2; (4) the series IS the Fourier series of S, that is a_n = (1/pi) times the integral over (-pi,pi) of S(x) cos(nx) dx for every n >= 0. The whole theorem rests on one identity: with K_n(x) = (1/(n+1)) (sin((n+1)x/2) / sin(x/2))^2 >= 0 the Fejer kernel, normalised so that (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of K_n over (-pi,pi) is 1, double summation by parts gives S(x) = sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) (D2 a_n) (1/2) K_n(x), with sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) D2 a_n = a_0 < infinity. Nonnegativity is then read off from D2 a_n >= 0 and K_n >= 0, and integrability from the normalisation. SHARP EDGES. (a) It is CONVEXITY, not monotone decrease, that does the work: monotone decrease to zero gives convergence off the origin by Dirichlet's test, but it does not produce the Fejer representation and therefore gives neither nonnegativity nor integrability of the sum. (b) The SINE analogue is false in this form. If (b_n) is convex and decreases to 0, then sum b_n sin(nx) still converges pointwise off 2 pi Z, but its sum is Lebesgue integrable if and only if sum b_n / n converges. The classical counterexample is b_n = 1/log n for n >= 2, which is convex and decreases to 0 while sum 1/(n log n) diverges: the resulting series converges everywhere but is not the Fourier series of any Lebesgue integrable function. Never transport the cosine statement to the sine case. (c) 'Integrable' cannot be improved to 'bounded': for a_n of order 1/n the sum behaves like log(1/|x|) near 0, which is integrable and unbounded. (d) The conclusion S >= 0 is on (0, 2 pi); nothing is claimed at x in 2 pi Z, where the series may diverge (it diverges precisely when sum a_n = infinity). (e) Convexity is only assumed for n >= 0 on the given sequence; a sequence that is eventually convex gives the same conclusions after subtracting a trigonometric polynomial, but then nonnegativity of the sum is lost.
(a_n)_{n >= 0} is a real sequence
the second differences a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are nonnegative for every n >= 0 (convexity)
a_n -> 0 as n -> infinity
consequences used and derived from these: a_n >= 0, a_n nonincreasing, n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, sum (n+1)(a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2}) = a_0
integrability is with respect to Lebesgue measure on the circle

[Corollary cor:VEB-volume of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] There exists a real number $\lambda_0 \in (0,1/2)$ such that the following holds. Consider any $\lambda \in (0,\lambda_0)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ such $p_0=1$ and, for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$. Suppose that $\overline{p}$ has finitely many bins which are strongly exposed. 
Let $X$ be the backoff process with
birth rate~$2 \lambda$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and cohort set~$\mathcal{C}=\{A,B\}$ (Definition~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)).
Let $j_0\geq 5$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where  all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Let $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$ be any event determined by 
$\{n^{X^B}(t') : t'\in [T^{\overline{p},j_0}]\}$
which entails that each 
$n^{X^B}(t')$ in this set is at least~$1$.
We will condition on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$.

Let
$\tau_0 =  T^{\overline{p},j_0}$. 
Let
$\Psi_0$ be the  initialising high-level state   
with $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be   the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper) and let $\ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$  (Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-state-space of the paper)) be the  $\Psi_0$-closure (Definition~(def:hls-closed of the paper)) of~$\mathrm{hls}$.  
The $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule~$\mathrm{hls}$ is a transition rule (Definition~(def:transition-rule of the paper)) by Observation~(obs:BB-bounding-is-transrule of the paper) and 
it is $\ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$-valid (Definition~(def:valid of the paper)) by
Lemma~(lem:backoff-bounding-valid of the paper).

Conditioned on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$, the VEB-coupling (Definition~(def:VEB-couple of the paper))   couples $X$ with a volume process $V$ from $\Psi(\tau_0)=\Psi_0$ with  transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$
and with a sequence $E_1, E_2,\ldots $ of escape processes with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
With probability at least~$99/100$,  
both of the following hold.

  
 
  
\begin{itemize}
\item for all $t \ge \tau_0$, $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} \ne \textup{failure}$. 
\item for all $j \ge j_0$, there is
a positive integer $t \le \tau_0 + 1+ {(8j)}^{\phi+1}(W_{j_0}+\dots + W_{j-1})$ such that 
$\Psi(t)$ is $j$-filling or $j$-advancing.
\end{itemize}

Write the independent simple-root coordinates as y_i and let the linear charge term be sum a_i*y_i. If a_i>0 and M_i>0, substituting u_i=mu_i*M_i*exp(gamma*y_i) gives integral exp(sum a_i*y_i-sum mu_i*M_i*exp(gamma*y_i))dy = gamma^(-r)*product[(mu_i*M_i)^(-a_i/gamma)*Gamma(a_i/gamma)]. A fixed root-coordinate determinant multiplies this expression when integrating in an orthonormal basis. Check: The Jacobian is gamma^(-r)*product du_i/u_i; the remaining integrals are independent Gamma integrals. This is an exact finite-dimensional integration conditional on the chaos masses, not an independence assertion about those masses. Obstruction: The remaining expectation is a joint negative moment of correlated GMC integrals carrying the three insertions. Their joint law does not factor because the root fields share the vector GFF. Existing semi-degenerate identities do not determine this general joint moment. No general structure-constant formula is obtained.

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] Let us consider $t\in \mathbb{R}^\times$. If we consider $\bm{a}_\ell$ and $\bm{b}_\ell$ with lengths $i_\ell$ and $j_\ell$ ($\ell=1,2,3$), respectively. Then 
\begin{align}
{}_{j_1} F_{i_1}\left(\begin{array}{c}
-t\bm{b}_1\\
-t \bm{a}_1
\end{array};\, x\right) 
{}_{j_2} F_{i_2}\left(\begin{array}{c}
-t\bm{b}_2\\
-t \bm{a}_2
\end{array};\, x\right)
=
{}_{j_3} F_{i_3}\left(\begin{array}{c}
-t\bm{b}_3\\
-t \bm{a}_3
\end{array};\, x\right)
\end{align}
if and only if
\begin{align}
\mathcal{H}^{(t)}\begin{bmatrix}
\bm{b}_1\\
\bm{a}_1
\end{bmatrix} (s_1z)
\boxplus^t
\mathcal{H}^{(t)}\begin{bmatrix}
\bm{b}_2\\
\bm{a}_2
\end{bmatrix} (s_2z)
=
\mathcal{H}^{(t)}\begin{bmatrix}
\bm{b}_3\\
\bm{a}_3
\end{bmatrix} (s_3z),
\end{align}
where $s_\ell = (-1)^{i_\ell+ j_\ell +1}$ for $\ell =1,2,3$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:E_cut_steps of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] Let \(E\) be a finite set of loops and let \(\mathbf{s}=\mathbf{s}(-\infty,\infty)\) be a two-sided path.
A step \((\mathbf{s}_{i-1},\mathbf{s}_i)\), \(i\in\mathbb{Z}\), is called an \textit{\(E\)-cut step} for \(\mathbf{s}\) if for every \(m_1< i\le m_2\), the step \((\mathbf{s}_{i-1},\mathbf{s}_i)\) is retained in the pruning
\[
\mathsf{Prune}\big(\mathbf{s}[m_1,m_2],E\big).
\]
Equivalently, writing $N_n := N_n\big(\mathbf{s}^{(m_1)}[0,m_2-m_1],E\big)$ for the translated path $\mathbf{s}^{(m_1)}_k := \mathbf{s}_{k+m_1}$, the condition is
\[
N_{i-m_1} - N_{i-m_1-1} = 1.
\]
title: $E$-cut steps

Let X be a {0,1}-valued field on Z^d, d>=2, such that sigma-fields on sets at sup-norm distance greater than integer r>=0 are independent. Suppose P(X_x=0)<=delta for every vertex. Put K=(r+1)^2. If delta<=64^(-K), then the good sites have an infinite nearest-neighbor component with positive probability; no stationarity or FKG assumption is needed.

Proof: restrict to the coordinate Z^2 plane. Color it by its two coordinates modulo r+1. Sites of any one color are mutually independent: successive use of the sigma-field range assumption is valid since every remaining site is farther than r from the previously selected set. Any specified set of m bad sites contains at least ceil(m/K) sites of one color, so its all-bad probability is at most delta^(m/K). No product over dependent sites is used.

If the origin is good but its good component in this plane is finite, its exterior vertex boundary contains a simple star-connected circuit of bad sites enclosing the origin. The elementary square-lattice contour fact follows by tracing the outer polygonal boundary of the union of unit squares of the finite component; successive exterior squares touch at sides or corners, and loops can be erased while preserving an enclosing circuit. For a circuit of m vertices, its intersection with the positive horizontal ray supplies a starting vertex (j,0), 1<=j<=m: enclosing the origin forces a crossing of that ray and of the opposite half-plane, and its diameter is at most m in the sup norm. For each of at most m starts there are at most 8^m star-step sequences. Thus the number of such circuits is at most m*8^m.

Set alpha=8*delta^(1/K)<=1/8. A union bound over the enclosing circuits gives

    P(origin belongs to an infinite good component)
      >= 1-delta-sum_{m>=1} m*alpha^m
      = 1-delta-alpha/(1-alpha)^2
      >= 1-1/64-8/49 = 2575/3136 > 0.

The sum includes impossible short circuits and is therefore a conservative bound. Delta=0 is immediate. An infinite component in the plane is also one in the full lattice. Let (M,g) be a complete connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n >= 2, and suppose there is a constant k > 0 such that Ric(v,v) >= (n-1) k g(v,v) for every tangent vector v (Ricci curvature bounded below by that of the round sphere of constant sectional curvature k). Then M is compact, diam(M) <= pi/sqrt(k), and the fundamental group of M is finite. The dimension condition is needed: for n = 1 the Ricci tensor vanishes and the hypothesis reads 0 >= 0, so the real line is complete, connected and not compact.

Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: A route through negative association would suffice: for N=L^d indicators with common mean rho and negative association, $\mathbb E e^{\theta S}\le(1-\rho+\rho e^\theta)^N$ for theta>0. Chernoff optimization at $e^\theta=\zeta(1-\rho)/(\rho(1-\zeta))$ yields $\mathbb P(S\ge\zeta N)\le e^{-N D(\zeta\Vert\rho)}$ for rho<zeta<1. Here D is Bernoulli relative entropy. At zeta=1 the bound is rho^N, obtained by a limit. Check: Differentiate the logarithm of the Chernoff bound to check the optimizer; strict convexity of Bernoulli entropy makes D positive for zeta>rho. The factorization uses association for products of increasing functions on disjoint coordinate sets, a stronger property than pairwise correlation signs. Obstruction: Negative association, or a comparably strong exponential-moment estimate, is unproved here for pi. A covariance table cannot justify this step.

[Lemma lem:SIG_facts_collect of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] The following hold on an event of probability one:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
        \item  [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] For $\xi_1 < \xi_2$ in $\mathfrak{X}$, $s < t$,  $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and $S \in \{L,R\}$,
        \[
        g_{(x,t)}^{\xi_1,S}(s) \le g_{(x,t)}^{\xi_2,S}(s).
        \]
        \item  [bhat-bus-soren]  \rm{(}see also [Busani_N3G]\rm{)} If $b$ is a finite eternal solution, then for each $(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and $S \in \{L,R\}$, $g_{(x,t)}^{b,S} = g_{(x,t)}^{\xi,S}$ for some $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$.
        \item  [bhat-bus-soren] If $b$ is a finite eternal solution, then for $x < y$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$, we have $g_{(x,t)}^{b,S}(s) \le g_{(y,t)}^{b,S}(s)$ for all $x < y$.
        \item [bhat-bus-soren] If $b$ is a finite eternal solution, then for all $s < t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$,
        \[
        \lim_{y \nearrow x} g_{(y,t)}^{b,L}(s) = g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}(s),\quad\text{and}\quad \lim_{y \searrow x} g_{(y,t)}^{b,R}(s) = g_{(x,t)}^{b,R}(s).
        \]
        \item [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] For all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $S \in \{L,R\}$,  
        \[
        \lim_{x \rightarrow \pm \infty} g_{(x,t)}^{\xi, S}(s)=\pm \infty.
        \]
        In particular, Items (it:some_g of the paper) and (it:g_b_mont of the paper) imply that  for every finite eternal solution $b$,
        \[
        \lim_{x \rightarrow \pm \infty} g_{(x,t)}^{b, S}(s)=\pm \infty.
        \]

[Definition 56 (Villain model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{Villain model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \begin{multline}
         e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)}
         =
         \Big(\prod_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\sigma_y)\Big)
            \Big(\prod_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\zeta_y)\Big);
            \\
         p_\beta(z,z'):=\sum_{m\in\Z} e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\big(\arg(z)-\arg(z')+2\pi m\big)^2}.
    \end{multline}
    Notice that the Hamiltonian is defined somewhat atypically and incorporates
    the dependency on $\beta$; more on this later.
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c^{\Villain}=\beta_c^{\Villain}(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c^{\Villain})$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\Villain, \beta}$.
    The label $\Villain$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.
title: Villain model

Under the even-N pairwise independent Rademacher law, S = sum_{i=1}^N epsilon_i has ||S||_p = N^(1 - 1/p) for every real p >= 2, while ||S||_2 = sqrt(N). So ||S||_p / ||S||_2 = N^(1/2 - 1/p): for p > 2 no upper Khintchine constant independent of N holds under pairwise independence alone.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] Let $G=(\mathfs{V},\mathfs{E})$ be a subgraph of $(\mathbb{Z}^d,\mathcal{E}(\mathbb{Z}^d))$ which is a forest. 
A graph $\mathfs{C}=(\mathfs{C}_V,\mathfs{C}_E) \subseteq \mathfs{V} \times \mathfs{E}$ is called a cluster in $G$, if it is a tree, and for any $w \in \mathfs{V} \setminus \mathfs{C}_V$ and $v \in \mathfs{C}_V$ with $\{ v,w \} \in \mathcal{E}(\mathbb{Z}^d)$, we have that $\{ v,w \} \notin \mathfs{E}$. In words, $\mathfs{C}$ is a maximal tree in the graph $G$.  We denote by $\partial \mathfs{C}$ the ${\mathbb{Z}}^d$-edge boundary of the vertices in $\mathfs{C}$.

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] A nonzero bounded linear functional $\rho$ on $\mathcal{B}$ is called \emph{a multiplicative functional} if $\rho(fg) = \rho(f)\rho(g)$ whenever $f, g$, and the product $fg$ are in $\mathcal{B}$.
    We say that \emph{$X$ is a maximal domain for $\mathcal{B}$} if for every multiplicative functional $\rho$ on $\mathcal{B}$, there exists $x\in X$ such that $\rho(f)=f(x)$ for all $f\in \mathcal{B}$.

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.25206, 'An extension of Stein's method incorporating dependence'] Let $M, Y$ be random variables on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$, with respective laws $\mu_M$ and $\mu_Y$, and with the dependence of $M$ on $Y$ given by the family $(\nu_y)_{\mathring{Y}(\Omega)}$ of probability laws, where
$\mathring{Y}(\Omega)$ is the essential range of $Y$, and where
\[
    \mu_M(A) = \int_\R \nu_y(A) \mu_Y(\mathrm{d}y), \quad (\forall A \in \mathcal{B}_\R).
\]
We assume given a Stein operator $\mathcal{N}_y$ for the law $\nu_y$ for
all $y \in \mathring{Y}(\Omega)$, as well as a suitable common class $\mathcal{C}$ of functions for the family of operators $(\mathcal{N}_y)_{y \in \mathring{Y}(\Omega)}$. Let $X$ be a given random variable.
With $d_{\textrm{TV}}$ denoting the total variation distance, and
$d_{\textrm{W}}$ the Wasserstein distance between laws, we have:
\begin{equation*} 
    d_{\textrm{TV}} (\mathbb{P}_{X,Y}, \mathbb{P}_{M,Y}) \leq
    \sup_{f \in \tilde{\mathcal{E}}_{TV}} \E{\mathcal{N}_Y \! f(X,Y)}
\end{equation*} 
and
\begin{equation*}
    d_{\textrm{W}} (\mathbb{P}_{X,Y}, \mathbb{P}_{M,Y}) \leq
    \sup_{f \in \tilde{\mathcal{E}}_{W}} \E{\mathcal{N}_Y \! f(X,Y)}.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.25206

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The gamma function is given at half-integers by
$$\Gamma(n)\simeq\left(\frac{n}{e}\right)^n\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{n}}
\quad,\quad\Gamma\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)\simeq\left(\frac{n}{e}\right)^n\sqrt{2\pi}$$
and we have the following uniform approximation formula for it,
$$\Gamma\left(\frac{N}{2}\right)\simeq\left(\frac{N}{2e}\right)^{N/2}\sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{N}}$$
valid for $N\in\mathbb N$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

[Lemma lem:joint-reflected-ricci-root of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let
\[
 \mathcal R^{\rm in}=W_+^{\rm in}\otimes W_-^{\rm out},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R^{\rm out}=W_+^{\rm out}\otimes W_-^{\rm in}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12a}$}
\]
be the physical doubled-reversal boundary.  Let
$B,B'\in\operatorname{Sym}_0(H)$ and
$|\alpha|,|\beta|,|\alpha'|,|\beta'|\le1$.  The complete distinct-time
aggregate-Ricci sources, with these statuses, and every finite or
unit-circle literal-$W$ Green kernel define an operator
\[
 \mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B'):
 \mathcal R^{\rm in}\longrightarrow\mathcal R^{\rm out}
\]
satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B')\|_\mathrm{op}
 \le \frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F,
 \qquad |z|=1,}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12b}$}
\]
with the same bound for every finite Green kernel.  At coincident
reflected root times the complete shared-plane source defines an operator
$\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},=}(B,B')$ obeying the same bound.  Consequently
every physically typed joint complement
\[
 K\in\mathcal S_1(\mathcal R^{\rm in},\mathcal R^{\rm out})
\]
obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 |\operatorname{Tr}(K^*\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B'))|
 \le\frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F\|K\|_1.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12c}$}
\]
At coincident times replace $\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}$ in this display
by $\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},=}$. 
The assertion is joint: no replica-projective factorization of $K$ is
assumed.  It remains true after tensoring the root operator by an
ancillary identity which lies outside the literal-$W$ Green rail.

[Cor bdd support II of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] Let $q>0$, $C_0>0$ be two  integers. 
Consider a  random vector $X$ in $\R^n$ and a discrete random variable $\mu$. Given $t$ such that $\mathbb{P}[\{\mu=t\}]>0$, let $Z_t$ be $X$ conditioned on $\{\mu=t\}$.
If $Z_t-\E[Z_t]\in \sum^q\mathcal{G}(\R^n)$ and  $\|\E[Z_t]\|\leq C_0$ for all $t$, then $X-\E[X]\in \sum^{q+10C_0}\mathcal{G}(\R^n)$.

body:
[Lemma 121 (Complexified momentum-fiber disintegration) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let
\[
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb R}
 :=\{F\in L^2([0,T]\times\R^3;\mathbb C):
 F(s,-\eta)=\overline{F(s,\eta)}\}
\]
with the real inner product from
\eqref{eq:hermitian-gaussian-hilbert-space}, and let
$\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}$ be its Hilbert-space complexification.  The map
from $\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}$ to the full complex space
$L^2([0,T]\times\R^3;\mathbb C)$ is unitary.  Consequently the changes of
variables
\[
 (\eta,\zeta)\mapsto(m=\eta+\zeta,\eta),
 \qquad
 (\eta,\zeta,r)\mapsto(\xi=\eta+\zeta+r,\eta,\zeta)
\]
induce the complex Hilbert direct-integral identifications
\begin{align}
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}\otimes_2\mathcal G_b^{\mathbb C}
 &\simeq\int_{\R^3}^{\oplus}
 L^2([0,T]^2\times\R^3_\eta)\dd m,
 \\
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}\otimes_2\mathcal G_b^{\mathbb C}
 \otimes_2\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}
 &\simeq\int_{\R^3}^{\oplus}
 L^2([0,T]^3\times\R^6_{\eta,\zeta})\dd\xi.
 
\end{align}
At finite cutoff, normalize the deterministic Wiener kernels so that the
first-Picard field and the linear field have measurable momentum fibers
$m\mapsto F_m^{\Lambda,\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}(t)$ and
$r\mapsto g_r^\Lambda(t)$.  With
\begin{equation}
 q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}^{[\epsilon_{\mathrm P}]}(t,m)
 :=|m_\Lambda(m)|^{2\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}
 q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}(t,m),
\end{equation}
their fiber norms satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|F_m^{\Lambda,\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}(t)\|^2
 =q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}^{[\epsilon_{\mathrm P}]}(t,m),
 \qquad
 \|g_r^\Lambda(t)\|^2
 =p_{a,\Lambda}(t,r)
\end{equation}
for almost every $m,r$.  Since the admissible multipliers are uniformly
bounded, the flagged density in
\eqref{eq:cubic-flagged-first-picard-density} is uniformly dominated by a
fixed multiple of the unflagged density.  Swapping the two color-$a$
slots preserves the total momentum $\xi$ and is unitary on every fiber of
\eqref{eq:three-noise-direct-integral}.  Hence
$\Sym_a=(I+\tau_{13})/2$ is a fiberwise orthogonal projection.

All these statements are made in the complexification of the same real
isonormal process.  The reality relation appears as conjugacy between the
$\xi$- and $-\xi$-fibers.

A proof for the critical variable-length boundary-to-boundary SAW law does not by itself prove convergence for the uniform n-step honeycomb walk rooted at the origin with a free endpoint. In a fixed finite path collection, conditioning fugacity weights x^L on L=n gives uniform n-step weights, but a shrinking conditioning probability can invalidate transfer from a weak mixture limit. A conditional local limit with relative error, as well as endpoint and domain transfer, is an additional premise. This campaign concept is a draft; it is not an SLE convergence proof.
P0003 exact source is Grimmett Question 2.2 (arXiv:2205.07318)
Related chordal source is Duminil-Copin--Smirnov Conjecture 1 (arXiv:1007.0575)

body: Publication record. Krauth and Mézard predicted in 1989 that the storage capacity of the Ising perceptron at zero margin is an explicit constant alpha* ≈ 0.8330786. With M_N the largest number of random patterns an N-dimensional Ising perceptron can store, Y. Shmalo, The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron: verification of the outstanding numerical conditions (arXiv:2607.11010, July 2026) gives a computer-assisted proof that M_N/N -> alpha* in probability, alpha* in [0.833078599, 0.833078600]: earlier work gave matching lower and upper bounds conditional on a one-variable global sign condition of Ding and Sun and a two-variable global sign condition of Huang, and the paper verifies both rigorously in Arb ball arithmetic. Nonzero margin and the general free-energy/TAP problem are not addressed. Certificates and verifiers: https://github.com/yspennstate/ising-perceptron-capacity (commit 072cdc2c624b); ResearchGate record 409127298. Not refereed. Item T069 of the owner's list of 200 famous open problems in probability.
title: Krauth-Mezard capacity conjecture for the Ising perceptron at zero margin proved by computer-assisted verification of the Ding-Sun and Huang conditions, alpha* in [0.833078599, 0.833078600] (Shmalo 2026, arXiv:2607.11010, repository yspennstate/ising-perceptron-capacity)

body:
[Lemma 6 (Sion's minimax theorem) of arXiv:2606.21137, 'A Sudakov--Fernique proof of Lehner-type edge bounds for matrix-valued GUE sums'] Let $X$ be a convex subset of a topological vector space,
	$Y$ be a convex subset of a topological vector space,
	and suppose either $X$ or $Y$ is compact.
	Suppose
	$f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$ is such that, for each $y\in Y$, the map
	$x\mapsto f(x,y)$ is upper semicontinuous and concave, and for each
	$x\in X$, the map $y\mapsto f(x,y)$ is lower semicontinuous and convex.
	Then
	\[
		\sup_{x\in X}\inf_{y\in Y} f(x,y)
		=
		\inf_{y\in Y}\sup_{x\in X} f(x,y).
	\]
title: Sion's minimax theorem

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When flipping a biased coin until reaching to $m$ heads,
$$P(s\ {\rm tails})=\binom{s+m-1}{s}(1-p)^sp^m$$
and so, $c_{mp}$ is the law of the number of failures, when playing this game.

body:
[Theorem thm:FS-no-exceptional of arXiv:2606.06612, 'The limit shape and emergence of the \\ Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $\beta>0$ large enough and consider $\phi\sim \pi^0_\Lambda$, the $(2+1)$\textsc{d}  \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace model on $\Lambda=\llbracket 1,L\rrbracket^2$ 
        with a floor and zero boundary conditions. Set $H(L)$ and $N_n$ per (eq:H-def,eq:Nn-def of the paper).
For fixed~$m$, let $\mathfrak{L}_n$ ($n=0,\ldots,m$) be the \texttt{large} $(H+1-n)$ level lines, where possibly $\mathfrak{L}_0$ does not exist.
Let $I_n = \llbracket \frac{L}2- N_n^{2/3},\frac{L}2+N_n^{2/3}\rrbracket$, let $\rho_n(x) := \min\{y\geq 0 \,:\; (\frac{L}2+x,y)\in\mathfrak{L}_n\}$ be the vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ from $I_n$, and 
$Y_n(t) := N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$.
Then there exists a constant $\sigma>0$  such that:
\begin{enumerate}[1.,leftmargin=2em]
\item The law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0$ converges weakly to the law of 
$m$ i.i.d.\ copies of the stationary Ferrari--Spohn diffusion $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$ on~$[-1,1]$.
\item For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})>L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=0}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})$ converges weakly to that of $m+1$ i.i.d.\ copies of 
$\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.
\item 
     For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist}) > L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid \mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist})$ converges weakly to that of $m$ i.i.d.\ copies of $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.
\end{enumerate}
The same statements hold for $\bar{Y}_n(t)$ corresponding to $\bar{\rho}_n(x)=\max\{y\leq \frac{L}2:(\frac{L}2+x,y)\in\mathfrak{L}_n\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:FS-no-exceptional of arXiv:2606.06612

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: In a finite killed domain V, let J(x) count departures from x during stabilization of n particles at 0, and let h be the final sleeper indicator. Conservation and the fresh uniform jump choice give $\mathbb E h(x)=n1_{x=0}+\Delta\mathbb E J(x)$, where $\Delta f(x)=(2d)^{-1}\sum_{y\sim x}f(y)-f(x)$ with zero extension outside V. This follows by stopping after K departures, taking expectations of arrivals, and then passing to the finite-domain absorption limit. It identifies the candidate continuum Poisson equation, but not its unknown density or free boundary. Check: The finite process has finite expected absorption time: from every reachable state there is a finite positive-probability sequence moving all particles to sinks, and the state space for fixed n,V is finite. Summing the identity over V gives final mass = initial mass minus expected boundary flux, independently checking the sign. Obstruction: A limit of the expected odometer is insufficient: concentration, a uniform bulk sleeper density, and inner/outer control of the visited region are all still required.

[Theorem lem:sufficient-energy of arXiv:2411.07680, 'Energy solutions of singular SPDEs on Hilbert spaces with applications to domains with bou'] We make Assumptions (A) and (B) and additionally assume that $S$ is a core for the operator $A$. Any adapted stochastic process $(u_t (f))_{t \geqslant 0,
  f \in  S}$ that satisfies all of the following conditions is an energy solution in the sense of Definition~(def:energy of the paper):
  \begin{enumerateroman}
    \item Path regularity: For all $f \in  S$ the process $t \mapsto u_t (f)$
    is continuous.
    
    \item Stationarity: $u_t \sim \mu$ for all $t \geqslant 0$.

    \item Weak solution: There exist $p<2$ and a sequence $(\rho_N)_{N \in \mathbb N}\subset L(H,V)$ such that for all $f \in S$ there is a process $\mathcal B^f$ with
    \begin{align*}
        \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty}\mathbb{P}\left( \left\|\mathcal B^f - \int_0^\cdot \langle {:} \tilde B^{\rho_N} (u_s, u_s) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V} \mathrm{d} s \right\|_{[0,T],p-\mathrm{var}}>\varepsilon\right) & = 0, \qquad \varepsilon, T>0,\\
        \lim_{N\to \infty} \left\| \langle {:} B (\eta, \eta) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V} - \langle {:} \tilde B^{\rho_N} (\eta, \eta) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V}\right\|_{\mathcal{H}^{-1}_0}& = 0.
    \end{align*}
    Moreover, the process
    \[ M^f_t := u_t (f) - u_0 (f) + \int_0^t u_s(Af)\mathrm{d} s - \mathcal B^f_t, \qquad t \geqslant 0, \]
    is a continuous martingale with quadratic variation $[M^f]_t =  2t \langle
    A f, f \rangle_H$.
    
    \item Behavior under time-reversal: for $T > 0$ the processes $\hat{u}_t (f)
    = u_{T - t} (f)$, and $\hat{\mathcal B}^f_t = (\mathcal B^f_T - \mathcal B^f_{T-t})$, $t \in [0, T]$, are such that
    \[
        \hat{M}^f_t := \hat{u}_t (f) - \hat{u}_0 (f) + \int_0^t \hat{u}_s(Af)\mathrm{d} s + \hat{\mathcal B}^f_t, \qquad t \in [0,T],
    \]
    is a continuous martingale in the filtration generated by $\hat{u}$, with quadratic variation $[\hat{M}^f]_t =  2 t \langle  A f, f \rangle_H$.
  \end{enumerateroman}
  If the sequence $(\rho_N)_{N\in \mathbb N}$ is as in Assumption~(B), then in point iii. it suffices to verify uniform convergence on compacts of $\int_0^\cdot \langle {:} \tilde B^{\rho_N} (u_s, u_s) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V} \mathrm{d} s$ to $\mathcal B^f$ and that $\mathcal B^f$ is of vanishing quadratic variation. It is not necessary to verify the convergence of  $\langle {:} \tilde B^{\rho_N} (\eta, \eta) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V}$ to $\langle {:} B (\eta, \eta) {:}, f \rangle_{V^{\ast}, V}$.

body:
[Theorem 11 (Averaged macroscopic-loop criterion) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(G_n\) be a random simple graph on \([n]\). Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).
Assume that \((G_n)_n\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:sparse-random-graph}, with limiting
edge density \(\alpha\), and that
\[
\alpha>c_{\theta,u}.
\]
Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Averaged macroscopic-loop criterion

body:
[Proposition 57 (Orthogonal block saturation) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \(H=\bigoplus_{j\geq1}E_j\), where
\(d_j:=\dim E_j\uparrow\infty\).  Let \(W^Q\) be a \(Q\)-Wiener process
with
\[
 Q=\bigoplus_{j\geq1}q_jI_{E_j},
 \qquad q_j>0,\qquad\sum_jq_jd_j<\infty.
\]
If \(A\) is its area on \([0,1]\), then the compressions are independent
and
\begin{equation}
 P_{E_j}AP_{E_j}\stackrel{\mathrm d}=q_j\mathcal L^{(d_j)}.
 
\end{equation}
This distributional statement holds for every choice of the blocks and
weights above.

Conversely, given any prescribed \(m_j\uparrow\infty\), the even
dimensions \(d_j\) can be chosen recursively so that the failure
probabilities in \eqref{cc:eq-critical-Brownian-bulk} and
\eqref{cc:eq-critical-Brownian-edge} are summable.  For that choice of
dimensions, and for any positive weights satisfying
\(\sum_jq_jd_j<\infty\), the resulting almost-sure event has, eventually,
\begin{align}
 s_n(A)&\geq aq_j,\qquad
 1\leq n\leq\lfloor\eta d_j\rfloor,
 \\
 s_k(P_{E_j}AP_{E_j})&\geq c_0q_jd_j/k,\qquad1\leq k\leq m_j.
 
\end{align}

body:
[Lem 2 of arXiv:2506.12443, 'Error Rates for Large Deviations in the domain of an $\alpha=1$ stable law'] Let $(Z_n)_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of random variables and $Y$ another random variable, defined on the same probability space but independent of all the $Z_n$.
    Assume that there exist three sequences $N=N(n)$, $z_N=z_{N(n)}$ and $y_N=y_{N(n)}$ such that, as $n\to\infty$, it holds that $N\to\infty$, $z_N\to\infty$ with $z_N=o(N)$, $y_N\to 0$ and
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[\em(a)] $y_N=o\left(\P(Z_n > N)\right)$ and $\P(Z_n > N \pm z_N) = \P(Z_n > N)+ O(y_N)$.
        \item[\em(b)]$\P(|Y| > z_N) = O(y_N)$.
    \end{itemize}
    
    Then $\P(Z_n+Y> N) = \P(Z_n > N)+ O(y_N)$ as $n \to \infty$.
title: Lem 2 of arXiv:2506.12443

[Proposition prop:Kn of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] The sequence of number of customers served in each stage  $\{K_n\}$ is a 
discrete time Markov chain with state space $\mathbb{Z}^+=\{1,2,\ldots\}$ and 
transition probability matrix given by 
\[
\mathbb{P}(K_{n+1}=m\mid K_n=k)=\left\{
\begin{array}{lll}
 \int_0^\infty \frac{1}{m!}(\lambda x)^m e^{-\lambda x}kG^{k-1}(x)dG(x), 
&& \mbox{for } m=2,3,\ldots,\\  && \\
\int_0^\infty (\lambda x +1) e^{-\lambda x}kG^{k-1}(x)dG(x)  && \mbox{for }m=1.
\end{array} \right.
\]

[Lemma lem:cascading of arXiv:2607.22908, 'Epidemic Phase Transitions in the Zero-Range Process'] For any $k \geq 0$,
  \begin{equation}
    H(B_{k+1}) \subset \bigcup_{j = 0}^{2} \bigcup_{(B, B') \in \mathcal{B}_j \times
    \mathcal{B}_j'} H(B) \cap H(B').
  \end{equation}
  In words, whenever $H(B_{k+1})$ occurs, there exists a pair of scale-$k$ boxes $B,B'$ that are separated vertically
  by at least $\ell_{k+1}/4$ or horizontally by at least $w_{k+1}/2$ such that $H(B)$ and $H(B')$ occur.
  The total number of candidate pairs of boxes $B$, $B'$ is at most
  \begin{equation}
    C_{\textnormal{\tiny (C:entropy of the paper)}} = 3(2\alpha + 3)^2.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cascading half-crossings

body:
[Defi Def:Bary-Subdiv-Weighted of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] \ \vskip 0.1cm
 For a weighted simplicial complex $(K,\mu)$, define the weight of the barycenter $b_{\sigma}$ of any simplex $\sigma$ in $K$ to be $\mu(\sigma)$. Then define a weight  $Sd(\mu)$ on $Sd(K)$ by:
    \begin{equation} 
     Sd(\mu)\big([ b_{\sigma_0},\cdots, b_{\sigma_l}]\big)=\mu(\sigma_l),\ \sigma_0\subsetneq \cdots\subsetneq \sigma_l \in K.
     \end{equation}
   
   Note that we have either
   $\mu(\sigma_0)\, | \, \cdots \, | \,\mu(\sigma_l)$ or 
    $\mu(\sigma_l) \, |\, \cdots\, |\, \mu(\sigma_0)$ depending on whether $\mu$ is ascending or descending. Then it is easy to 
    check that $Sd(\mu)$ is a divisible weight on $Sd(K)$ which is ascending (or descending) if so is $\mu$.  
     We call $(Sd(K),Sd(\mu))$ the \emph{barycentric subdivision} of $(K,\mu)$. For any integer $m\geqslant 1$, let $(Sd^m(K),Sd^m(\mu))$ 
 denote the $m$ iterated barycentric subdivisions of $(K,\mu)$.
title: Barycentric Subdivision of Weighted Simplicial Complex

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Geometric Jensen-Shannon divergence between equivalent Gaussian measures}]
		
		Let $\mu_i = \Ncal(m_i, C_i) \in \Gauss(\Hcal, \mu_{*})$, $i=0,1$, with $C_i= C_{*}^{1/2}(I-S_i)C_{*}^{1/2}$, $S_i \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{< I}$. Let $m_{\alpha} \in \Hcal, S_{\alpha} \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{<I}, C_{\alpha} \in \Sym^{+}(\Hcal) \cap \Tr(\Hcal)$ be as in Theorem \ref{theorem:geometric-interpolation-equivalent-Gaussian-Hilbert-space}. Then
		\begin{align}
			&\JS_{G_{\alpha}}(\mu_0||\mu_1) = (1-\alpha)\KL(\mu_0||\mu_{\alpha}) + \alpha \KL(\mu_1||\mu_{\alpha})
			\\
			& = \frac{(1-\alpha)}{2}||C_{\alpha}^{-1/2}(m_0- m_{\alpha})||^2 - \frac{1-\alpha}{2}\log\dettwo[(I -S_{\alpha})^{-1}
			(I-S_0)]
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad +\frac{\alpha}{2}||C_{\alpha}^{-1/2}(m_1- m_{\alpha})||^2 -\frac{\alpha}{2}\log\dettwo[(I -S_{\alpha})^{-1}
			(I-S_1)].
		\end{align}
		In particular, for $S_0, S_1 \in \SymTr(\Hcal)_{< I}$,
		\begin{align}
			\JS_{G_{\alpha}}(\mu_0||\mu_1) &=\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2}||C_{\alpha}^{-1/2}(m_0- m_{\alpha})||^2 +\frac{\alpha}{2}||C_{\alpha}^{-1/2}(m_1- m_{\alpha})||^2
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad - \frac{1}{2}\log\frac{\det(I-S_0)^{1-\alpha}\det(I-S_1)^{\alpha}}{\det(I-S_{\alpha})}
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad  +\frac{1}{2}\trace[(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1}(S_{\alpha}-(1-\alpha)S_0- \alpha S_1)].
			
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2506.10494

Own-work draft; F0124_C16 version 3; status: independently checked proof. For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with p in [37/39,1] and independent iid fair sign scenery, every exterior configuration is good. At theta=(1-p)/p=2/37 the constant-word WHOLE no-cut coefficients h_l have an exponentially decaying bound h_l<=C(1001/1000)^(-l) for some finite C. Confined-path resolvents give the full path partitions E,J,Q; exact renewal yields H=Q-1-(J-1)^2/E. Its ballistic pole cancels. Writing lambda=(1+sqrt(1-16theta z^2))/2 and r=(1-lambda)/lambda gives uniformly convergent meromorphic series. Along 0<=z<=1001/1000, lambda>=682/1000 and r<=318/682; the regular series is bounded by six exact rational terms plus an analytic bound on its ENTIRE infinite tail, giving a strictly positive denominator G. H continues analytically along that interval. Its coefficients are nonnegative, so the proved Vivanti-Pringsheim argument gives a Taylor radius greater than 1001/1000 and summability. Monotonicity of raw coefficients in theta extends the result to all p>=37/39; p=1 is iid. Real-axis analyticity alone would be insufficient without nonnegative coefficients. This is a restricted high-drift result, not the full p>4/5 classification, and no novelty is asserted.

body: Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). From a symmetric start (Q = q0 I, R = 0) the ODE enters the symmetric plateau, where all students have equal overlap with every teacher; the plateau is a saddle whose one unstable direction is the antisymmetric mode, with rate lambda(eta) > 0. Open (top-400 row T240): for K = 2, prove that the plateau exit time tau_N of SGD at dimension N satisfies tau_N / log N -> 1/(2 lambda(eta)) in probability, for small eta or an explicit eta interval. This requires deterministic entry into the plateau, positive transverse noise there, and recovery after the exit.
title: Open problem: escape time from the symmetric plateau of a teacher-student soft committee machine

body:
[Theorem eq:counter-match of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:counterexample}
Fix \(p\ge3\) and \(\sigma>1\).  There exists a symmetric probability law \(\mu=\mu_{p,\sigma}\) on \(\mathbb R\) with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item \(\mu\) has a strictly positive \(C^\infty\) density and is sub-Gaussian.
\item If \(\xi\sim\mu\) and \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\xi^r=\mathbb E G^r,
 \qquad r=1,\ldots,2p.
\end{equation}
\item There is a compact interval \(B\subset(0,\infty)\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 >\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\end{equation}
Moreover, the same interval satisfies
\begin{align}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^J(B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^G(B),
 \\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\min}^J(-B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\min}^G(-B).
 
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
In particular, sub-Gaussianity together with Gaussian moment matching
through order \(2p\) does not force the Gaussian rate of unregularized
critical-point counts in a compact energy window when no spatial
localization restriction is imposed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Smooth sub-Gaussian moment-matching counterexample
