[Lem 62 of arXiv:2608.28200, '\textbf On the Formality of Configuration Spaces of $\aka$'] Let $\mathcal T_n$ be the set of maximal trees on the vertex set $\setn$; that is, each $T \in \mathcal T_n$ is an unoriented graph with $n-1$ edges and no cycles. Let $e$ be an edge with vertices $\lr{i,j}$, $i<j$. Denote $\omega^e=\omega^{\lr{i,j}}=\mu_i\bp\mu_j-\mu_j\bp\mu_i$. Then 
$$
\omega^{\setn}
= \sum_{i=1}^n (-1)^{i-1}\mu_i \bp\mu_1\cdots \widehat{\bp\mu_i}\cdots \bp\mu_n 
=\sum_{T\in \mathcal T_n} \sT \prod_{i=1}^n (z^i)^{d^T_i-1} \bigwedge_{e\in T} \omega^{e} 
$$
where $d^T_i$ is the degree of the vertex $i$ in the tree $T$, the wedge product is taken in lexicographical order of the pairs $(i,j)$, and $\sT\in \lr{\pm1}$ is a sign.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted calculation or proof-obstruction analysis after primary-source comparison Result: A commute-time identity controls the sum of opposite hitting times, not a lower bound of comparable size for each direction. A unit-conductance star with n vertices gives a concrete check: from a leaf a to its center b the hitting time is1, while the reverse mean is2*n-3; their sum is2*n-2=2*|E|*R(a,b). Thus a large commute time cannot be assigned to the outward hitting time. Even a genuine large expectation need not give a lower-tail bound: a nonnegative variable equal to n^2 with probability1/n and zero otherwise has mean n but is zero with probability tending to one. A displacement upper bound therefore needs a genuine lower-tail control on exit times or a suitable heat-kernel estimate, beyond these expectation identities. Check: First-step conditioning at the star center gives m=(1/(n-1))*1+((n-2)/(n-1))*(2+m), hence m=2*n-3. The one-way/commute discrepancy is exact. Obstruction: No claim that exit-time concentration fails in the DGFF model. The examples invalidate proposed proof implications, not the requested estimate.

body: [Proposition prop_7 of arXiv:2412.03774, '{ Refining Concentration for \\Gaussian Quadratic Chaos with\\ Applications in Sonar and C'] If $n=2,4,6$, then the weak $\chi^2$-bound is sharper than the $m_\infty$-bound regardless of the positive-definite matrix~$A$~and~$t$. body:
[Cor daffodil of arXiv:2411.07609, 'Activated Random Walks on $\bZ$ with Critical Particle Density'] Let $n$ be an integer, and let $I = \llbracket a, a + n - 1 \rrbracket$ be an interval in $\mathbb{Z}$ for some integer $a$. Consider activated random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ with sleep rate $\lambda > 0$. Let $\sigma$ be an initial configuration with at least one active particle on $I$. 

For any subinterval $I_{b,\gamma}=[ b,b+\lfloor n\gamma\rfloor-1]\subseteq I$ for some integer $b$, let $Y_{I_{b,\gamma}}(u_0)$ be the maximum number of sleeping particles remaining in $I_{b,\gamma}$ after applying a stable odometer $U$ on $I_{b,\gamma}$ with 
$U(b)=u_0$ and $U(x)>0$ for any site $x \in I_{b,\gamma}$ with a particle in $\sigma$. Then, for any 
$\rho > \rho_*(\lambda)$,

$$\mathbb P_\sigma[Y_{I_{b,\gamma}}(u_0)\geq \rho \lfloor n\gamma\rfloor-1]\leq Ce^{-cn}$$
where $C$ and $c$ are positive constants depending only on $\lambda$ and $\rho$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor daffodil of arXiv:2411.07609

body:
[Theorem thm:abstract-radial of arXiv:2608.18293, 'Critical tensor covariance at the Marchenko--Pastur threshold'] Let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$ and $p_n\to\infty$. For each $n$, let
$x_n^{(1)},\ldots,x_n^{(N_n)}$ be independent copies of a random vector
$x_n\in\mathbb F^{p_n}$, set
\[
 R_n=\frac{\|x_n\|^2}{p_n},
 \qquad
 T_n=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{\alpha=1}^{N_n}
 x_n^{(\alpha)}{x_n^{(\alpha)}}^*,
\]
where $*$ denotes transpose or conjugate transpose according to the field,
and suppose $p_n/N_n\to c\in(0,\infty)$. Assume that $R_n\Rightarrow\nu$,
that $\{R_n\}$ is uniformly integrable, and that for some $\varepsilon_n\to0$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{A\in\mathbb{C}^{p_n\times p_n}\\\|A\|_\mathrm{op}\le1}}
 \mathbb{E}\left|p_n^{-1}x_n^*Ax_n
 -R_np_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr} A\right|^2\le\varepsilon_n.
 
\end{equation}
Then $\operatorname{ESD}(T_n)$ converges weakly in probability to the unique probability
measure $\mu_{c,\nu}$ whose Stieltjes transform satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{m(z)}+z=\int_0^\infty\frac{r}{1+crm(z)}\,\nu(\,\mathrm{d} r).
 
\end{equation}
If $\sum_n e^{-ap_n}<\infty$ for every $a>0$, the convergence is almost sure.
No independence between $R_n$ and $x_n/\|x_n\|$ is assumed, and no
mean-one normalization of $\nu$ is needed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Endogenous radial covariance principle

body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be iid real random variables with finite logarithmic moment generating function Lambda(t) = log E[exp(t X_1)] for every real t, and let S_n = (X_1+...+X_n)/n. Let Lambda*(x) = sup_t (t x - Lambda(t)) be its Legendre-Fenchel transform. Cramer's theorem states that S_n obeys a large deviation principle with rate function Lambda*: for every Borel set A, -inf_{interior of A} Lambda* <= liminf_n (1/n) log P(S_n in A) <= limsup_n (1/n) log P(S_n in A) <= -inf_{closure of A} Lambda*. In particular P(S_n in F) decays like exp(-n inf_F Lambda*) for closed F. Due to Harald Cramer.
title: Cramer's theorem (large deviations)

body:
[Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Let
		\[
		S(t,\tau):\mathcal P_{4,z}(H)\longrightarrow
		\mathcal P_{4,z}(H),\qquad t\geq\tau,
		\]
		be a measure evolution process satisfying
		\[
		S(\tau,\tau)=I,\qquad
		S(t,s)S(s,\tau)=S(t,\tau),
		\quad t\geq s\geq\tau.
		\]
		A family
		$\mathscr A=\{\mathscr A(\tau):\tau\in\mathbb R\}
		\in\mathfrak D$
		is called a $\mathfrak D$-pullback measure attractor for $S$ if:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(1)] for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, the set
			$\mathscr A(\tau)$ is nonempty and compact in
			$(\mathcal P(H),d_{\mathcal P(H)})$;
			
			\item[(2)] $\mathscr A$ is invariant, namely,
			\[
			S(t,\tau)\mathscr A(\tau)=\mathscr A(t),
			\qquad t\geq\tau;
			\]
			
			\item[(3)] $\mathscr A$ pullback attracts every $D\in\mathfrak D$,
			that is, for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$,
			\[
			\lim_{r\to\infty}
			\operatorname{dist}_{w,H}
			\bigl(
			S(\tau,\tau-r)D(\tau-r),
			\mathscr A(\tau)
			\bigr)=0.
			\]
		\end{enumerate}
		Here compactness and attraction are understood in the weak topology
		of probability measures on $H$, while membership in $\mathfrak D$
		retains the fourth-order and vertical-derivative moments required
		to restart the equation.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03750

[Prop 15 (Two-replica variational problem) of arXiv:2608.18276, 'The branching random walk in a uniform magnetic field : magnetization concentration and ov'] Fix $h>0$, $\beta>\beta_c(h)>0$, recall $m^*=m^*(h)=\tanh(\beta_c h)$ and the definition of the free energy $f(\beta,h)$ from Theorem \ref{thm:theoremB}.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] We have
\[
\max_{{\bf q} \in\mathcal P}\Xi_{\beta,h}({\bf q})=2f(\beta,h),
\]
where the $\max$ is attained at a unique 
${\bf q}^* = {\bf q}^*(h) \in \mathcal P$ with
\[
q^*_{ab}=\left(\frac{1+am^*}{2}\right) \left(\frac{1+bm^*}{2}\right), \qquad \forall \, a,b \in \{-1,1\}.
\]
In particular $\rho({\bf q}^*)=(m^*)^2$.

\item[(ii)] For every $\eta\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}
 
c_2=c_2(\beta,h,\eta):=2f(\beta,h)-\max\left\{\Xi_{\beta,h}({\bf q}):\ {\bf q}\in\mathcal P,\
|\rho({\bf q})-(m^*)^2|\ge\eta\right\}>0.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.22514, 'Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions\\ along vector fields'] Suppose that assumptions
$\mathbf{A}_V$,
$\mathbf{A}_\tau$,
$\mathbf{A}_{V,\mu}$ and
$\mathbf{A}_\varkappa$ hold. Then, for any initial values $y\in\bR^d$ and $\iota\in \{1,\dots,p\}$,
the gliding evolutions $\{Y^{\e,\delta}\}$ converge weakly in $C(\bR_+,\bR^d)$
to a diffusion $Y$ starting at $y$ with the generator
\ba

Bf
&=\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \sum_{i}  \sigma_{i}^2  \langle \nabla^2 f V_i ,V_i\rangle
+ \frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu}\sum_{i} \lambda_{i}^2 \langle \nabla f, DV_i[V_i]\rangle
+\frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu}\sum_{j<i} \mu_i\mu_j \langle \nabla f, DV_i[V_j] \rangle
,\quad f\in C^3_b(\bR^d,\bR).
\ea
The diffusion $Y$ is a solution to an It\^o-SDE
\ba

\di Y_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(Y_t)\,\di W^i_t +
\frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu} \Big(
\frac12\sum_{i} \lambda_{i}^2 DV_i[V_i](Y_t)
+\sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  D V_i [ V_j](Y_t)
\Big)\,\di t,
\ea
where $W^1,\dots,W^p$ are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions.
The SDE \eqref{e:SDEY} can be rewritten in the Stratonovich form
as
\ba

\di Y_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(Y_t)\circ\di W^i_t
+\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  [ V_i,V_j](Y_t)\,\di t.
\ea (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces and let T from X to Y be a linear map (defined on all of X). If the graph of T, the set of pairs (x, T(x)), is closed in the product space X x Y (equivalently: whenever x_n converges to x in X and T(x_n) converges to some y in Y, it follows that y = T(x)), then T is bounded (continuous). The converse is immediate, so for everywhere-defined linear maps between Banach spaces, closed graph and continuity coincide. The hypothesis that T is defined on all of X and both spaces are complete is essential (densely defined closed unbounded operators exist).
X and Y are Banach spaces
T : X -> Y is linear and defined on all of X
the graph of T is closed in X x Y

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2606.20908, 'On It\^o-Stratonovich formula for rough sheets'] Let $\ga_1,\ga_2>1$, and recall that the spaces $\cb_j\cp$ are defined for $j=1,2$ in Notation~\ref{not:BP-ZP}. Then:

\smallskip

\noindent\emph{(1)}
There exist two maps $\laa_1:\cb_1\cp_{3,3}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}\to\cp_{2,3}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}$ and $\laa_2:\cb_2\cp_{3,3}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}\to\cp_{3,2}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}$ such that $\der_j\laa_j=\id$. These maps satisfy the bound $\|\laa_j(h)\|_{\ga_1,\ga_2} \le c_{\ga_j} \|h\|_{\ga_1,\ga_2}$ for $j=1,2$.

\smallskip

\noindent\emph{(2)}
There exists a map $\laa:\cb\cp_{3,3}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}\to\cp_{2,2}^{\ga_1,\ga_2}$ such that $\der\laa=\id$. This map satisfies the bound $\|\laa(h)\|_{\ga_1,\ga_2} \le c_{\ga_1,\ga_2} \|h\|_{\ga_1,\ga_2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:conformal-restriction of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $K \subset \overline\BH$ be a compact subset with finitely many connected components, each of which meets $\partial \BH$, such that $\BH \setminus K$ has a unique unbounded connected component $H_K$, and let $u \neq v$ be two points of $\partial\BH \setminus K$ lying on $\partial H_K$. Fix a conformal mapping $\phi$ from $H_K$ onto $\BH$. Let $\eta$ be a chordal SLE$_4$ curve in $\BH$ from $u$ to $v$. Then, the law of $\phi(\eta)$ conditionally on the event that $\eta \cap K = \emptyset$ is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the law of a chordal SLE$_4$ curve in $\BH$ from $\phi(u)$ to $\phi(v)$.

[Definition 1 (BESQ flow; {\cite[Definition 3.3) of arXiv:2512.05466, 'Stochastic Flows and Marked Stable Processes'] {aidekon2023stochastic}, \cite[Definition 2.2]{AWYskew}}]

Let $\delta \in \bR$ and ${\mathcal W}$ be a white noise on $\bR_+\times \bR$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by ${\mathcal W}$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in \bR,a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in \bR_+\times \bR$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the unique strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \dd s) + 
\delta (x-r),\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
where, if $\delta\le 0$, the process is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in \bR$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\cS_{r,y}(a)=\cS_{x,y}\circ \cS_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\cW$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\cS_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\cS_{r,x}(a)=0\}$. 

We call general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  a  ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow or a  killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow.

[Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\underline T$ be a $p$-adic fine log
      	PD-base, and let
      	$u\colon\underline P_0\to\underline Q_0$ be a morphism of affine fine
      	pre-log algebras over  the special fibre $\underline T_0$ of $\underline T$.
        Let $\underline P$ and
      	$\underline Q$ be affine log-smooth liftings
        of $\underline P_0$ and $\underline Q_0$
        over $\underline T$ respectively,
        and let
      	\[
      	\widetilde u_1,\widetilde u_2\colon
      	\underline P\longrightarrow\underline Q
      	\]
      	be two liftings of $u$ over $\underline T$. Then
      	\[
      	\widehat\omega^*(\widetilde u_1)
      	\simeq
      	\widehat\omega^*(\widetilde u_2)
      	\quad\text{in }\mathcal D(T)^\wedge_p.
      	\]
      	More precisely, if $c_{\underline P}$ and $c_{\underline Q}$ denote Kato's
      	comparison equivalences \eqref{eq;omegalogcryscomparison}, 
        then, 
      	\begin{equation}
      		\widehat\omega^*(\widetilde u_i)\circ c_{\underline P}
      		\simeq
      		c_{\underline Q}\circ u^*\quad\text{ for }
           i=1,2.
      	\end{equation}
      	These identifications are compatible with composition.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] Let $\{ \varepsilon_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables. 
	Suppose there exists a stochastic process $\{ \mathbf{X}_n \}$ taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $d \ge 1$, which governs the distribution of inter-arrival times $\{ \tau_n \}$.
	Let \(\Phi(t,\mathbf{x})\) be a function defined for \(t \ge 0\) and \(\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d\), and assume that \(\Phi(\cdot,\mathbf{x})\) is strictly increasing in \(t\) for each fixed \(\mathbf{x}\).
	The inter-arrival time \(\tau_n\) is related to \(\varepsilon_n\) by
	\begin{equation}
		\varepsilon_n = \Phi(\tau_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) 
		\qquad \text{equivalently,} \qquad
		\tau_n = \Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) ,
		
	\end{equation}
	where the inverse is taken with respect to $t$, holding $\mathbf{x}$ fixed.
	The process $\mathbf{X}_n$ evolves according to an update function $\Psi$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{X}_n = \Psi(\mathbf{X}_{n-1}, \tau_n). 
	\end{equation}
	The associated point process \(N\) on \(\mathbb{R}^+\) is defined by
	\[
	N = \sum_{n \in \mathbb N} \delta_{T_n}, 
	\qquad  \qquad 
	T_n = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i
	\]
	where \(\delta_t\) denotes the Dirac measure at \(t\).

[Definition 1 (hub-cores) of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Given $p \ll 1$, we say a graph $G \subseteq K_n$ with no isolated vertices is a hub-core if it contains a vertex cover of size at most 
 \[
    \min\left\{e_G / \omega, \bigl(\log\log(1/p)\bigr)^{3} \cdot \max\bigl\{1, (e_G/f)^{v_H}\bigr\} \cdot \max\{1, e_G/n\}\right\}.
  \]
If $p  \leq n^{-1/\Delta} \cdot (\log n)^{-\omega}$, we also require that the minimum degree of $G$ satisfies $\delta(G) \geq d_H$.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] In Notation \ref{n.basis}, let $x_a, y_a, t$ be the regular functions on $\sH$ determined by $$\log h \ = \ \sum_{a=1}^m (x_a(h) X_a + y_a(h) Y_a) + t(h) T 
$$ for all $h \in \sH$, defining a global coordinate system $(x_1, \ldots, x_m, y_1, \ldots, y_m, t)$  on $\sH$. Then the following holds.  \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] The group multiplication is expressed as \begin{eqnarray*} \lefteqn{(x_1, \ldots, x_m, y_1, \ldots, y_m, t) \cdot (z_1, \ldots, z_m, w_1, \ldots, w_m, s) =} \\ & & (x_1 + z_1, \ldots, x_m + z_m, y_1 + w_1, \ldots, y_m + w_m, t + s + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{a=1}^m (x_a w_a - y_a z_a)). \end{eqnarray*}
\item[(ii)] The elements  $X_a, Y_a, T \in \fh$ regarded as left-invariant vector fields on $\sH$ are expressed as
    $$X_a = \frac{\p}{\p x_a} - \frac{1}{2} y_a \frac{\p}{\p t}, \ Y_a = \frac{\p}{\p y_a} + \frac{1}{2} x_a \frac{\p}{\p t}, \ T = \frac{\p}{\p t}.$$
\item[(iii)] The space of  right-invariant vector fields   on $\sH$ are spanned by 
    $$\sX_a := \frac{\p}{\p x_a} + \frac{1}{2} y_a \frac{\p}{\p t}, \ \sY_a := \frac{\p}{\p y_a} - \frac{1}{2} x_a \frac{\p}{\p t}, \ T = \frac{\p}{\p t}.$$
\item[(iv)] The natural left-invariant contact structure $H \subset T\sH$ on $\sH$ determined by $\fh_1$ is given by the left-invariant 1-form $$ \theta = \sum_{a=1}^m(x_a {\rm d} y_a - y_a {\rm d} x_a) \ - \ 2 {\rm d} t.$$
    
    \end{itemize}

body: [Cor complete-k0 of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $C$ have genus $g\ge 2$ and let $n\in\Lev(C)$ be realised by a cyclic cover $\pi$ with a separable model $y^n=h(x)$ defined over $k_0$. Then (alg:main of the paper), run over $k_0$, outputs $n$; for $\deg h\ge 3$ the candidate arising from the branch divisor of $\pi$ yields a normal form of $\pi$, and for $\deg h=2$ step 5 yields one. The constant field is extended at most once, by degree at most $\deg h$, and only when $3\le\deg h$, no root of $h$ is $k_0$-rational, and either $\deg h$ divides $n$ or $\deg h=n+\gcd(n,\deg h)$ with $\gcd(n,\deg h)>1$.

[Defn conditions of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a closed interval and $C>0$ be a constant. We
    define $\mathcal{G}_{I,C}$ to be the set of finite weighted graphs
    $G=(\text{\boldmath $A$},\text{\boldmath $h$})$ satisfying the following conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(SW), ref=(SW)]
        \item
        All eigenvalues of $\text{\boldmath $A$}$ lie in $I$. If additionally the
        length of $I$ is strictly less than $1$, we refer to this as
        the \emph{spectral width condition}.
    \end{enumerate}
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(SG), ref=(SG)]
        \item
        The operator norm bound $\|\text{\boldmath $A$}\|_{\infty\rightarrow\infty}\le
        C$ holds, i.e. the $\ell^1$ norm of any row of $\text{\boldmath $A$}$ is at
        most $C$. We refer to this as the \emph{sparse graph
        condition}.
    \end{enumerate}
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(BF), ref=(BF)]
        \item
        The entrywise bound $\|\text{\boldmath $h$}\|_\infty\le C$ holds, i.e. the
        magnitude of the external field $h_i$ on each spin $i\in[N]$
        is at most $C$. We refer to this as the \emph{bounded field
        condition}.
    \end{enumerate}

Let $f_n,f:S\to\mathbb{R}$ be functions. Assume that
$f_n\to f$ locally uniformly on $S$, i.e.\ for every compact $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_n\to f$ uniformly on $S\cap K$. Assume further that there exists a function $g:S\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
$f_n(x)\le g(x)$ for all $x\in S$ and all $n$ and 
$g(x)\to -\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$ within $S$.
Then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in S} f_n(x)=\sup_{x\in S} f(x).
\]

[Proposition prop:5.5 of arXiv:2607.06785, 'On the smallest singular value of the product of random and deterministic matrices'] Fix \(C_0>0\). There exists \(K_{{\color{blue}5.5}}>0\), depending only on \(C_0\), such that for every \(n\geqslant2\) and every \(1\leqslant r\leqslant n-1\), there is an invertible diagonal matrix \(M\) satisfying
\[
  r\leqslant \sr(M^{-1})\leqslant 2r
\]
and
\[
  \mathbb{P}\!\left(s_{\min}(MA)> \frac{C_0}{\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}}\right)
  \geqslant e^{-K_{{\color{blue}5.5}}r}.
\]

[Definition dppdef of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] \rm
    Let $1 \leq p, q \leq \infty$ be given. \\
    {\rm (i)} A Banach space $Y$ is said to have the {\bf sequential (p,q)-Dunford-Pettis property} ($\mathrm{sDPP}_{(p,q)}$, for short) if $y_n^*(y_n) \to 0$ for every $(y_n)_n \in \ell_p^w(Y)$ and every $(y_n^*)_n \in \ell_q^w( Y^*)$. For $p = \infty$ (or $q = \infty$), we replace $\ell_p$ (or $\ell_q$) by $c_0$ (see [gab2024]). \\
    {\rm (ii)} A Banach space $Y$ is said to have the {\bf Dunford-Pettis* property of order $p$} ($\mathrm{DP}^*\mathrm{P}_p$, for short) if  $y_n^*(y_n) \to 0$ for every $(y_n)_n \in \ell_p^w(Y)$ and every $(y_n^*)_n \in c_0^{w^*}(Y^*)$. For $p=\infty$, we replace $\ell_p$ by $c_0$ (see [zeefou14]).
title: Definition dppdef of arXiv:2609.03988

[Lemma lem:OU-mean of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Assume that $B_{11}$ and $C:=B_{22}-B_{21}B_{11}^{-1}B_{12}$ are Hurwitz.
Fix $t>0$ and let $m_s^\varepsilon(z)=e^{-(I^\varepsilon B)s}z=(x_s^\varepsilon(z),y_s^\varepsilon(z))$ be the mean of $Z_s^\varepsilon$
given $Z_0^\varepsilon=z=(x,y)$. Define
\[
w_s^\varepsilon(z):=x_s^\varepsilon(z)+B_{11}^{-1}B_{12}y_s^\varepsilon(z),\qquad s\in[0,t].
\]
Then for every compact $K\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ there exists a constant $C_{t,K}<\infty$ such that, for all
$\varepsilon\in(0,1]$,
\begin{align}
\sup_{z\in K}\sup_{0\le s\le t}|w_s^\varepsilon(z)| &\le C_{t,K}\,\varepsilon, \\
\sup_{z\in K}\sup_{0\le s\le t}\big|y_s^\varepsilon(z)-e^{-Cs}\Phi(z)\big| &\le C_{t,K}\,\varepsilon.
\end{align}
In particular, with
\[
m_s^0(z):=\bigl(-B_{11}^{-1}B_{12}e^{-Cs}\Phi(z),\ e^{-Cs}\Phi(z)\bigr),
\]
we have $\sup_{z\in K}\sup_{0\le s\le t}|m_s^\varepsilon(z)-m_s^0(z)|\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.
title: Fast--slow estimate for the OU mean

In the contact substitution model, each of the X_L local infectious contacts is independently replaced by a global infectious contact with probability p in [0, 1]. The effective number of global contacts is X_G^(p) = X_G + Binomial(X_L, p) and the effective number of local contacts is X_L^(p) = X_L - Binomial(X_L, p). As p increases from 0 to 1, local contacts are converted to global contacts while the total number of contacts X_G + X_L remains invariant.
p in [0, 1]
Replacement choices are independent conditionally on X_L
title: Contact Substitution Model with Global Replacement Probability p

DRAFT; independent check by w395 pending. A fixed-radius box-minimizer event is determined by inside edges; the analogous global-minimizer event need not be. Set every edge induced by B_1 to weight 1. In one completion all other edges also have weight 1, and the horizontal S_1 chord through 0 is globally minimizing. In a second completion give every edge of the S_2 perimeter and every nearest-neighbor edge from S_1 to S_2 weight 1/20; all remaining edges have weight 1. Each S_1 pair has an outside bypass of at most ten cheap edges, costing at most 1/2, while any simple through-origin path costs at least 2. The completions agree inside B_1, but only the first has a globally minimizing S_1 chord through 0. The local box event is true in both. This scope distinction matters before conditioning on an inside-edge filtration. It is a deterministic positive-weight example, not an iid FPP counterexample.

[Proposition 65 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(X,\AA,\mu)$ be a measure space, $\{f,g\}\subset \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item Suppose $\int_Af^+\dd\mu\lor \int_A g^-\dd\mu<\infty$ and  $\int_{A} f\dd\mu\leq \int_{A}g\dd\mu$ for all $A\in \AA$ (or just for $A=\{f>g\}$). Then $f\leq g$ a.e.-$\mu$. 
\item  Suppose $\mu$ is $\sigma$-finite, $(\int f^-\dd\mu\land \int f^+\dd\mu)\lor (\int g^-\dd\mu\land \int g^+\dd\mu)<\infty$, and $\int_A f\dd\mu\leq \int_A g\dd\mu$ for all $A\in \AA$. Then again $f\leq g$ a.e.-$\mu$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 65 of arXiv:2604.01685

[Lem Lemma: Compactness criterion of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $\Delta$ be a locally compact second countable group, $\Gamma$ a group acting ergodically on a standard probability space $(X, \nu)$, and $\alpha: \Gamma \times X \to \Delta$ a cocycle. For Borel $B \subset X$, set
    $$ E(x, B) := \{\alpha(\gamma, x) : \gamma \cdot x \in B\} \subset \Delta.$$
    If there exists $B$ with $\nu(B) > 0$ such that $E(x, B)$ is relatively compact for $x$ in a set of positive measure, then $\alpha$ is cohomologous to a cocycle taking values in a compact subgroup of $\Delta$.
title: Lem Lemma: Compactness criterion of arXiv:2605.16921

body: Conjecture 13 of the Randomstrasse 2024 problem list asks whether the Sylvester Hadamard matrix H_k of order 2^k has discrepancy disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) sqrt(2^k) for odd k, where disc(A) = min over sign vectors x of the sup-norm of Ax. In plain terms: take the 2^k x 2^k matrix of plus and minus ones whose entry in row a and column u is (-1) to the mod-2 dot product of the k-bit strings a and u, and ask for the smallest possible largest absolute entry of the product Hx over sign vectors x. Indexing H_k by (-1)^{a.u} and reading x as the +-1 truth table of a Boolean function f on k variables, H_k x is the Walsh transform W_f, so disc(H_k) = min_f max_a |W_f(a)| = 2^k - 2 NL_max(k), where NL_max(k) is the largest nonlinearity of a Boolean function on k variables (the covering radius of the Reed-Muller code RM(1, k)). The conjectured value is exactly the bent-concatenation bound NL = 2^{k-1} - 2^{(k-1)/2}, which is beaten for odd k = 15 (Patterson and Wiedemann, 1983) and for every odd k > 7 (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel, 2006), and is optimal for k <= 7. So the conjecture holds exactly for k in {1, 3, 5, 7} and fails for every odd k >= 9. The numbers: for k <= 7 the maximum nonlinearity equals the bent-concatenation value (the covering radius of RM(1,5) is 12, Berlekamp and Welch 1972; of RM(1,7) is 56, Mykkeltveit 1980; k = 1, 3 by hand); for k = 9 functions of nonlinearity 242 exist (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel 2006), so disc(H_9) <= 512 - 484 = 28 < 32; for every odd k = 9 + 2j the direct sum of such a function with a bent function on 2j variables has largest Walsh coefficient 28 * 2^j, below 32 * 2^j, since the Walsh spectrum of a direct sum is the product; and Patterson and Wiedemann's nonlinearity 16276 on 15 variables gives disc(H_15) <= 216 < 256.

body: [Proposition 33 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $F:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ be right-continuous and nondecreasing. Then $\dd F$ is: $\sigma$-finite; finite iff $F$ is bounded; a probability iff  $\lim_\infty F-\lim_{-\infty}F=1$. For $x\in \mathbb{R}$, $\dd F(\{x\})=F(x)-F(x-)$. \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{align}
    R(q)=C(q) \cdot {C_{\beta=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\kappa}}}^{\rm ImDOZZ}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{1}{4\beta} - \frac{\beta}{2},\frac{1}{4\beta} - \frac{\beta}{2},\frac{1}{4\beta} - \frac{\beta}{2}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)},\quad \text{where }C(q)=\sqrt{\kappa/2} \cdot\frac{\sin(\kappa\pi/2)}{\sin(4\pi/\kappa)}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $\pi_n(\delta_z)$ be the distribution after $n$ steps of the OBABO discretization of \eqref{eq: general kinetic Langevin} when starting at $z\in \R^{2d}$.  
    Then there exist $C,h_0>0$ such that for all $z,\tilde z\in \R^{2d}$, $h\in(0,h_0]$ and $n\in\N$ such that $hn\leq1$ we have
    \begin{equation}
    
        \dTV{\pi_n(\delta_z),\pi_n(\delta_{\tilde z})}\leq C\frac{h^{1/2}}{(1-e^{-\gamma h/2})^{1/2}}\br{\frac{e^{\gamma h/2}}{(hn)^{3/2}}+\frac{1-e^{-\gamma h/2}}{h}\frac{e^{\gamma h/2}}{(hn)^{1/2}}+(hn)^{1/2}}|\tilde z -z|.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. Assume w_0=0 and an integer budget T>=120max{exp(1),n}/gamma^2. Choose the fixed step eta=gamma^2 T/120 for this run. Then the source phase-transition bound satisfies tau<=T/2 and L(w_T)<=480log(gamma^4 T^2)^2/(gamma^4 T^2). Thus the displayed upper bound is O(log(T)^2/T^2) for a fixed data set and fixed positive gamma. The step is constant within the run and selected using its budget T.

body: [Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.30513, 'Brieskorn spheres bound orbit spaces of torus manifolds'] For any pairwise coprime integers $p,q,r>1$ such that $\Sigma(p,q,r)$ bounds a smooth contractible manifold $W^{4}_{m}$, there exists a locally standard, smooth torus manifold $N^{8}$ with the contractible orbit space $Q=N^{8}/T^{4}$ with boundary $Q_{3}$ that is homotopy equivalent to $\Sigma(p,q,r)$ having $\pi_{1}(Q_{2})=\pi_{1}(Q_{3})$ a nontrivial perfect group. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop p:efron-stein-ineq of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $\{B_k\}_{k\in \mathbb{Z}}\subset\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be a bi-infinite sequence of pairwise essentially disjoint Borel sets (meaning $|B_k\cap B_{k'}|=0$ for all $k\ne k'$).
    Denote $B \coloneqq  \bigcup_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} B_k$.

    
    For $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ let $\xi,\eta_A : (\Xi_\mathrm{re},\mathcal{F}_\mathrm{re},\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{re})\to(\Xi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be coupled white noises as in (equation e:def-xi-eta of the paper) (so $\eta_A$ is obtained from $\xi$ by resampling $\xi|_A$).
    Then for any $Z\in L^2(\Xi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}_\mathrm{re}\left[
            \bigl(Z(\xi)  - Z(\eta_{B})\bigr)^2
        \right]
        \leqslant \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{re}\left[
            \bigl(Z(\xi) - Z(\eta_{B_k})\bigr)^2
        \right].
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Efron--Stein inequality for white noise

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Put \(\Lambda=\NS(A)\), let \(e_1,\dots,e_r\) be an integral basis,
where \(r=\rho(A)\), and let \(Q=(e_i\cdot e_j)_{i,j = 1}^r\).  There is an
integral symmetric matrix \(B=(b_{ij})\in\Sym_r(\Z)\) such that, in
\(H^4(A\times A,\Z)\),
\begin{equation}
 [W]=3[A\times\{0\}]+3[\{0\}\times A]-[\Delta_A]+\Gamma_B,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_B=\sum_{i,j=1}^r b_{ij}e_i\boxtimes e_j.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                              \tr(BQ)=12.
\end{equation}
We shall call \(B\) the \emph{residue matrix}.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a determinantal point process with correlation kernel K, Hermitian and satisfying 0<=K<=I in the discrete finite-space setting, the conditional law of the process restricted to a subset given the exact configuration on the complementary subset is again determinantal, with a kernel given by a Schur-complement formula. Partitioning the index set into A, the observed subset, and B, the remaining subset, and writing K in block form with entries K_AA, K_AB, K_BA, K_BB, the conditional kernel on B given the exact points observed in A is expressed via a Schur-complement expression such as K_BB - K_BA (K_AA - I)^{-1} K_AB, with the precise form depending on the convention used (correlation kernel versus L-ensemble) and on whether one conditions on points being present or absent in A. This identity is the fundamental tool for analyzing conditioning, dynamics, and Gibbs-type properties of determinantal processes, including eigenvalues of random matrices, non-intersecting paths, discrete orthogonal polynomial ensembles, and, via the transfer-current theorem, uniform spanning trees, reducing conditional analysis to linear algebra on the kernel matrix. It does not apply outside the determinantal class of point processes, or its Pfaffian analogue for orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, which has a related but distinct formula, and the exact form of the Schur complement depends sensitively on the specific conditioning event and on invertibility of the relevant block, which can fail or require a pseudo-inverse or limiting argument at special parameter values. Typical failure: Applying a Schur-complement conditional-kernel formula derived under one convention, such as conditioning an L-ensemble on a fixed exact sample, to a different conditioning question, such as conditioning on a sub-event like at least one point in a region, or mixing up the correlation-kernel and L-ensemble conventions, without re-deriving the correct formula; determinantal-process conditioning identities are convention-sensitive, and mixing them up produces a kernel that still looks plausible, expressed via some Schur complement, but does not correctly describe the actual conditional process. Canonical reference: Shirai and Takahashi, 2003, Journal of Functional Analysis; Borodin and Rains, 2005, Journal of Statistical Physics; Lyons, 2003, Annals of Probability.

 X:=E_I^{>},\qquad Y:={}_I E^{<}.

[Theorem thm.IMRN of arXiv:2609.01007, 'Global universality of the expected number \\of zeros of non-analytic random signals'] Suppose that the function $f$ satisfies the condition $\mathbf{(H1)}$. {Then, there exists a stationary and centered Gaussian process $(X_{\infty}(t))_{t \in [0, 2\pi]}$} such that as $n$ goes to infinity, the sequence stochastic processes $(X_n(t))_{t \in [0,2\pi]}$
converges to $(X_{\infty}(t))_{t \in [0, 2\pi]}$ in the sense of finite marginals.
Moreover, under each of the following additional conditions,
\begin{enumerate}
\item the function $f$ is $\mathcal C^2$,
\item there exists $\beta>2$ and $\gamma>0$ with $\beta \gamma  >1$  such that $f$ is $\mathcal C^{1+\gamma}$ and $\mathbb E[|a_1|^{\beta}]<+\infty$,
\item there exists $\gamma>0$ such that $f$ is $\mathcal C^{1+\gamma}$ and $\mathbb E[|a_1|^4]<+\infty$,
\item $\alpha$ is Diophantine and $p_n/n$ converges to $\alpha$ at a polynomial rate, $f$ is piecewise linear and $\mathbb E[|a_1|^4]<+\infty$,
\end{enumerate}
\smallskip
we have the following convergence in distribution as $n$ goes to infinity
\[
\mathcal N\left( f_n, \left[ \frac{p_n}{n}, \frac{p_n+2\pi}{n}  \right]\right) =\mathcal N\left( X_{n} , \left[ 0, 2\pi \right]\right) \xrightarrow{law} \mathcal N\left( X_{\infty} , \left[ 0, 2\pi \right]\right).
\]
Moreover, the limit process is such that 
\[
\mathbb E\left[ \mathcal N\left( X_{\infty} , \left[ 0, 2\pi \right]\right)\right] = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \sqrt{\frac{\langle f', f'\rangle}{\langle f, f\rangle}}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Combination of the main results of \cite{AP20IMRN}

\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}

\mathbf{E}^{(N)}_{t_1,\dots,t_N}\Big[\sup_{t\in[t_k, t_{k+1})}\|\Delta_t^n\|^r\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t_k}\Big]
&\leq_C \|\Delta_{t_k}^n\|^r
+h_n^{r\gamma +\frac{1}{2}}(1+\|X_{t_k}^{(n)}\|^{r\gamma\chi+r}) +h_n^{r\gamma }(1 + \|X^n_{t_k}\|^{r\gamma\chi+r})\\
&+h_n  (U_{t_k}^n)^r
+ h_n^{r\gamma+\frac12} (U_{t_k}^n)^{r\gamma\chi}  + h_n^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
for $n$ large enough uniformly over
$N\in\mathbb{N}_0$, partitions $\{t_1,\dots, t_N\}$,  and $k=0, \dots, N$.

body:
Let Omega = Omega_0^n. A function f: Omega -> R is called a configuration function (or self-certifying function) if there exists a family of certificates such that: (1) for each x, the value f(x) is certified by a subset of coordinates I(x) subset {1, ..., n} of size |I(x)| <= f(x); (2) whenever y agrees with x on I(x) (i.e. y_i = x_i for all i in I(x)), then f(y) >= f(x).
f is a real-valued function on a product space

[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] In the setting of \cref{sp:thm:spectral-rigidity}, let
\(F=(F^1,\ldots,F^k):Z\to\C^k\) be holomorphic and globally Lipschitz,
and let
\begin{equation}
 r=\dim_\C
 \frac{\Span_\C\{F^1,\ldots,F^k\}+\C1}{\C1}.
\end{equation}
Then, after selecting \(r\) complex-linear
combinations and making a complex-linear target change, there is a global
biholomorphic isometry
\[
             (Z,d,J)\cong(\C^r,g_{\rm E},J_0)\times(Z',d',J')
\]
under which the selected map is the projection.  The residual factor is
complete, normal, and klt, and
\begin{equation}
                         \Sing Z=\C^r\times\Sing Z'.
\end{equation}
For the tangent shrinker potential and its canonical ancient flow, the
corresponding potential, weighted-mass, and negative-time conclusions of
\cref{sp:thm:singular-product} also hold with \(m\) replaced by \(r\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 33 of arXiv:2609.02878

body: Every linear threshold function f = sgn(w.x - theta) on {-1,1}^n satisfies H(f) <= 14.22 I(f), where H is the Fourier entropy and I the total influence; the class was listed as open by Chakraborty et al. (LATIN 2018, arXiv:1903.11635). Ranking coordinates by |w_i|, the derivative D_i f is the indicator of a slab of width 2|w_i|, and the Erdos-Littlewood-Offord inequality applied to noise on the heavier coordinates gives E_S sum_{i in S} ln+(r(i)/|S|) <= 4.151 I, so the spectral sample lives on the top O(|S|) coordinates by weight; entropy against a rank-weighted reference measure, plus O'Donnell-Wright-Zhou's level-entropy bound (at most 3I), gives the constant (optimum exponent a = 1.2006, 14.2142). For f = G(w.x) with G changing sign t times, H(f) <= C_t I(f) with C_t = O(log t) (16.57 at t = 2). The supremum of H/I over threshold functions appears numerically to be about 4. The rank criterion is sufficient, not necessary: it fails for recursive ternary majority.

[Thm Slicing of arXiv:2607.19037, 'Semiclassical analysis for Yang--Mills \\ random connections on compact surfaces'] Let $E = \Sigma \times \mathbb{C}^N \to \Sigma$ be a $G = \mathsf{SU}(N)$-vector bundle of rank $N$, and let $\nabla = \mathrm{d} + A$ with $A \in \Omega^1(\Sigma, \mathfrak{su}(N))$ be a flat connection on $E$. Consider the twisted transport equation
\begin{equation}
    \partial_t g_t + \mathcal{L}_V g_t + A(V) g_t = 0,
\end{equation}
with initial condition $g_0 = 1_G$. Then the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The family of solutions $(g_t)_{t \geqslant 0}$ to (2.1) yields a family of gauge transformations in $C^\infty(\Sigma, G)$ such that
\[
\underbrace{g_t^{-1} \mathrm{d} g_t + g_t^{-1} A g_t}_{\text{in $C^\infty$ connection}} \;\xrightarrow[t \to \infty]{}\; 
\underbrace{A_\infty \coloneqq \sum_{a \in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)} \left( \int_{W^s(a)} A \right) U_a}_{\text{Morse-theoretic flat connection}},
\]
where convergence holds in $\mathcal{D}^{\prime,1}_{\Gamma_u}(\mathcal{S})$, and each $U_a$ (for $a \in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)$) is the current of integration along the unstable curve $W^u(a)$.

\item If $A_1, A_2 \in \Omega^1(\Sigma, \mathfrak{su}(N))$ are gauge equivalent, then
\[
\exp\left(A_{1,\infty}\right) = g^{-1}\exp\left( A_{2,\infty}\right) g
\]
for some fixed group element $g \in \mathsf{SU}(N)$. This means that the holnomy representations induced by the two connections are conjugated by $g\in G$.

\item The moduli space of flat connections modulo gauge,
\[
\mathcal{M}_g := \left\{ A \in \Omega^1(\Sigma, \mathfrak{su}(N)) : \mathrm{d} A + A \wedge A = 0 \right\} \big/ C^\infty(\Sigma, \mathsf{SU}(N)),
\]
admits the description
\[
\mathcal{M}_g = \left\{ \mathsf{Hol}_{\partial\mathcal{S}}\!\big( (g_a)_{a \in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)} \big) = 1_G \right\} \big/ G,
\]
where the quotient is taken with respect to the adjoint action of $G$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Slicing flat connections with a Morse gauge

[Proposition kill_bill of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] Let $G$ be a finite simple connected  graph and denote $x,y,z\in V(G)$ three distinct vertices in $G$. Assume that $G$ is 3-connected to $\{x,y,z\}$, that any $v\in V(G) \setminus \{x,y,z\}$ has degree 3 and that $x$, $y$ and $z$ have exactly degree two. Assign labels $\ell(x)=0$, $\ell(y)=u$ and $\ell(z)=u'$ for some $u,u' \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. We have
 \[
\operatorname{Diag}((G,\{x,y,z\},\ell))\leq C_{|E(G)|} \tau(0,u)\tau(u',u)\tau(u',0),
  \]
where the constant  $C_{|E(G)|}<\infty$ only depends on the edge cardinality of $G$.

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ be independent mean zero random variables with variance one, and for some $M>0$,
		$$
		\inf_{1\le i\le n}
		\E\bigl[\xi_i^2\mathbf 1_{\{|\xi_i|\le M\}}\bigr]\ge\frac12.
		$$
		There are constants $C=C(M)<\infty$ and $s_0=s_0(M)>0$ with the
		following property. Let $w_1,\ldots,w_n\in\R^m$ satisfy
		$$
		\sum_{i=1}^n w_iw_i^\top=I_m,
		\qquad
		s:=\max_{1\le i\le n}\|w_i\|_2\le s_0.
		$$
		If $G\sim N(0,I_m)$ is independent of the $\xi_i$'s, then
		$Y_s:=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\xi_i+sG$ has a density $f_{Y_s}$ satisfying
		$\|f_{Y_s}\|_\infty\le C^m$.

[Theorem t:KLR of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] {KonLehvRe19}}]
Assume \linebreak $(M,\nu,\msA,\mssL,\mathsf{\Gamma})$ is a standard Markov triple satisfying a Bakry--\'Emery Ricci-curvature lower bound.
Then, distributional solutions~$\rho_\bullet$ to~$\martp{\alpha}{\mssL}$ exist if and only if~$\alpha=n$ is a non-negative integer and the (possibly random) initial value~$\rho_0$ consists of exactly~$n$ atoms of \emph{equal} mass $\mbbP$-a.s., viz.~$\rho_0=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i^n \delta_{X^i_0}$.

In this case, the distributional solution is unique in law and it is given by the empirical measure~$\rho_t=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i^n \delta_{X^i_{nt}}$ of~$n$ independent diffusion processes, each with generator~$\big({\mssL,\msD(\mssL)}\big)$ and (random) starting point~$X^i_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 12 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $f\colon \R^2 \to \R$ be a continuous function.
	Let $Z\subset \R^2$ denote the critical set of~$f$
	(i.e. the set of all points where $f$ is not differentiable, or has $\nabla f = 0$).
	Let $E^*$ be the union of all connected components of the level sets
	of $f$ which have strictly positive length (i.e. Hausdorff measure $\H^1$).
	We say that $f$ has the \emph{weak Sard property}, if
	\begin{equation*}
		f_\# (\L^2 \rest (Z\cap E^*)) \perp \L^1. 
	\end{equation*}

Construct a short line segment Sigma through a non-equilibrium point of that orbit, transverse to the vector field (possible since omega(gamma^+) has no equilibria); the flow is then transverse to Sigma nearby, and successive intersections of the orbit through q with Sigma are monotonic along Sigma, a planar fact following from the Jordan curve theorem applied to the closed curve formed by an arc of the orbit between two consecutive intersections together with the segment of Sigma joining them, which separates the plane so the rest of the trajectory cannot cross it. Let $(\zeta_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a centered L\'evy process on $\ER^d$ and $h$ denote the step of the Euler scheme. Assume that $(x,\mu)\mapsto \sigma(x,\mu)$ is bounded (on $\MM\times{\cal P}(\MM)$). Then, \ref{condhvdeux} holds in the two following situations.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)](Standard Euler scheme)  The dynamics is given by \eqref{eq:formegeneralenoyau}, the step $h$ is small enough, $\zeta_1$ has moments of any order and some positive $\alpha$ and $C$ exist such that
$$ \langle x, b(x,\mu)\rangle \le C-\alpha |x|^2\quad\textnormal{and}\quad |b(x,\mu)|^2\le C(1+|x|^2) $$
\item[(ii)](Modified Euler scheme) The dynamics is given by \eqref{eq:formegeneralenoyautronc}, there exists $\alpha>0$ such that $\ES[|\zeta_h|^\alpha]<+\infty$ and Condition \ref{condhtronc} holds.

 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:GSsurround of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Assume the hypotheses of (thm:GS of the paper). There are $c,C>0$ and $D_1$, depending only on $d$, such
that for all $D\ge D_1$,
\[
  \mathbb{P}\big[F\text{ does not surround the origin at distance }D\big]\ \le\
  \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle\sum_{s\ge D}s\,\exp\Big\{-\frac{C\eta L\sqrt s}{(\log Ls)^{c}}\Big\}, & d=1,\\[2ex]
    \displaystyle\sum_{s\ge D}s^d\exp\Big\{-\frac{C\eta Ls}{(\log Ls)^{c}}\Big\}, & d=2,\\[2ex]
    \displaystyle\sum_{s\ge D}s^d\exp\{-C\eta Ls\}, & d\ge3 .
  \end{cases}
\]
In particular the right-hand side is summable in $D$ in every dimension, so by Borel--Cantelli $F$
surrounds the origin at an almost surely finite distance. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a6723bcdde0e3a400ceed939d5e5b320475951c52f9e7ffb42a5f62c93a80bff","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a6/a6723bcdde0e3a400ceed939d5e5b320475951c52f9e7ffb42a5f62c93a80bff.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7707778f7100c0a1b9461ae0b9e657355e028b198ef4e25fdf191ddb8af9f983","bundle_entry_key":"rank-one-fixed","bundle_id":"population.t419-rank-one-fixed-step-margin-and-noiseless-risk-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA rank-one convergence and deficiency margins","draft":"w705/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-rank-one-all-scale-gaussian-fixed-step-margin-rate","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C020 v1: one fixed-step rank-one population rate at every Gaussian scale

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This strengthens the step/accuracy quantifiers in C015: one fixed step works simultaneously for all target accuracies on one high-probability event. The method is the published positive-deficiency-margin idea (Min-Tarmoun-Vidal-Mallada, arXiv:2105.06351, Corollary 5, p.10), applied after the first strict discrete descent, together with C014's explicit boundedness argument. The zero-output invariant subspace is already in Zhang-Liu-Chen, arXiv:2502.01235, Theorem 3.1/C.10. No specialist-level novelty has been established.

## Statement

Let Delta=u v^T with unit u in R^m and unit v in R^p, arbitrary m,p>=1. Initialize b0=0, a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), any s>0, independently of everything else. Fix 0<rho<1 and set

 D_bar=2ps^2/rho, K_bar=D_bar+5.

For simultaneous ordinary GD on ||b a^T-Delta||F^2/2 choose any one constant step

 0<eta<=1/(6K_bar+1).

With probability at least 1-rho, for every integer t>=1,

 ||b_t a_t^T-Delta||F
 <=exp[-eta^3 s^4 rho^4 (t-1)/(128K_bar)].

In particular, for every 0<eps<1, the same run reaches eps by

 t>=1+ceil[(128K_bar/(eta^3 s^4 rho^4))log(1/eps)].

The step does not depend on eps. This includes a proper input and output rank-one bottleneck when m,p>=2 at every Gaussian scale. Rank-one signal condition number is 1; target singular value lambda>0 is handled by s_bar=s/sqrt(lambda), eta_bar=eta lambda and eps_bar=eps/lambda. The constants are deliberately conservative. This is a high-probability statement, not an unconditional expected-risk theorem for an initialization-independent fixed step.

## One initial event and the boundedness component

Let d=||a0||^2 and x0=v^T a0. As in C015, Markov and the standard normal density give the simultaneous event

 d<=D_bar, |x0|>=s rho/2

with probability at least 1-rho, using a union bound. Fix this event.

For the normalized population loss, C014 applies with r=1, C=I_p, D=Delta, q0=1/2, J=d+1, R=2 and K=d+5<=K_bar. Its safe-step conditions are eta<=min{1/2,1/(6K+1)}. The chosen bound meets both. Thus every iterate has

 q_(t+1)<=q_t-(eta/2)||grad q_t||F^2,
 ||b_t||^2+||a_t||^2<=K_bar.

C014 proves these facts through the exact simultaneous Gram-drift identity, a trace factor bound and a descent-segment induction; it does not assume boundedness. No Gaussian event for future iterates is multiplied into the initial probability.

## A positive deficiency margin after the very first step

Because b0=0, the first gradient in a is zero and the first gradient in b is -u x0. Its squared norm is x0^2>0. Descent gives

 q1<=1/2-(eta/2)x0^2,
 e1:=sqrt(2q1)<=sqrt(1-eta x0^2)<1.

The radical is real; explicitly eta x0^2<=eta d<=K_bar/(6K_bar+1)<1. The elementary inequality 1-sqrt(1-z)>=z/2 for 0<=z<=1 now gives

 1-e1>=eta x0^2/2.

This is the rank-one special feature: the initial residual norm is exactly the sole target singular value, so any strict decrease creates positive margin. At higher rank, reducing ||Delta||F slightly need not cross its smallest singular value, and this argument is not a general-rank warm-up proof.

## The margin keeps the output factor away from zero

The known invariant subspace gives b_t=beta_t u at every step. Descent implies e_t=sqrt(2q_t)<=e1 for all t>=1. The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives

 |beta_t|||a_t||=||b_t a_t^T||F>=1-e_t>=eta x0^2/2.

Since ||a_t||^2<=K_bar, it follows uniformly that

 beta_t^2>=eta^2 x0^4/(4K_bar)
             >=eta^2 s^4 rho^4/(64K_bar)=:b_lower^2>0.

This conclusion concerns the scalar factor coefficient in a known rank-one output subspace; it does not assume that the wide input factor is invertible or aligned.

## Gradient domination and the fixed-step rate

In this output subspace, grad_a q=beta_t(beta_t a_t-v). Hence

 ||grad q_t||F^2>=2 beta_t^2 q_t>=2 b_lower^2 q_t,
 q_(t+1)<=(1-eta b_lower^2)q_t, t>=1.

The multiplier is nonnegative. In fact b_lower^2<=beta_t^2<=K_bar and eta K_bar<1/6. Iterating and using e1<=1 yields

 e_t<=exp[-eta b_lower^2(t-1)/2],

which is exactly the displayed rate and hitting time. This is an analytic proof; no floating-point trajectory is used as evidence of convergence. Independent audit remains required.

## Boundaries

C015 remains a valid but more conservative finite-horizon route; the present proof replaces its accuracy-dependent step with a fixed-step margin argument at rank one. It does not claim the known margin technique or invariant reduction as new. It does not extend the all-scale guarantee to ranks greater than one, whose first step need not establish positive deficiency margin. The Gaussian failure event still exists, so C013's unconditional fixed-step expected-limit-risk obstruction remains compatible with this theorem.


Full deterministic C014 component:
# T419-C014 v1: empirical GD boundedness with an initialization-dependent step

Kind: bound. Target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This is an explicit anisotropic version of the published Gram-imbalance/descent method, not a solution of Target 2. It proves a trajectory component without assuming the iterates are bounded. The prior source is Du-Hu-Lee, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, Claim B.1; its full convergence theorems have different initialization/step hypotheses. C009 already identifies the exact covariance metric and C010 the positive-noise empirical landscape.

## Statement

Let C be any real positive definite p-by-p matrix, D any real m-by-p matrix, and r>=1. Put lambda=lambda_min(C)>0, c=||C||op, ell=||D||op, W=D C^(-1), and

 q(B,A)=(1/2)||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2,

with B m-by-r and A r-by-p. This is the empirical regression objective up to a constant when C=XX^T/n and D=ZX^T/n. Initialize at any finite deterministic factors B0,A0, and define

 q0=q(B0,A0), J=||A0 A0^T-B0^T B0||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(r)(J+2R), L=6Kc+ell.

For any fixed

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/L},

simultaneous ordinary factor GD satisfies, for every integer t>=0,

 q_t<=q0,
 ||B_t||F^2+||A_t||F^2<=K,
 ||(A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t)-(A0 A0^T-B0^T B0)||F<=2eta q0<1,
 sum_(t>=0) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/eta.

In particular the gradient tends to zero, every accumulation point is critical, and for every integer T>=1,

 min_(0<=t<T) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/(eta T).

All constants are finite and computable from C,D and the initialization. There is no Gaussian assumption and no low-rank assumption on W. No iterate-convergence, saddle-avoidance or statistical-risk assertion is included.

## Exact identities and product/factor bounds

Let G=BA C-D. The two factor gradients are G_B=G A^T and G_A=B^T G. With E_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t the first-order cross terms cancel exactly, giving

 E_(t+1)-E_t=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B),
 ||E_(t+1)-E_t||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2).

This cancellation only uses dependence on BA and does not require isotropic C. Also

 (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2
 <=r [||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2].

To verify it, write P=B^TB,Q=AA^T. Scalar trace Cauchy-Schwarz gives (tr(P+Q))^2<=r tr((P+Q)^2), and cyclicity of trace gives tr((P+Q)^2)=||P-Q||F^2+4 tr(PQ), tr(PQ)=||BA||F^2. No commutation is assumed.

When q<=q0, positivity of C gives ||BA-W||F<=sqrt(2q0/lambda), hence ||BA||F<=R. If additionally ||E-E0||F<=1, then ||E||F<=J, so the preceding trace bound implies

 ||B||F^2+||A||F^2<=sqrt(r) sqrt(J^2+4R^2)<=K.

The initialization meets these conditions and therefore has pair norm at most sqrt(K).

## Descent established before closing the boundedness induction

Suppose at the current iterate the pair norm is at most sqrt(K), and preceding steps have valid descent inequalities. Then

 ||grad q||F<=||BA C-D||op sqrt(||B||F^2+||A||F^2)
             <=(Kc/2+ell)sqrt(K).

Because eta<=1/(6Kc+ell), the proposed next point has pair norm at most 2sqrt(K). The connecting segment also lies in that ball. On that ball the Hessian quadratic form in a perturbation (dB,dA) is

 ||(dB A+B dA) C^(1/2)||F^2+2<BA C-D,dB dA>.

Its absolute value is at most

 [c(||A||op^2+||B||op^2)+||BA C-D||op]
 times (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2)
 <=[4Kc+(2Kc+ell)] (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2).

Here the first summand uses Cauchy-Schwarz on dB A+B dA; the cross term uses |<G,dB dA>|<=||G||op||dB||F||dA||F. Thus the Hessian operator norm on the segment is at most L. Taylor's theorem along that segment proves

 q_next<=q-eta||grad q||F^2+(L eta^2/2)||grad q||F^2
        <=q-(eta/2)||grad q||F^2.

In particular q_next<=q0. Telescoping the descent inequalities, including the proposed step, and using q>=0 yields

 sum_(j=0)^t eta^2||grad q_j||F^2<=2eta q0
 <=2q0/(1+2q0)<1.

Summing the imbalance increments now proves ||E_next-E0||F<=2eta q0<1. The product/factor bound therefore puts the endpoint back in the smaller ball of pair radius sqrt(K). This closes the induction without assuming a bound before proving descent on the required larger segment. The q0=0 case is included: both gradients vanish, the sequence is constant, and all inequalities still hold.

## Consequences and exact remaining gap

Telescoping for every finite horizon gives the infinite summability bound. A nonnegative summable sequence tends to zero, so the gradients vanish. Bounded finite-dimensional factor pairs have convergent subsequences; gradient continuity makes every subsequential limit critical. The running-minimum bound follows by averaging the finite sum. These statements do not require that the entire sequence converges to one point.

For B0=0 and a Gaussian A0, this provides an allowed positive step after observing the initialization, conditional on every full-row-rank design. It does not supply a single positive step independent of the unbounded Gaussian initializer. C013 shows that unconditional expected-limit risk with such an initialization-independent fixed step can diverge even at rank one.

Combining this bound with the already verified empirical strict-saddle landscape C010 is insufficient to conclude global optimization. One must additionally show that the specified zero/Gaussian initialization does not approach a nonglobal critical point, with all hypotheses of a saddle-avoidance theorem checked for its lower-dimensional initial support and step rule. Vanishing gradients do not establish that. Even convergence almost surely would not by itself justify passing to expected population risk; a failure-tail/integrability or finite-stopping argument is separately required. The usual full-ambient absolutely-continuous random-initialization theorem cannot simply be cited for the plane B0=0.

Independent reviewer audit and any novelty assessment remain pending. [Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.15432, 'A Concavity Theorem for the Parisi PDE'] Let \(\gamma\in\Opendenseset_\alpha\). Then the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every \(j\ge1\),
\[
\partial_x^j\Psi^\gamma\in C_b([0,1]\times\mathbb R),
\]
and, for every \(j\ge0\),
\[
\partial_s\partial_x^j\Psi^\gamma
\in L^\infty([0,1]\times\mathbb R).
\]
In particular, for every $j\geq 1$,
\[
\partial_x^j\Psi^\gamma\in
C_b^{\alpha/2,\alpha}([0,1]\times\mathbb R).
\]

\item For every \(s\in[0,1]\), the function
\(x\mapsto\Psi^\gamma(s,x)\) is even,
\(x\mapsto\partial_x\Psi^\gamma(s,x)\) is odd, and
\(x\mapsto\partial_{xx}\Psi^\gamma(s,x)\) is even.

\item For all \((s,x)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R\),
\[
|\partial_x\Psi^\gamma(s,x)|\le1,
\qquad
0\le \partial_{xx}\Psi^\gamma(s,x)\le1,
\qquad
|\partial_{xxx}\Psi^\gamma(s,x)|\le4.
\]
In particular, \(x\mapsto\Psi^\gamma(s,x)\) is convex.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:lamperti of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $f\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ with $f>0$ and let $b$ be as in Theorem~(thm:opvol of the paper). Suppose
there exist a $C^{2}$ diffeomorphism $g$ of $\mathbb{R}$ with $g'>0$, a constant $\sigma>0$ and
a function $\tilde b$ \emph{independent of the law}, such that for every compactly
supported $\mu$ with a density the spectral velocity field of $g(X)$ is that of a free
SDE with constant diffusion coefficient $\sigma$, that is
\begin{equation}
  g'(x)\Big(b(x)+f(x)^{2}H(f^{2}\mu)(x)\Big)
  =\tilde b\big(g(x)\big)+\sigma^{2}H\big(g_{\#}\mu\big)\big(g(x)\big).
\end{equation}
Then $g$ is affine and $f$ is constant. Equivalently, a non-constant state-dependent
sandwich volatility cannot be removed by any change of spectral variable.

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T in B(X,Y). If ran T has finite algebraic codimension in Y, i.e. there is a finite-dimensional subspace F of Y with ran T + F = Y and ran T ∩ F = {0}, then ran T is closed in Y. Consequently, closedness of the range need not be assumed in the definition of a Fredholm operator. (The hypothesis is genuine finite codimension; a merely dense proper range, such as that of a compact injective operator with dense range, has infinite codimension and is not closed.)
X and Y are Banach spaces (completeness of both is used through the open mapping theorem)
T: X -> Y is bounded and linear
ran T has an algebraic complement in Y of finite dimension

Fix $M,a,a_1 > 0$ such that $a,a_1$ are sufficiently small (depending on $a_0$). 
Let $\widehat{G}_{M,a}$ be the event that for every $0 \le s < t \le \infty$, the domain $D \setminus \eta([0,s]\cup[t,\infty))$ is $(M,a)$-good. Let $\widehat{E}_\delta$ denote the event that $\sup_t\mathrm{dist}(\eta(t),\partial D) \le \delta$. Let $U \subseteq D_\eta$ be the $\delta^{1+a_1}$-neighborhood of $\eta$. Then
\[ \mathbf{P}\left[ G^U_{\widehat{0},\widehat{\infty}}(M\delta^{-c(a+a_1)})^c \cap \widehat{G}_{M,a} \cap \widehat{E}_\delta \right] = O(M\delta^{{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}-ca-ca_1}) \quad\text{as}\quad \delta \to 0.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma le:close_geodesic of arXiv:2507.15589

\]
the sum for the bridge starting at $m=3$, and

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30232, 'Strong Unique Continuation for Fractional Schr\"odinger Operators'] Let \(n\ge3\), \(0<s<1\), and let \(\Omega\subset\R^n\) be open. Suppose

$$
    V\in L^{\frac{n}{2s}}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\C),
    \qquad
    u\in H^s(\R^n;\C),
$$

and

$$
    (-\Delta)^s u=Vu
    \qquad\text{in }\Omega
$$

in the sense of distributions. If, for some \(x_0\in\Omega\),
\begin{equation}
\int_{B_r(x_0)}|u|^2,dx=O(r^N)
\qquad\text{as }r\downarrow0
\end{equation}
for every \(N>0\), then \(u\equiv0\) in \(\R^n\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 225 (\textbf{main result}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For the spherical projection pursuit problem \eqref{eq:proj-pursuit-def}, we have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item 
        
        If $\mu \in \ocM^{\sph}(\alpha)$, for any $\iota > 0$ there exist $L$ large enough and $c$ small enough such that for sufficiently large $N$, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm that $(\iota,1-e^{-cN})$-attains $\mu$.
        \item 
        
        For any $\fq \in [1,2)$ and $\iotamsr > 0$, there exists small $\iotasol > 0$ such that the following holds.
        For any $L$, there exists small $c>0$ such that for sufficiently large $N$, all $L$-Lipschitz algorithms are $(\fq,\iotamsr,\iotasol,1-e^{-cN})$-confined to the set $\ocM^{\sph}(\alpha)$.
        \item 
        
We have $\ocM^{\sph}(\alpha) = \ocM^{\sph, \concave}(\alpha)$, i.e., concave $p$ suffice to achieve all endpoint measures of \eqref{eq:main-process-intro-general}.
    \end{enumerate}
The analogous results hold in the Ising setting, replacing $\ocM^{\sph}(\alpha), \ocM^{\sph, \concave}(\alpha)$
with $\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha), \ocM^{\Ising, \concave}(\alpha)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textbf{main result}

For $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ define $\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x) e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,dx$ for every $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^d$; the integral converges absolutely for every $\xi$. The map $f\mapsto\hat f$ is linear, $\hat f$ is bounded and uniformly continuous, and $\|\hat f\|_\infty \le \|f\|_1$. Symmetry rules (for $a,b\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\lambda>0$): $x\mapsto f(x-a)$ has transform $e^{-2\pi i a\cdot\xi}\hat f(\xi)$; $x\mapsto e^{2\pi i b\cdot x}f(x)$ has transform $\hat f(\xi-b)$; $x\mapsto f(\lambda x)$ has transform $\lambda^{-d}\hat f(\xi/\lambda)$; $\overline f$ has transform $\overline{\hat f(-\xi)}$. The inverse transform of $g\in L^1$ is $\check g(x)=\int g(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi$. With this convention Plancherel reads $\|\hat f\|_2=\|f\|_2$. Convention warning: texts using $\int f(x)e^{-ix\cdot\xi}dx$ have inversion with a factor $(2\pi)^{-d}$ and $\|\hat f\|_2=(2\pi)^{d/2}\|f\|_2$; the unitary convention puts $(2\pi)^{-d/2}$ in front of both. Constants in Plancherel, Poisson summation, the uncertainty principles and Paley-Wiener depend on the convention, so check it before importing a constant.
f is Lebesgue integrable on R^d
convention: kernel e^{-2 pi i x.xi} with no normalizing constant
title: Fourier Transform on L^1(R^d)

[Lemma lower_bnd of arXiv:2607.05054, 'Root Dynamics of Differentiated Polynomials with Rotationally Invariant Structure'] Let $Q$ be a polynomial of degree $n \geq 1$ with positive real roots, and let 
$(r_j)_{1 \leq j \leq n}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive real numbers, such that 
$$ \max_{1 \leq j \leq n-1} (r_j/r_{j+1}) \leq \alpha.$$
Suppose the $ j $-th smallest root of $ Q $ is at least $ r_j $ for $ 1 \leq j \leq n $. Then, for integers $m \geq 1$, $ 1 \leq q \leq m-1 $ and $ 1 \leq j \leq n $, the $ j $-th smallest root of the polynomial $S$ given by 
$$S(z) = q Q(z) + m z Q'(z)$$
is at least
\begin{align*}
\left(1 - \frac{1}{ \max(1, j - 1 - y)}\right) r_j.
\end{align*}  
For $ 2 \leq j \leq n $, the $ (j-1) $-th smallest root of $ Q' $ is at least  
\begin{align*}
\left(1 - \frac{1}{ \max(1, j - 1 - y)}\right) r_j.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lower_bnd of arXiv:2607.05054

body:
[Defin 77 ($\epsilon$-cluster structure) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\eps>0$ and $\bs{n}_K=(n_1, \dots, n_K)\in (\mathbb{N}^*)^K$ with $\ov{\bs{n}}_K=\sum_{k=1}^K n_k = N$. One says
that $\bs{x}_N \in \R^{N}_{<}$ has the $\epsilon$-cluster $\bs{n}_K$  if the following is true.
Define $i_1=1$ and $i_k = n_1 + \dots + n_{k-1}+1$ for $k\geq 2$, so that $x_{i_k}$ is the leftmost particle in the $k^{\e{th}}$ cluster.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For all $k = 1, \dots, K$,  $x_{i_k + j} - x_{i_k + j-1} \leq \epsilon$ for all $j = 1, \dots, n_k -1$.
\item For all $k = 2, \dots, K$,  $x_{i_{k}}  - x_{i_{k} -1} > \epsilon$.
\end{enumerate}
We let $\mc{E}_{\eps}( \bs{n}_K)$ be the set of $\bs{x}_N \in \R^{N}_{<}$ that have $\epsilon$-cluster $\bs{n}_K$.
title: $\epsilon$-cluster structure
Auxiliary distance recursion

[Lemma lem:iicnew2 of arXiv:2604.08462, 'Convergence of $k$-point functions in\\ high dimensional percolation'] Fix an integer $k \geq 1$ and a tree $T \in \mathfrak{T}_k$.
    For each $n \geq 1$, suppose we have 
    a sequence $( \{ x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}\})_{n=1}^\infty$ where for each $n$,
    $(x_0^{(n)}, x_1^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}) \in G(\epsilon, n)$, and  where $x_i^{(n)} = 0$ for all $n$ for some arbitrary $0 \leq i \leq k$. Suppose also that there exists a $c > 0$ such that
    \begin{equation}\liminf_{n \to \infty} n^{(d-4)k + 2}\tau_T\left(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_{k}^{(n)} \right) \geq  c \ .
    
    \end{equation}

    Then, for each cylinder event $E$,
    we have for each $i$:
    \begin{equation}  \lim_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}( E \mid  \Gamma(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}), \, \mathcal{T}(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}) = T) = \nu(E)\ . \end{equation}

    In particular, with the same $i$ and $(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)})$, for each fixed finite $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$, we have
    \begin{equation} 
    \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{P}(\Gamma_{T,i}(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}; \mathcal{D}))}{\tau_T(x_0^{(n)}, \dots, x_k^{(n)}) \nu(\Xi(\mathcal{D}))} = 1\ . 
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:iicnew2 of arXiv:2604.08462

Let X_1,...,X_n be iid from a finite or countable discrete distribution p=(p_j), n>=1, and M_n=sum_j p_j*1_(j does not appear among X_1,...,X_n). For every epsilon>0, Pr(M_n>E[M_n]+epsilon)<=exp(-n*epsilon^2) and Pr(M_n<E[M_n]-epsilon)<=exp(-C0*n*epsilon^2/4), where C0=inf_(0<x<1/2) 2/[x*(1-x)*log(1/x)]. The source gives C0 approximately7.6821, and C0>=2*e>4, so both tails admit the weaker exponent -n*epsilon^2. The statements concern missing probability mass, not the number of unseen symbols.
IID observations from a discrete probability distribution; finite n>=1; epsilon>0.

[Lemma lem:averaging-close of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Let $E=\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$ and let
\[
\Pi(dz)=e^{-V(z)}\,dz
\]
be a probability measure on $E$, where $V\in C^1(E)$.
Let $a_2:E\to\mathbb{R}^{d_y\times d_y}$ be measurable and symmetric, and assume that $a_2$ is locally bounded and uniformly elliptic on compact sets (as in (sec:setting of the paper)). Define the pre-form on $L^2(\Pi)$ with core $\mathcal D_0:=C_c^\infty(E)$ by
\[
\mathcal E_{y,0}(v,w)
:=\int_E \langle \nabla_y v(z),\,a_2(z)\nabla_y w(z)\rangle\,\Pi(dz),
\qquad v,w\in\mathcal D_0.
\]
Then $(\mathcal E_{y,0},\mathcal D_0)$ is closable in $L^2(\Pi)$. We denote its closure by
$(\mathcal E_y,\mathcal D(\mathcal E_y))$ and equip $\mathcal D(\mathcal E_y)$ with the norm
$\|v\|_{\mathcal E_y,1}^2:=\|v\|_{L^2(\Pi)}^2+\mathcal E_y(v,v)$.

body:
[Lemma lem:centers of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ be nonzero and nonnegative, and set
$\kappa:=\|f\|_1$.  Then $\mathsf C(f)$ is nonempty and compact, and
$\mathcal A(f)<2\kappa$.  Moreover, the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$,
then every $\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\mathbb R^2\setminus B_r(\mathbf b)}f
  \,\mathrm d\mathbf x
  \leq\frac12\mathcal A(f);
\end{equation}
\item if, for some $r,s>0$ and $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^2$,
\[
  \operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0),
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}f\subset B_s(\mathbf a),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf a|\leq r+s
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
moreover, the mass center $\mathbf X_f$ defined by (equation eq:mass-center of the paper) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_f|
  \leq\frac{r+2s}{\kappa}\mathcal A(f)
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$
and $\mathcal A(f)<\kappa$, then
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{diam}\mathsf C(f)\leq2r;
\end{equation}
\item for any nonzero, nonnegative $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$,
\[
  |\mathcal A(f)-\mathcal A(g)|\leq2\|f-g\|_1;
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ has a closed graph with respect
to strong $L^1$ convergence: if $f_n,f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ are nonzero and
nonnegative, then
\[
  f_n\to f\ \text{in }L^1(\mathbb R^2),\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\to\mathbf b\ \text{in }\mathbb R^2,\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\in\mathsf C(f_n)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f);
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ is upper semicontinuous\footnote{See
[AubinFrankowska2009] for this standard definition.} with
respect to strong $L^1$ convergence: for every nonzero, nonnegative
$f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ and every open set $O\subset\mathbb R^2$ with
$\mathsf C(f)\subset O$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that
\[
  g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2),\quad g\geq0,\quad g\not\equiv0,\quad
  \|g-f\|_1<\delta
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathsf C(g)\subset O.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Properties of optimal translation centers

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Let $m=m(n)$ be a sequence of positive integers with the same parity as $n$, with $|m|\le Cn^{3/4}$. Then,
$$\E(\tilde{Z}_m)\sim\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\cdot\exp\left(-\dfrac{1}{12}\cdot\dfrac{m^4}{n^3}-\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$$
and
$$\dfrac{\E(\tilde{Z}_m^2)}{\E(\tilde{Z}_m)^2}\sim\exp\left(\dfrac{1}{2(d-1)}\cdot\dfrac{m^4}{n^3}+\SL{i=3}^\infty\dfrac{d^{-i}}{2i}\right).$$
Moreover, these convergences are uniform in $m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:vector-KP-nondegeneracy-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Assume that 
\(
\mathbb{E}(X_0+X_1)=1
\), 
and let 
\(
M=\lim_n M_n
\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\kappa_X<1\), then the following are equivalent:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathbb{P}(M>0)>0\);

\item \(\mathbb{E} M=1\);

\item 
\(
H^+(X)<\infty
\)
and 
\(
\gamma(X)<0
\).
\end{enumerate}

\item If 
\(
\kappa_X=1
\),
then the following boundary dichotomy holds. If
\[
X_0+X_1=1
\qquad\text{almost surely},
\]
then
\[
M_n=1\quad(n\ge0),
\qquad
M=1
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
If instead
\[
\mathbb{P}(X_0+X_1=1)<1,
\]
then
\[
M=0
\qquad
\text{almost surely}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:vector-KP-nondegeneracy-paper of arXiv:2606.08683

body:
[Theorem 6 (Teichm\"uller's Theorem) of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let $x=[X,f]$ and $y=[Y,g]$ be points of $\mathcal T(S)$. There exists a
unique quasiconformal map, called the Teichm\"uller map, 
\( h\colon X\to Y \)
satisfying $h\circ f\simeq_{\text{iso}} g$.

If $x\ne y$, then there exist unique unit-area quadratic differentials
\( q\in\mathcal Q^1(X), q'\in\mathcal Q^1(Y), \)
and a number $K>1$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \mu_h
  =
  k\frac{\overline q}{|q|},
  \quad
  k
  =
  \frac{K-1}{K+1},
  
\end{equation}
almost everywhere on $X$. After choosing compatible natural coordinates
\( z=x+iy\) for $q$, $w=u+iv$ for $q'$,
the map $h$ is affine and has the form
\begin{equation}
  u=K^{1/2}x,
  \quad
  v=K^{-1/2}y.
  
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\( d_{\mathrm T}(x,y)=\frac12\log K. \)
If $x=y$, the extremal map is conformal. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Teichm\"uller's Theorem

[Cor 4 of arXiv:2506.12145, 'Functional central limit theorem for dependent models with finite memory'] We have, as $n \to \infty$,
\[\left\{\sqrt{n}\left(\frac{S_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^E}{\lfloor nt\rfloor} \right) \ , \ t\geq 0 \right\} \overset{d}{\longrightarrow} \left\{W_t \ , \ t\geq 0\right\},\]
where $\E[W_sW_t] = \frac{1}{t}\sigma^2_{\alpha,k}$ for all $0<s\leq t$.

Moreover, as $n \to \infty$, we have that almost surely: $C^E_n \to 0$  and
\begin{equation}
\frac{C^E_n}{\sqrt{n}}\overset{d}{\longrightarrow} N\Big(0,\frac{\sigma^2_{\alpha,k}}{3}\Big).
\end{equation}
The details of $\sigma_{\alpha,k}^2$ are given in Section \ref{sec:ERW}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma easyproj of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho, \mu)$ be a rooted finitely measured Polish $\mathbb{R}$-tree.
For all $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, let $\rho \! \in \!  \mathtt{t}_n\!\subseteq\! \mathtt{t}_{n+1}\!\subseteq\! T$ be closed subtrees. We set $\mu_n \! = \!  \mathtt{P}_{\! \mathtt{t}_n}\mu$. Then the following properties hold true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] For all integers $n\! \geq \!  m$, $\mathtt{P}_{\!\mathtt{t}_m}\mu_n\! = \!  \mu_m$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] $\sup_{n\in \mathbb{N}} \mu_n (T\backslash B(\rho, r)) \! \leq \!  \mu (T\backslash B(\rho, r)) \! \longrightarrow\!  0$ as $r\! \rightarrow \! \infty$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] Let us denote by $\mathtt{t} $ the closure of $\, \bigcup_{n\in \mathbb{N}} \mathtt{t}_n$. Then $\mu_n \! \rightarrow \! \mathtt{P}_{\!\mathtt{t}} \mu$ weakly.
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma easyproj of arXiv:2608.09856

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). In two-dimensional critical or near-critical percolation, RSW theory states that if crossing probabilities of n x n squares are uniformly bounded away from 0 as n grows, then crossing probabilities of rho n x n rectangles, for any fixed aspect ratio rho, are also uniformly bounded away from 0 (and from 1) by a constant depending on rho but not on n. The classical proof glues together several square-crossing events using the FKG inequality and translation and reflection symmetry of the lattice. RSW estimates are the essential multi-scale input for proving arm-exponent bounds, conformal-invariance-adjacent results, and, via the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, for establishing sharpness of the phase transition without relying on exact self-duality. RSW does not by itself prove existence of a scaling limit as n -> infinity, does not give the exact value of any crossing probability, only two-sided bounds; and the classical form required exact self-duality (p=1/2 on the square lattice), so extending the theory to general planar lattices or to p != 1/2 required a genuinely new, duality-free argument (Tassion, 2016). Typical failure: Assuming that RSW-type bounded-away-from-0/1 crossing estimates transfer automatically to a new planar model merely because it is monotone and planar; RSW requires either exact self-duality or the more robust but still nontrivial Tassion-style construction, and models without FKG, or with strong enough long-range dependence, can fail to admit the needed gluing arguments even though they look superficially similar to Bernoulli percolation. Canonical reference: Russo, 1978, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Seymour and Welsh, 1978, Annals of Discrete Mathematics; Tassion, 2016, Probability Theory and Related Fields.

body:
[Corollary 47 (Normal root with a Gaussian tangential fibre) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(B\in\Sym_d(R_0)\) be invertible.  Form
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf F_{\rho,B}^\bullet
 &=
 \Tot\left(
 \mathsf K_{\rho,h}^\bullet
 \widehat\otimes_{R_0}
 (\Omega_{R_0}^\bullet,\delta_B)
 \right),\\
 \mathsf{DR}_{\rho,B}^\bullet
 &=
 \Tot\left(
 \widehat{\mathsf{DR}}_{\rho,h}^\bullet
 \widehat\otimes_{R_0}
 (\Omega_{R_0}^\bullet,\nabla_B)
 \right).
\end{align*}
Then
\[
 \Theta_{\rho,B}
 =
 \iota_\rho\widehat\otimes\Theta_B
 :
 \mathsf F_{\rho,B}^\bullet
 \longrightarrow
 \mathsf{DR}_{\rho,B}^\bullet
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism.  Its cohomology is concentrated in degree \(d+1\),
where
\[
 H^{d+1}(\mathsf{DR}_{\rho,B}^\bullet)\simeq R_0/(h).
\]
For a top form,
\begin{equation}
 \left[
 a(r,x)\,\mathrm d\log r\wedge\operatorname{vol}_x
 \right]
 =
 \left[
 \exp\!\left(\frac12\Delta_C\right)a(0,x)
 \right]_{x=0}
 \left[
 \mathrm d\log r\wedge\operatorname{vol}_x
 \right].

\end{equation}
Thus normal restriction at the connected root and complete tangential Wick
contraction are the two factors of one de Rham reduction.

When \(\Re h>0\) and \(\Re B>0\), the physical period is
\begin{equation}
 (2\pi)^{-d/2}
 \int_0^1\int_{\R^d}
 r^h e^{-x^{\mathsf T}Bx/2}
 \frac{\mathrm d r}{r}\,\mathrm d x
 =
 \frac{\det(B)^{-1/2}}{h}.

\end{equation}
Hence a connected root produces exactly one simple pole and its residue is
the Gaussian forest amplitude.

[Theorem thm:strong-law of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $g$ be real-valued and of bounded variation on the torus with
		at least one jump. Then, with the average taken over a period in
		time,
		\begin{equation}
			\mathbb{E}_{t}\,Y_{M} = \big(\kappa_{g} + o(1)\big)\log M,
			\qquad
			\operatorname{Var}_{t}(Y_{M}) = O(\log M),
			\qquad
			\kappa_{g}
			= \frac{\Vert g\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\sum_{j}|J_{j}|^{2}}{2\pi^{2}},
			
		\end{equation}
		and consequently, for almost every $t$,
		\begin{equation}
			\frac{Y_{M}(t)}{\log M}\;\longrightarrow\;\kappa_{g};
			
		\end{equation}
		at almost every time the density lies outside $H^{1/2}$, its
		critical mass diverging at the universal logarithmic rate
		$\kappa_{g}$; moreover, for almost every $t$ the density lies in
		$C^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, in no Besov space
		$B^{\sigma}_{1,\infty}$ with $\sigma > \tfrac12$, and its graph has
		upper box dimension exactly $\tfrac32$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
