[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ be given as in \eqref{LAG}, where $A$ is symmetric and positive definite and $G$ is arbitrary. Then it holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] There exists a symmetric matrix of real numbers $S=(s_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le d}$, such that $\mu=e^{\langle x, Sx\rangle}\text{d}x$ is an infinitesimally invariant measure for $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$.
\item[(ii)] Assume that $G$ is a Hurwitz matrix, i.e. all eigenvalues of $G$ have strictly negative real parts. Let
$$
S=\left(-\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{Gt}\,(2A)\,e^{G^T t}\,dt \right)^{-1}.
$$
Then $S$ is negative definite and $\mu=e^{\langle x, Sx\rangle}\text{d}x$ is the unique infinitesimally invariant measure for $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and the unique (finite) invariant measure for the semigroup associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}. (Here uniqueness is meant up to a multiplicative constant.)\\
In particular, let $\tilde{G}:= S+(G-AS)$. Then, $\tilde{G}$ is Hurwitz and
$$
Sx+(G-AS)x
$$
is the unique SOHHD of $\tilde Gx$, and $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and $(L^{\widetilde{G}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ have the same unique (finite) infinitesimally invariant measure $\mu$.
\item[(iii)] Suppose that the semigroup $(T_t)_{t>0}$ associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ or its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}, admit a finite invariant measure. Then $G$ is a Hurwitz matrix. Thus, the OU-semigroup $(T_t)_{t>0}$ or the OU-process admit a finite invariant measure if and only if $G$ is a Hurwitz matrix.
\end{itemize}

body:
Let Ω ⊂ R^n (n ≥ 2) be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, dS the surface measure and ν the outward unit normal (defined dS-a.e.), and let 1 ≤ p < ∞.

(1) Existence and boundedness. There is a unique bounded linear operator T : W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^p(∂Ω, dS) such that Tu = u|_{∂Ω} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄). Tu is the trace of u, and ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C(Ω, p) ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Ω)}.

(2) Kernel. ker T = W^{1,p}_0(Ω), the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω). A W^{1,p} function vanishes on ∂Ω in the trace sense exactly when it is a W^{1,p}-limit of compactly supported smooth functions.

(3) Range (Gagliardo). For 1 < p < ∞ the range of T is exactly the fractional Sobolev space W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω), and T has a bounded linear right inverse W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω) → W^{1,p}(Ω). In particular T : H^1(Ω) → H^{1/2}(∂Ω) is bounded and onto, and every g ∈ H^{1/2}(∂Ω) has an extension u ∈ H^1(Ω) with Tu = g and ||u||_{H^1(Ω)} ≤ C ||g||_{H^{1/2}(∂Ω)}. For p = 1 the range is all of L^1(∂Ω). Since H^{1/2}(∂Ω) ↪ L^2(∂Ω) is compact, T : H^1(Ω) → L^2(∂Ω) is a compact operator.

(4) Integration by parts with traces. For u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), v ∈ W^{1,p'}(Ω) with 1/p + 1/p' = 1 (p' = ∞ for p = 1) and each i,
   ∫_Ω u ∂_i v dx + ∫_Ω v ∂_i u dx = ∫_∂Ω (Tu)(Tv) ν_i dS.
Hence for u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω) Green's first identity ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v dx + ∫_Ω (Δu) v dx = ∫_∂Ω (∂_ν u)(Tv) dS holds with ∂_ν u := ν · T(∇u) ∈ L^2(∂Ω), and for u ∈ H^1_0(Ω) all boundary terms vanish.

Where it fails. There is no trace operator on L^p(Ω): ∂Ω has Lebesgue measure zero, an L^p class has no boundary values, and an estimate ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C||u||_{L^p(Ω)} is false (the full W^{1,p} norm is needed). For p > 1 the range is NOT L^p(∂Ω): a general g ∈ L^2(∂Ω) has no H^1(Ω) extension. The kernel and range statements use the Lipschitz boundary (a segment / extension property); for domains with cracks, slits or cusps the boundary is not Lipschitz and these statements need modification (a crack has two sides with two different traces). The trace of ∇u exists for u ∈ H^2(Ω), not for a general u ∈ H^1(Ω), so ∂_ν u is not defined in L^2(∂Ω) for arbitrary H^1 functions.
Ω bounded open with Lipschitz boundary, n ≥ 2
1 ≤ p < ∞ for existence, boundedness and kernel; 1 < p < ∞ for the fractional-space range description
Green's identity form: u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω)

				$\bigl(W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_n)}^{(q)}(\cdot,y)\bigr)_{n\ge1}$,
				where for each $n\ge1$,
				$W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_n)}^{(q)}(\cdot,y)$ is a.s. the unique solution to
				\eqref{volterra_approx}. Then,
				\[				
				\E\left[\sup_{x\in[y,T]}
				\left|
				W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu_n)}^{(q)}(x,y)
				-
				W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu)}^{(q)}(x,y)
				\right|^2
				\right]
				\longrightarrow 0,
				\qquad \text{as $n\to\infty$},
				\]
				where $W_{{\mathbf{T}}(\nu)}^{(q)}(\cdot,y)$ is the unique solution to
				\eqref{volterra_limit}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  \operatorname{supp}f\subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf a)
\]
for some $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^2$,
one has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D(f)\leq C_{\rm loc}\mathcal A(f).
\end{equation}

Let X be a random vector in a real separable Hilbert space with E||X||^2<infinity and covariance H=E[X tensor X]. Assume exact interpolation: Y=<X,theta_star> almost surely for a fixed theta_star in the Hilbert space. Assume R>0 and the operator fourth-moment bound E[||X||^2*(X tensor X)]<=R*H in positive-semidefinite order. Start theta_0=0 and use fresh IID examples with the single-example SGD update theta_(t+1)=theta_t-gamma*(<X_(t+1),theta_t>-Y_(t+1))*X_(t+1), where gamma>0 is constant during the run. Put D=||theta_star||^2 and f_t=E Rcal(theta_t), where Rcal(theta)=E(<X,theta>-Y)^2/2 =||H^(1/2)*(theta-theta_star)||^2/2; the outer expectation is over SGD samples. If 4*gamma*||H||<=1, then for each integer t>=1, f_t<=D/(4*gamma*t)+gamma*R*sum_(k=0)^(t-1) f_k/(t-k). The convolution is over preceding expected risks and does not assume that the last-iterate risks are monotone. No strictly positive smallest covariance eigenvalue is required.
Fresh IID noiseless samples, theta_star in the real Hilbert space, theta_0=0.
H=E[X tensor X] with E||X||^2<infinity; E[||X||^2*(X tensor X)]<=R*H for R>0.
4*gamma*||H||<=1.

[Theorem 6 (Mod-\(\phi\) convergence for \(B_N\)) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Let $X_N$ denote the number of inversions of a random signed permutation of $B_N$. Then \(X_N/N\) converges mod-\(\phi\) with parameter \(N\), domain
\[
	\mathscr{D}=\{z\in\C:\ \tfrac{e^{2zt}-1}{2zt}\notin(-\infty,0] \text{ for all } t\in[0,1]\},
\]
normalization function
\[
\phi(z)=\int_0^1 \log\Bigl(\frac{1-e^{2zt}}{-2zt}\Bigr)\,dt,
\]
and limiting function
\[
\psi(z)=\exp\Bigl(\frac12\log\Bigl(\frac{1-e^{2z}}{-2z}\Bigr)-\frac{z}{2}\Bigr)
=\sqrt{\frac{e^{2 z}-1}{2 z}}\;e^{-z/2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; PROOF UNAUDITED; ROUTE FAILURE, NO NOVELTY CLAIM. For the square tripod f(x)=sum_i max(0,1/2-||x-c_i||_1) v_i, with c_i=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1) and unit planar v_i at pairwise angle 120 degrees, every continuous scalar factorization F=g composed with h has uniform error at least 1/4. Every depth L>=2 exact biased ReLU representation, with linear output, consequently satisfies d_l product_{k!=l} a_k >=1/8, where a_l and d_l are its two leading squared weight singular values. These constraints imply cost >= L^2/(L-1) times ((L-1)/8)^(1/L), but admit abstract spectra a_l=((L-1)/8)^(1/L), d_l=a_l/(L-1), whose cost per layer tends to 1. For L>=17 the spectra also obey the global top-singular-value product bound sqrt(2). Thus these necessary scalar inequalities alone cannot establish asymptotic cost 2. The spectra are not a representing network and do not settle Jacot's conjecture.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:86a406c244efd15153f2a84c796a6f8cfa5c2e0bd5e467b74ef5175a50b3d563","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/86/86a406c244efd15153f2a84c796a6f8cfa5c2e0bd5e467b74ef5175a50b3d563.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5b109ff4f77ecccfe672b9e67ce2a2c41354c2383e61f6e640c75bfd049bb523","bundle_entry_key":"tripod-centered-rank-one-truncation-barrier","bundle_id":"population.w715-t276-truncation-barrier-unaudited","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Deep ReLU representation cost","draft":"w715/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.deep_networks:jacot-tripod-centered-rank-one-truncation-barrier-unaudited","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Single-layer rank-one truncations do not force normalized cost two

Target 2. Status: proof unaudited; route-failure result, not a network construction.

The setting is the dossier's exact tripod map f on the square. All norms below
are Euclidean or their induced operator norms, except the Frobenius norm.

## A uniform obstruction to scalar factorization

Every F=g composed with h, with h:[0,1]^2 -> R continuous, satisfies

    sup_x ||F(x)-f(x)|| >= 1/4.                                  (1)

Here g need not be continuous. To prove this, suppose the error is <1/4.
The three distinguished corner values f(c_i)=v_i/2 have pairwise distance
sqrt(3)/2, so F(c_i) are distinct. Thus h(c_i) are distinct. Choose j so
h(c_j) lies between the other two values. As in the dossier, there is a path
between the other corners outside the closed support triangle of leg j.
The intermediate value theorem gives a point q on this path with
h(q)=h(c_j), hence F(q)=F(c_j). But f(q) is zero or lies on another leg.
For its parameter t>=0, the squared distance to f(c_j) is

    ||v_j/2-t v_i||^2=1/4+t^2+t/2 >=1/4       (i != j).

It follows that ||f(q)-f(c_j)||>=1/2, whereas the assumed approximation
and F(q)=F(c_j) give a strict upper bound 1/2. This is a contradiction.
The support complement and tip facts are settled ground from Target 1.

## Necessary constraints on every layer

Let a depth-L biased ReLU network represent f exactly. The final layer is
linear, as in Jacot's model. Let s_{1,l}>=s_{2,l} be the two largest
singular values of W_l. All W_l have rank at least two: a rank-one weight
matrix, even with its bias and subsequent nonlinear layers, would provide
an exact scalar factorization of f.

Fix p0=(1/2,1/2), whose maximum distance to the square is R=1/sqrt(2).
Replace W_l by its top rank-one singular truncation W_l^(1), and replace
its bias by

    b_l' = b_l + (W_l-W_l^(1)) alpha_{l-1}(p0).

The altered network F_l factors through one scalar at layer l. Its raw
layer error at input x is

    (W_l-W_l^(1))(alpha_{l-1}(x)-alpha_{l-1}(p0)).

ReLU is globally 1-Lipschitz. Prefix and suffix Lipschitz bounds therefore give

    ||F_l-f||_infinity <= R s_{2,l} product_{k != l} s_{1,k}.

This estimate also holds when l is the final linear layer. Combining it
with (1), and squaring, yields for every l

    d_l product_{k != l} a_k >= c,
    a_l=s_{1,l}^2, d_l=s_{2,l}^2, c=1/8.                       (2)

## Exact optimization of these spectral constraints

Put t=product_l a_l. Constraint (2) says d_l>=c a_l/t. Thus the total
parameter cost C_L, including nonnegative bias costs, satisfies

    C_L >= sum_l(a_l+d_l)
        >= (1+c/t) sum_l a_l
        >= L t^(1/L)(1+c/t).                                  (3)

For L>=2 the derivative of the last expression, as a function of t>0, is

    t^(1/L-2) [t-(L-1)c].

Its minimum is attained at t=(L-1)c. Therefore these constraints give

    C_L >= [L^2/(L-1)] [(L-1)/8]^(1/L).                       (4)

The important finding is the limitation, not an improved finite-depth bound.
For each L>=2 the abstract spectral values

    a_l=[(L-1)/8]^(1/L),    d_l=a_l/(L-1),    all l,

satisfy 0<d_l<=a_l and EVERY inequality (2) with equality. Their summed
squared singular values equal the right side of (4), whose quotient by L
tends to 1. For L>=17 they also satisfy the ordinary product-of-top-singular-
values Lipschitz constraint product_l s_{1,l}>=sqrt(2) for this map.

Hence the collection of all centered single-layer rank-one truncation
inequalities (2), the singular-value order constraints, and the global
Lipschitz product lower bound cannot by themselves force R_infinity>=2.
The missing ingredient is consistency of the features and singular directions
across layers. The displayed spectral values are NOT a network representing f
and do NOT prove R_infinity=1. No lower bound stronger than the full problem's
known normalized lower endpoint follows asymptotically from this route alone.

For orientation, the right side of (4) is
L+log L+1-log 8+O((log L)^2/L). This expansion is not needed for the barrier:
the exact normalized expression already converges to 1 by taking logarithms.

## Checks and remaining step

The rank-one approximation uses a new bias so that prefix differences, rather
than unbounded activation magnitudes, enter the estimate. Every denominator
is positive because all layers have rank at least two. The scalar surrogate
may depend on the layer l, which is allowed in (1). Constraint multiplication
in the witness is deterministic algebra; no probabilistic independence is used.

scripts/check_truncation_barrier.py checks the witness constraints using exact
rational identities a_l^L=(L-1)/8, including L=2 and L=17, without approximating
an L-th root. The general argument is the algebra above, not a finite scan.

[Proposition 16 (Strict interior slack and row-general-position supremum) of arXiv:2608.26877, 'When Is the Sharp Covariance Envelope Tight? Feature-Only Geometry for Volume-Sampled Leas'] If $X$ is in row general position, $\lossstar>0$, $d\ge2$, and $d<s<m$, then
\begin{equation}
  M_s\prec\alpha\lossstar G^{-1}.
  
\end{equation}
For every fixed $(m,d,s)$ with $m>d$, $d\ge2$, and $d\le s<m$, row-general-position
perturbations $X^{(a)}\to X_0$ of the family
\eqref{eq:ue-attaining-family} can be chosen so that, with the same fixed
$y$,
\begin{equation}
  \left\lVert
    \frac{G_a^{1/2}M_{s,a}G_a^{1/2}}{\lossstar_a}-\alpha I_d
  \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
  
\end{equation}
Thus, for $d\ge2$ and $d<s<m$, the coefficient is not attained in row general
position but is its supremum.  At the rank-size endpoint $s=d$, the basis
identity already gives equality for every positive-loss row-general-position
design; at $s=m$ no normalized ratio is formed.

[Lemma 2 (Information equality for the ignoring estimator) of arXiv:2609.00774, 'Semi-Supervised Classification with Informative Missing Labels in Weibull Mixture Models'] Let
\[
 S_Y(\theta)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\log p_Y(Y;\theta),
 \qquad
 S_{Z\mid Y}(\theta)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\log p(Z\mid Y;\theta),
\]
and let
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{ig}}(\theta)
 =S_Y(\theta)+(1-M)S_{Z\mid Y}(\theta)
\]
be the score of $\ell_{\mathrm{ig},1}$. Under the conditional-independence assumption $M\perp Z\mid Y$ and the usual differentiability and moment conditions,
\begin{equation}
 -\E\left\{\frac{\partial\psi_{\mathrm{ig}}(\theta)}
 {\partial\theta^\top}\right\}
 =
 \E\{\psi_{\mathrm{ig}}(\theta)\psi_{\mathrm{ig}}(\theta)^\top\}
 =
 \J_{\mathrm{ig}}(\theta,\xi).
 
\end{equation}
If, in addition, $\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ig}}\xrightarrow{p}\theta$, $\J_{\mathrm{ig}}$ is nonsingular, and the standard local regularity conditions for M-estimation hold, then
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ig}}-\theta)
 \xrightarrow{d}
 N\!\left(0,\J_{\mathrm{ig}}^{-1}\right).
 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Information equality for the ignoring estimator

[Definition def:HNabelian of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $\cA$ be an abelian category with central charge $Z$.
A filtration
\[
0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\ldots\subset E_n=E
\]
of an object $E\in\cA$ is a \textbf{Harder--Narasimhan (HN) filtration} if $A_i\coloneqq E_i/E_{i-1}$ is non-zero and semistable for $i=1,\ldots,n$ with $\phi(A_1)>\phi(A_2)>\ldots>\phi(A_n)$.

The central charge $Z$ has the \textbf{Harder--Narasimhan (HN) property} if every object in $\cA$ has a Harder--Narasimhan filtration.
title: Definition def:HNabelian of arXiv:2609.00978

[Proposition L2 distances for X epsilon alpha of arXiv:2606.19207, 'Extrema of cooling branching Brownian motion and related Gaussian fields'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$. There exists $C>0$ such that, for every
	$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every $z_1,z_2\in[0,1]^d$ satisfying
	$\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{E}\bigl[(X_\varepsilon^\alpha(z_1)-X_\varepsilon^\alpha(z_2))^2\bigr]
		\leq
		C\,\vartheta_\alpha(\varepsilon)\,
		\frac{\lVert z_1-z_2\rVert_2}{\varepsilon},
	\end{equation}
	where $\vartheta_\alpha(\varepsilon):=\bigl(1+\log(1/\varepsilon)\bigr)^{-2\alpha}$.

[Proposition 23 (Finite-horizon stability of the first killed hit) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let
\[
    \sigma^\delta=\tau_A^\delta\wedge\tau_\calC^\delta,
    \qquad
    \sigma=\tau_A\wedge\tau_\calC .
\]
For $\pi^\eps$-almost every $z\in\Omega$ and every $M<\infty$, as
$\delta\downarrow0$,
\[
    \sigma^\delta\wedge M
    \Longrightarrow
    \sigma\wedge M .
\]
Moreover, as $\delta\downarrow0$,
\[
    \bfone_{\{\tau_A^\delta<\tau_\calC^\delta\}}
    \Longrightarrow
    \bfone_{\{\tau_A<\tau_\calC\}}
    \qquad\text{under }\Pbb_z .
\]
The same statement holds for the adjoint processes.

body:
[Lemma equiv-spectra-vs-gl-spectra of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Any $G$-equivariant weak equivalence between equivariantly cofibrant orthogonal $G$-spectra is a $G$-global weak equivalence. Moreover, the inclusion induces a fully faithful functor $i\colon{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G\simeq{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G^\textup{cof}\hookrightarrow{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{$G$-gl}$, and this admits a right adjoint, which is a localization at the $G$-equivariant weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
        The first claim is immediate from Proposition~(prop:restr-left-Quillen-G-Sp of the paper) together with Ken Brown's Lemma. 
        For the second claim, we fix a functorial cofibrant replacement $\varepsilon\colon Q\to\textup{id}$ for the $G$-equivariant model structure on $\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$. By $2$-out-of-$3$, a map $f$ is a $G$-equivariant weak equivalence if and only if $Qf$ is a $G$-equivariant or equivalently (by the above) a $G$-global weak equivalence. In particular, the full subcategory ${\mathcal{C}}\subset\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ of those objects for which $\varepsilon_X\colon QX\to X$ is a \emph{$G$-global} weak equivalence is itself closed under $G$-global weak equivalences. Thus, [g-global]*{Proposition~A.1.15} shows that the inclusion of ${\mathcal{C}}$ remains fully faithful after localizing both sides at the $G$-global weak equivalences. As on the other hand the inclusion of equivariantly cofibrant objects into ${\mathcal{C}}$ admits a homotopy inverse (namely, $Q$), this shows that the map ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_G^\textup{cof}\to{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G$-gl}$ induced by the inclusion is indeed fully faithful.

        We will now show that $Q$ defines a right adjoint to this map; as we have already seen that it precisely inverts the $G$-equivariant weak equivalences, this will then complete the proof of the lemma. For the claim it suffices to show that $\varepsilon$ exhibits $Q$ as an idempotent comonad on ${\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\text{$G$-gl}$, i.e.\ that for every $X\in\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ the two maps $Q\varepsilon_X,\varepsilon_{QX}\colon QX\rightrightarrows QQX$ are $G$-global weak equivalences. This follows at once from them being \emph{$G$-equivariant} weak equivalences between equivariantly cofibrant objects by construction.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lmm smdef of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] Let \(p\in(0,1)\) and \(\theta\ge 0\). Define
\[
\mathfrak{v}_{\theta,p}(x)
:=
\theta x^2
-x\log\frac{x}{p}
-(1-x)\log\frac{1-x}{1-p},
\qquad x\in[0,1],
\]
where here and throughout, we use the convention $0\log 0:=0$.

If $(\theta,p) \in \Omega$, where
 \begin{align}
\Omega
:=
([0,\infty)\times(0,1))
\setminus
\left\{
\left(\log\frac{1-p}{p},p\right):
0<p<\frac1{1+e^2}
\right\},\end{align}

then \(\mathfrak{v}_{\theta,p}\) has a unique maximizer on \([0,1]\), denoted by $s_{\theta,p}$. Consequently, the map $(\theta,p)\mapsto s_{\theta,p}$ is well-defined on $\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 20 (Local spatial regularity) of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] Assume \textnormal{(A1)-(A4)}. Let $D\in\mathfrak D$, $\omega\in\Omega_0$ and $R>0$. Then there exist a time $T=T(D,\omega)\geq2$, independent of $R$, a finite random constant $C_R(\omega)>0$ and a deterministic constant $C_R^P>0$ such that, for all $t\geq T$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $(x,\mu)\in D(\theta_{-t}\omega)$,
	\begin{align}
		\left\|
		\varphi_H^\epsilon
		(t,\theta_{-t}\omega,x,\mu)
		\right\|_{H^1(B_R)}^2
		\leq C_R(\omega),
	\end{align}
	and
	\begin{align}
		\int_H\|y\|_{H^1(B_R)}^2
		\big[\varphi_P^\epsilon(t)\mu\big](dy)
		\leq C_R^P.
	\end{align}
	In \eqref{Le7-2}, the local $H^1$-norm is understood as an extended Borel functional on $H$, equal to $+\infty$ outside $H^1(B_R)$. In particular, the terminal state belongs to $H^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R^n)$ and the terminal law is concentrated on $H^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R^n)$.

second branch do not decompose undifferentiated full-centered deposits
$\mathsf C_{v_s}$ before equal-time fusion and fixed-column packetization.
At the root-fused allocation step resolve only vertices of unpreassigned
ordinary mobile fixed-column packets as in (eq:3.4.1x-7f of the paper); deposits assigned

complete derivative/status orbit and its reflection before taking an

\]

[Definition def:osi of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] {CamanoEtAl2025}}]

Fix integers $r \le k \le n$ and a parameter $\alpha \in (0,1]$. A random  $n\times k$ matrix $S$
is \emph{$(r,\alpha)$-OSI} if it satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1)] \emph{Isotropy:} for every vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$,
    \[
        \mathbb{E} \|S^\top x\|_2^2 = \|x\|_2^2.
    \]
    \item[(2)] \emph{Injectivity:} for every fixed $r$-dimensional subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, with probability at least $9/10$,
    \[
        \alpha \|x\|_2^2 \le \|S^\top x\|_2^2
        \qquad \forall x \in V.
    \]
\end{itemize}
The probability $9/10$ in the second condition
can be replaced with another number close to one.

[Corollary 9 (Critical learning rate of Nesterov) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] There exists a unique critical learning rate satisfying
\[
\kappa_{\nesterov}
\bigl(\eta_{\nesterov}^{\crit},\rho\bigr)
=1
\]
before the local stability boundary. The Nesterov iteration is risk stable if and only if
\[
0<\eta<\eta_{\nesterov}^{\crit}.
\]
Under the power-law and high-momentum assumptions
\(
\lambda_i\eqsim i^{-\beta},
\beta>1,
B\gg1,
1-\rho\ll1,
\)
\begin{equation}

\eta_{\nesterov}^{\crit}
\eqsim
\min\{1,B^\beta(1-\rho)\}.
\end{equation}

[Corollary 46 of arXiv:2506.15044, '2506.15044'] Let $H\in \mathcal{P}^\mathbb{C}$ and $X\in \mathcal{S}^\mathbb{C}$.
Then the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
  \item[$(i)$] $H\in\mathcal{L}^\mathbb{C}(X)$.
  \item[$(ii)$] There exist a coupled predictable process $\widetilde{H}$ for $H\in\mathcal{P}^\mathbb{C}$ and an FCS $(T_n,X^{(n)})$ for $X\in \mathcal{S}^\mathbb{C}$ such that $\widetilde{H}\in\mathcal{L}(X^{(n)})$ for each $n\in \mathbf{N}^+$.
  \item[$(iii)$] There exist an FCS $(T_n,H^{(n)})$ for $H\in\mathcal{P}^\mathbb{B}$ and an FCS $(T_n,X^{(n)})$ for $X\in \mathcal{S}^\mathbb{C}$ such that  $H^{(n)}\in\mathcal{L}(X^{(n)})$ for each $n\in \mathbf{N}^+$.
  \item[$(iv)$] There exist an FS $(\tau_n)$ for $\mathbb{C}$ such that $H^{\tau_n}\in\mathcal{L}(X^{\tau_n})$ for each $n\in \mathbf{N}^+$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 17 (Vanishing diagonal regularization) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(\widetilde H\) be a bounded centered array with zero diagonal and an
exactly stochastic, uniformly flat off-diagonal variance matrix
\(\widetilde S\).  Let \(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_N\) be independent, centered,
variance-one, uniformly bounded random variables, independent of
\(\widetilde H\).  For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ij}
 :=\sqrt{1-\eta/N}\,\widetilde H_{ij}\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ii}:=\sqrt{\eta/N}\,\chi_i.
\end{equation}
Then the variance matrix of \(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) is exactly stochastic
and satisfies the uniform lower and upper bounds required by the
generalized-Wigner theorem, with constants allowed to depend on \(\eta\).
For every finite family of functions analytic near \(\Gamma\),
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|
 \E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right|&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta,
 \\
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\Var\!\left(
 \Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right)&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta.
 
\end{align}
Moreover, the Li--Xu expectation and covariance formulas converge to their flat
zero-diagonal versions in the order \(N\to\infty\), then
\(\eta\downarrow0\).  Consequently the joint CLT for
\(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) transfers to \(\widetilde H\).

[Theo 17 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] Let $(\nu_h)\in {\cal M} ( \gamma , \R^{2n} )$  with $\gamma <0$. Suppose that  the function 
  $\varphi $ in  (\ref{Four-mes}) is a quadratic form, namely,
  
   \be \varphi (u) = - \frac  {1}  {2} 
     \sum _{jk} a_{jk} u_j u_k = - \frac  {1}  {2}  (Au ) \cdot  u , \ee 
    
  where   $A=(a_{ij})$ is a symmetric  matrix with a   definite positive 
  real part.   Then, 
  
  
  i) We have for every  $F$ and  $G$ in  $ D_{\lambda h}(\R^{2n})$ 
  (with large enough $\lambda $),
   
  $$ F \sharp _h ^{\nu_h} G = R e^{h L^{\nu}(D)} (F \otimes G) ,$$
  
 where  $L^{\nu}$ is a quadratic form whose matrix also denoted by 
  $L^{\nu}$ is written as,
  
  \be 
    L^{\nu} =  \frac  {1}  {2} 
     \begin{pmatrix} 0 & B +  A   \\  B^T +  A  &  0  \end{pmatrix} 
    ,\quad B  = - \frac  {1}  {2} 
       \begin{pmatrix} 1 & i \\ -i &   1 \end{pmatrix}.  \ee 
       
       
       ii) For any  $F\in  D_{\lambda h}(\R^{2n})$
  (with $\lambda $ sufficiently large), we have the estimates, 
  
   $$ \frac {h^m}  {m!} \Vert ( L^{\nu}(D)) ^m F \Vert_{ D_{  h }( \R^{2n})} 
  \leq  \frac {C^{m+1}}  {(\lambda - 1) ^m}
  \Vert  F \Vert_{ D_{\lambda  h }( \R^{2n})}. $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 (Series reduction) of arXiv:2609.02080, 'Logarithmic basis number of graphs'] Let $v$ be a degree-two vertex incident with two distinct non-loop edges $uv$ and $vw$, where possibly $u=w$.  Let $G'$ be obtained by suppressing $v$ and replacing those two edges by one edge $uw$ (a loop if $u=w$).  Then
\[
    \bn(G')=\bn(G)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \beta(G')=\beta(G).
\]

[Lemma Ll of arXiv:2608.02897, 'Local limit theorem and Edgeworth expansions for inhomogeneous random walks on $GL(d,\bbR)'] For all $0<\delta_0<T$
there exists $L\in\mathbb N$ such that,
$$
\sup_{\delta_0\leq |t|\leq T}\sup_j\|\mathcal L_{j,it}^L\|_*<1.
$$
As a consequence, there are $C,c>0$ that may depend on $\delta_0$ and $T$ such that
$$
\sup_{\delta_0\leq |t|\leq T}\|\mathcal L_{0,it}^n\|_*\leq Ce^{-cn}.
$$

[Lemma 203 (Commuting $\upmu$-weighted Cartesian derivatives with the geometric vectorfields) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $1 \leq N \leq \Ntop$.
Then the following commutator estimates hold on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
\begin{align}
\begin{split} 
	& 
	\left| [\upmu \partial_i, \tander^N] (\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt) \right|,

	\fundbootsmall \upmu |\tander^{[1,N]} \velocityarray| 
	+ 
	\fundbootsmall |\tandersmall^{[1,N]} \badcontrolvars|. 
\end{split}
\end{align}

[Theorem thm:fin-add-price-chain of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be a gamble space.
  For all measurable $X:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    
    \sup_{Q\in\Delta_{0,f}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_Q X
    \leq
    \sup_{Q\in\Delta_f(\Omega)} \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_Q[ X - Z]
    \leq
    \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \sup_{Q\in\Delta_f(\Omega)} \mathbb{E}_Q[ X - Z]
    =
    \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X~.
  \end{equation}
  If $X$ is additionally bounded, the first inequality is an equality when  $\mathcal{Z}$ is upward-scalable and contains zero, and the second when $\mathrm{dcl}(\mathcal{Z})$ is convex.

[Proposition prop:HOMFLY width 1 of arXiv:2608.29986, 'Khovanov-Rozansky homology over $\F[U,V]$'] Let $K \subset S^3$ be a knot and $\widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ its reduced Khovanov-Rozansky homology. If the Rasmussen's $\mathfrak{sl}_1$ spectral sequence from $\widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathbb{F}} $ collapses after the first differential $d_1$, then $\mathit{CH}(K)$ splits as a direct sum of
\begin{itemize}[label=$-$]
    \item $C(1, -1, \dots, 1, -1)$ or $C(-1, 1, \dots, -1, 1)$, and
    \item some $1 \times 1$ squares.
\end{itemize}
One of the sides of each $1 \times 1$ square is decorated with a $-1$ and all other arrows are decorated with a $1$.

[Lemma calc of arXiv:2412.08334, 'Maker-Breaker on Galton-Watson trees'] Let $(S_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ be a left-continuous random walk with positive drift and $\pi_{-1}>0$, started in $S_0=0$.

body:
[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2608.26259, 'Cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for Potts Glauber Dynamics\\on lattice at High Temperature'] Fix \(\lambda_0>0\). There exist
constants \(C<\infty\), \(K<\infty\), and \(\theta_0\in(0,1)\), depending only on
\(d,q,\lambda_0\), such that the following holds.

Let \(A\subset\Lambda\) be finite and nonempty, let \(X\) be a compatible outside history with \(h=\ell_A(X)\). Let \(\sigma\) be a \([0,T]\cup\{\infty\}\)-valued stopping time for \((\widehat{\mathscr F}_u^A)\). Construct the non-coalescing branching envelope on the same probability space, and assume that \(\sigma\) is also a stopping time for its filtration.
Assume that, on \(\{\sigma<\infty\}\), one has \(\sigma\ge h\).

Let
\[
        L_s:=\int_0^s |\widehat{\mathcal H}_A(u)|\,du,
\]
and let \(\chi_s\) be the total spatial length of all spatial edges in the actual history up to backward time $s$. Let \(\mathcal C_s\) be the event that \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_A(s)\ne\varnothing\) and the truncated space--time history $\mathcal H_A\cap(\Lambda\times[T-s,T])$ is connected.

Then for every \(0<\theta\le\theta_0\), with \(\gamma=c_{\mathrm{cone}}^{-1}\theta\), there exists $\beta_0(\theta)$ such that, for all $\beta<\beta_0$, for every \(a\in(0,1-K\beta)\),
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb E
\left[
\mathbf 1_{\{\sigma<\infty\}}\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C_\sigma}
e^{a\sigma}
e^{\theta(L_\sigma-\sigma)+\gamma\chi_\sigma}
\,\middle|\,
\mathcal U_A(X)
\right]
\le
C e^{-\lambda_0 W(A)}
e^{-(1-K\beta-a)h}.
\end{equation*}

			[f]_{W^{r,p}(0,T)}^p,
			\qquad
			t,t'\in[0,T].
		\end{equation*}

[Lemma lem:covering_number_in_jin of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] Let $\mathcal V$ denote a class of functions of the form
\[
V(\cdot)=\min\Bigl\{\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\bigl[w^\top\phi(\cdot,a)+\beta\sqrt{\phi(\cdot,a)^\top\Lambda^{-1}\phi(\cdot,a)}\bigr],H\Bigr\},
\]
where the parameters satisfy $\|w\|_2\le L$, $\beta\in[0,B]$, and $\lambda_{\min}(\Lambda)\ge \lambda$.
Assume $\|\phi(x,a)\|_2\le 1$ for all $(x,a)$.
Let $\mathcal N_\epsilon$ be the $\epsilon$-covering number of $\mathcal V$ under
$\mathrm{dist}(V,V')=\sup_x|V(x)-V'(x)|$.
Then
\[
\log \mathcal N_\epsilon
\le d\log\Bigl(1+\frac{4L}{\epsilon}\Bigr)
+d^2\log\Bigl(1+\frac{8\sqrt d\,B^2}{\lambda\epsilon^2}\Bigr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covering-number bound for optimistic value functions, Lemma D.6 in \cite{jin2020provably}

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Consider the situation of Lemma \ref{allinvariantmeasures0}. The following are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $G=\mathbf{P}_1$ is Hurwitz (so that $S$ is negative definite), and $\mu$ is an infinitesimally invariant measure for $\big (L^{A,\mathbf{P}}, C_0^{\infty}(\R^2)\big )$. 
\item[(b)] $\mu$ is a finite invariant measure for the semigroup associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,\mathbf{P}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ and its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}. 
\end{itemize}
Moreover, in either case (a) or (b), the following hold: 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
$\mu$ is the (up to a multiplicative constant) the unique finite invariant measure for the semigroup mentioned in (b), and the unique finite infinitesimally invariant measure for  $(L^{A,\mathbf{P}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2))$.
\item[(ii)]
If $\alpha_{2,0}\not =-\frac{\beta_{2,1}}{2}$ or $\beta_{2,2} \not=-\frac{\alpha_{2,1}}{2}$, then there is no SOHHD for $\tilde{\mathbf{P}}$.
\item[(iii)]
If $\alpha_{2,0}=-\frac{\beta_{2,1}}{2}$ and $\beta_{2,2} =-\frac{\alpha_{2,1}}{2}$ then
\eqref{OHHD2dim} is the unique OHHD for $\tilde{\mathbf{P}}$.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem 7 (van den Berg) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that $D$ is simply connected and that $\partial D$ is Minkowski nondegenerate with
Minkowski dimension $\msf d_M(\partial D)\in[1,2)$. That is,
\[0<\liminf_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}\leq
\limsup_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}<\infty,\]
where we define
\[\partial D_r=\left\{x\in\mbb R^2:\inf_{y\in\partial D}|x-y|<r\right\}.\]
There exists constants $c\in(1,\infty)$ and $\th>0$ such that
\begin{align}

c^{-1}t^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2}\leq\msf{A}(D)-\msf M_0(t)\leq ct^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2},\qquad t\in(0,\th).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For an odd prime p and integer a, the Legendre symbol (a/p) is 0 if p | a, +1 if a is a nonzero quadratic residue mod p (some x^2 = a), and -1 if a is a quadratic nonresidue. Euler's criterion gives (a/p) = a^{(p-1)/2} mod p; the symbol is completely multiplicative in a. It is the object of the law of quadratic reciprocity and generalizes to the Jacobi symbol for composite lower arguments.
title: Legendre Symbol

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

\]
Futhermore,  there exists a saddle-point $(\hat\lambda_{t},\hat\tau_{t})\in \mathcal{M}_{t,T} \times \mathcal{M}_{t,T}$,
\[
\hat\lambda_{t}:=\min\Big\{T,\inf\Big\{a\in[t,T)|Y(a)=U(a)\Big\}\Big\}, \]
\[
\hat\tau_{t}:=\min\Big\{T,\inf\Big\{a\in[t,T)|Y(a)=L(a)\Big\}\Big\},
\]
that is,
\[
\mathbb E\left[R_{t}(\hat\lambda_{t},\tau ) \mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right]\leq\mathbb E\left[R_{t}(\hat\lambda_{t},\hat\tau_{t} ) \mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right]=Y(t)\leq\mathbb E\left[ R_{t}(\lambda,\hat\tau_{t})\mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right],\; a.s.,
\]
for point $(\lambda,\tau)$ in $\mathcal{M}_{t,T} \times \mathcal{M}_{t,T}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2609.03881, 'Eulerian insertion operators and an Eulerian form of the Pieri rule'] Let \(\boldsymbol m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\) have total size \(N\), and set
$h_{\boldsymbol m}=h_{m_1}\cdots h_{m_n}$.

\begin{equation}
 h_{\boldsymbol m}
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_{\boldsymbol m}}
   F_{N,\Des(\pi)},
 \qquad
 \Phi_N(h_{\boldsymbol m})
 =\Hom_{\boldsymbol m}(x,y).
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every permutation \(\sigma\) of \([n]\),
$\Hom_{\boldsymbol m}(x,y)
 =\G_{m_{\sigma(n)}}\cdots
  \G_{m_{\sigma(1)}}(x)$.

body:
[Lemma lem:row-bounds-short of arXiv:2608.05123, 'A central limit theorem for the random assignment problem'] If \(R=\osc U\le(n-2)/4\), then uniformly in \(i\),
\[
 \left\|\frac{\,\mathrm d\mathcal L(D_i\mid U)}{\,\mathrm d d}\right\|_\infty\le C,
 \qquad c\le\Var(D_i\mid U)\le C(R+1)^2,
\]
and for fixed \(p\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E(|D_i-\mathbb E(D_i\mid U)|^p\mid U)\le C_p(R+1)^p,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(D_i\ge R+s\mid U)\le Ce^{-s/2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every \(M\), some \(B_M\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbb P_n^{\mathrm{ref}}}\{R+\max_iD_i>B_M\log n\}\le C_Mn^{-M}.
\end{equation}

Let $(D, \phi, a_1, a_2, a_3)$ be an embedding of $S_0$. For each $i \in I$, identify the first marked point of $S_i$ with the vertex $a_i$ of $S_0$, and forget this marked point. Let $S$ be the resulting three-pointed quantum surface. }

body: [Theorem 2.6 (Maximum–entropy characterisation) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$, latent positions $U=(U_{i})_{i=1}^{n}\in(0,1)^{n}$, and a finite index set $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathbb{N}_{0}\times\mathbb{N}_{0}$. Let $\Omega:=\{0,1\}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ and identify $A\in\Omega$ with an undirected adjacency matrix by setting $A_{ji}:=A_{ij}$ and $A_{ii}:=0$. Using the statistics $S_{00}(A)$ and $S_{rs}(A,U)$ defined in Section 2.4, fix target moments $m_{00}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $(m_{rs})_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}$ and define $\mathcal{Q}(m):=\Bigl\{Q\text{ pmf on }\Omega:\;\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00},\;\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}\ \ \forall(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}\Bigr\}.$ Assume $\mathcal{Q}(m)\neq\varnothing$. (i) Existence and uniqueness. There exists a unique maximiser $Q^{\star}\in\mathcal{Q}(m)$ of Shannon entropy $H(Q):=-\sum_{A\in\Omega}Q(A)\log Q(A),$ where $\log$ is the natural logarithm and $0\log 0:=0$. (ii) Exponential-family characterisation (attainable moments). For $\theta=(c,(s_{rs})_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}})$ define $P_{\theta}(A\mid U):=\exp\Bigl\{c\,S_{00}(A)+\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)-\Psi_{n}(\theta;U)\Bigr\},$ with $\Psi_{n}(\theta;U):=\log\sum_{A\in\Omega}\exp\Bigl\{c\,S_{00}(A)+\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)\Bigr\}.$ If there exists $\theta^{\star}$ such that $P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid U)\in\mathcal{Q}(m)$ (equivalently, $\mathbb{E}_{\theta^{\star}}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00}$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\theta^{\star}}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}$ for all $(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}$), then $Q^{\star}=P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid U).$ In particular, if one restricts $\theta$ to the WL–ERG subfamily (e.g. by imposing symmetry constraints inherited from a symmetric coefficient matrix), then any moment-matching WL–ERG member must coincide with $Q^{\star}$ and hence is the unique maximum–entropy distribution under the constraints. The maximising distribution is always unique; the canonical parameter $\theta^{\star}$ is unique whenever the exponential family is minimal.

body:
[Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.22156, ''] $(1)$. If $S_4$ is filled then $p_6(x)\geq \frac{1}{6}$ for $x\in [0,3^{m}/2]\times \{0\}$.

$(2)$. If $S_4$ is unfilled then $p_6(x)\geq \frac{\mu_0(S_1)}{6(\mu_0(S_1)+\mu_0(S_4))}$ for $x\in [0,3^{m}/2]\times \{0\}$.
  \begin{proof}
$(1)$.  Set $S=\inf\{t>0,W_t\in\{3^{m}/2\}\times [0,3^{m}]\}$. Then 
\begin{align*} 
P^x(W_T\in L_1)&=P^x(W_T\in L_1,S<T)\\
&=E^x[P^{W_S}(W_T\in L_1);S<T]\\
&=E^x[P^{W_S}(W_T\in L_6);S<T]\\
&\leq P^x(W_T\in L_6).
\end{align*}
So $p_1\leq p_6$, similarly $p_2\leq p_5,\ p_3\leq p_4$. 

Next, we set $R_0=0$, and 
\begin{align*} 
V_i&=\inf\{t>R_i,W_t\in [0,3^{m}]\times \{3^{m}/2\}\}\quad\hbox{ for }i\geq 0,\\ R_i&=\inf\{t>V_{i-1};\ W_t\in[0,3^{m}]\times\{0\}\}\quad\hbox{ for }i\geq 1. 
\end{align*}  
Then $p_6=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}P^x(W_T\in L_6,\ R_i<T<R_{i+1})$, and by the strong Markov property,
\begin{align}
    p_5&=\sum_{i=0}^\infty P^x(W_T\in L_5,\ R_i<T<R_{i+1})\nonumber\\ 
    &=\sum_{i=0}^\infty P^x(W_T\in L_5,\ V_i<T<R_{i+1})\nonumber\\
    &=\sum_{i=0}^\infty E^x[P^{W_{V_i}}(W_T\in L_5,\ T<R_1);\ V_i<T]\nonumber\\
    &=\sum_{i=0}^\infty E^x[P^{W_{V_i}}(W_T\in L_6,\ T<R_1);\ V_i<T]\nonumber\\
    &=\sum_{i=0}^\infty P^x(W_T\in L_6;V_i<T<R_{i+1})\leq p_6.
    \end{align}
 Similarly, $p_4\leq p_5$ by applying the reflection symmetry about the diagonal connecting $(0,3^{m})$ and $(3^{m},0)$. 

To conclude, we proved $p_6\geq p_5\geq p_4$ and $p_4+p_5+p_6\geq p_1+p_2+p_3$, hence 
\[
p_6\geq \frac13\sum_{i=4}^6p_i\geq\frac{1}{6}\sum_{i=1}^6p_i=\frac16.
\]

For $(2)$, set $f=\mathds{1}_{L_6}$ be the indicator function of $L_6$ on $\partial_o (S_1\cup S_4)$ in Lemma \ref{lemma3.2} and use $(1)$ above, 
\[
p_6(x)=P^x(W_T\in L_6)=\frac{\mu_0(S_1)}{\mu_0(S_1)+\mu_0(S_4)}P^x(X(\mathcal{T}_{\partial_o S_1-\{y=0\}})\in L_6)\geq \frac{\mu_0(S_1)}{6(\mu_0(S_1)+\mu_0(S_4))}.
\]
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Question 5 of Hu and Sun's survey on Hunt's hypothesis (H) (arXiv:1908.06825) asks whether every pure-jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfies (H). The classical sufficient conditions bound Im psi by a multiple of 1 + Re psi; the oldest, Kanda-Forst, asks |Im psi(z)| <= M (1 + Re psi(z)) for all z. The driftless subordinator with Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}, x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}, has sum a_m x_m = 1 and sum a_m = infinity, and along z_m = 1/(m x_m) its exponent psi(z) = int (1 - e^{izx}) nu(dx) satisfies |Im psi(z_m)| / (1 + Re psi(z_m)) = 4m + O(1) (computed at high precision: 23.999 at m = 6, 32.000008 at m = 8), so the Kanda-Forst ratio is unbounded and the classical route to (H) is closed for it. It is not a counterexample to (H): an octave-by-octave estimate of the Kesten-Bretagnolle integral int Re(1/(1 + psi(z))) dz suggests the integral diverges, so points would be polar - a heuristic, not a proof. The example is atomic, outside the survey's type-(alpha, beta) density class, and the survey's Theorem 2.8 and Remark 2.21 anticipate processes of this kind, so it is an explicit witness with a computed rate rather than a new phenomenon.

[Definition Interval extension of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For the remainder of this section, an \textit{interval} is a closed interval with rational endpoints. An \textit{interval enclosure} of a variable $x$ is an interval $[x] := [\underline{x},\overline{x}] \ni x$. Its width is \(\operatorname{wd}([x])=\overline{x}-\underline{x}\). 
    For a real function $F(x_1,\dots,x_m)$, a function $[F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m])$ is said to be an \textit{interval extension} of $F$ if
    \[
        x_j\in[x_j]\quad (1\le j\le m)
        \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
        F(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in [F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m]).
    \]
    Interval extensions also naturally define operations on intervals. For example,
    \[
    I+J=[\underline I+\underline J,\overline I+\overline J],
    \qquad
    I/c=[\underline I/c,\overline I/c]\quad(c>0).
    \]
    We henceforth implicitly assume all interval operations are performed with ``outward'' rounding (lower endpoints rounded downward and upper endpoints upward) to maintain rationality of the endpoints.
title: Interval extension

[Theorem 5 (Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] For every \(C_0\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C=C(C_0)\) with the following property. Let
\[
A_i=B_i+L_i,
\qquad
i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
be self-adjoint matrices. Assume that \(B_i\in\mathcal A\) for a finite-dimensional \(C^*\)-algebra \(\mathcal A\) satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A\le C_0n$, and assume $\|B_i\|\le 1$, $\|L_i\|\le 1$, and $\|L_i\|_F^2\le \frac{n}{\log^3(en)}$ for every \(i\in[n]\). Then, there exist signs \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{\pm1\}\) such that
\[
\Bigl\|
\nlsum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i
\Bigr\|
\le
C(C_0)\sqrt n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families

\]

body:
[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $L\subset M_{n,m}(\R)$ and $K\subset \R^n$ be compact sets of positive volume whose convex hulls contain the (appropriate) origin in their interiors. Then, 
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n]((K^{\star,Q})_{\circ,Q})^m 
    \] 
    and 
    \[ 
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((L_{\circ,Q})^{\star,Q})\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m,
    \]
    with equality only for invariant sets (up to sets of Lebesgue measure zero). 
    
    In particular, the following two statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $K$ or $K^\circ$, has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m 
    \]
    with equality if and only if $K=E$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets; 
    \item  if $L_{\circ,Q}$ or $(L_{\circ,Q})^\circ$ has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m
    \]
    with equality if and only if $L=E^{\star,Q}$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset \R^n$ up to removal of null sets.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma Lanti of arXiv:2510.12480, 'Cyclic and alternating $U$-statistics'] Let $f\in L^2({\mathcal X}\times{\mathcal X})$ be real and antisymmetric.
The the operator $T_f$ on $L^2_{\mathbb C}({\mathcal X})$
is anti-self-adjoint and has purely imaginary eigenvalues.
Let $(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)_{q\in{\mathcal Q_+}}$ be an enumeration of the positive real numbers
such that\/ 
$\mathrm{i}\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q$ is an eigenvalue of $T_f$ (counted with multiplicities).
Then the multiset of nonzero eigenvalues $(\lambda_r)_1^R$
of the self-adjoint operator $T_{{\widehat{f}}}$ on
$L^2({\mathcal X}\times\ensuremath{[0,1]})$ (counted with multiplicities)
 equals
\begin{align}
\Bigset{\pm\frac{2}{(2k-1)\pi}\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q:q\in{\mathcal Q_+},k\in\mathbb N}\quad
\text{with each  pair $(q,k)$ counted twice.}
\end{align}

As a consequence, if $\zeta_r$ are i.i.d\xperiod{} standard normal variables and
$\eta_q$ are independent random variables with the stochastic area
distribution (equation area of the paper), then
\begin{align}
  \sum_{r=1}^R \tfrac12\lambda_r(\zeta_r^2-1) \overset{\mathrm{d}}{=} \sum_{q\in{\mathcal Q_+}} \lambda^{\mathsf a}_q\eta_q.
\end{align}
Furthermore,
\begin{align}
  \sum_{r=1}^R\lambda_r^2
=2\sum_{q=1}^{Q_+}(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)^2
= \int_{{\mathcal X}^2}f(x,y)^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu(x)\,\mathrm{d}\nu(y)
<\infty
.\end{align}

body:
[Lemma strong-approximations of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Assume the conditions of Lemma~(lemma:LIL of the paper) hold. If $ \mathbb{E}[x(1)^{\alpha}] < \infty $ for some $ \alpha > 2 $, then there exist two standard Brownian motions $ \check{B}' $ and $ \check{B}'' $ such that
	\[
	\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{1/\alpha}} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big\vert \sum_{i = 1}^{\lfloor t \rfloor} x(i) - t - c_{x} \check{B}'(t)\Big\vert \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{1/\alpha}} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \vert N(t) - t - c_{x} \check{B}''(t) \vert \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} 0.
	\]
	If $ \mathbb{E}[\exp(t x(1))] < \infty $ in a neighborhood of $ t = 0 $, then there exists a positive number $ C_{x} $ such that
	\begin{align*}
		\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log T} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big\vert \sum_{i = 1}^{\lfloor t \rfloor} x(i) - t - c_{x} \check{B}'(t)\Big\vert & \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{<} C_{x},\\
		\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log T} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \vert N(t) - t - c_{x} \check{B}''(t) \vert & \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{<} C_{x}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma strong-approximations of arXiv:2505.04942

body:
[Theorem thm:existenceweaksolutions of arXiv:2608.16946, 'A diffusion model for time-dependent compositional data'] The SDEs (equation canonicalSDE of the paper), (equation adjustedSDE of the paper), and (equation truncatedSDE of the paper) have weak
solutions. Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}
\renewcommand{\alph{enumi}}{\alph{enumi}}

\item Given a probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with support contained in $\mathcal{S}$, there exist weak
solutions for SDEs  (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper) such that $X(0)$ has the 
prescribed distribution, and $X(t)\in\bar\mathcal{S}$ for all $t\geq0$, $P$-a.s.
\item Given a probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$ with support contained in $\mathcal{S}^-$, there exists a weak
solution for SDE (equation truncatedSDE of the paper) such that $X^-(0)$ has the 
prescribed distribution, and $X^-(t)\in\bar\mathcal{S}^-$ for all $t\geq0$, $P$-a.s.
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, these solutions are unique in distribution, and they are equivalent, in the sense that:
\begin{enumerate}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\renewcommand{\alph{enumi}}{\alph{enumi}}

\item Any weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) is a solution for (equation adjustedSDE of the paper) and viceversa.
\item If $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X(t)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ is a weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper),
then $((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\allowbreak\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X^-(t))$ is a weak solution for (equation truncatedSDE of the paper).
\item If $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X^-(t)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ is a weak solution for (equation truncatedSDE of the paper),
then $((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},\allowbreak W(t),X^+(t))$ is a weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:existenceweaksolutions of arXiv:2608.16946

[Corollary of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{cor:anchored_isop_dim}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J: V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d\alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (1,2)$.
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$. 
    
    Then the infinite cluster $K_{\infty}$ has anchored isoperimetric dimension at least $1/(\alpha-1)$ almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered corollary of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $\gamma\in \R, \gamma > 0$ be fixed. Let $0 < \alpha < 1$. Then
		\begin{align}
			&\JS_{G_{\alpha}}^{\gamma}(\mu_0||\mu_1) \geq 0 \;\;\forall \mu_0,\mu_1 \in \Gauss(\Hcal),
			\\
			&\JS_{G_{\alpha}}^{\gamma}(\mu_0||\mu_1) = 0 \equivalent \mu_0 = \mu_1 \equivalent m_0 = m_1, C_0 = C_1.
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2506.10494

body: [Proposition Prop:asymp of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] The line $v+t_0$ is an asymptote of the time constant function, i.e.\ $\lim_{v \to \infty} \Lambda(v)-v-t_0=0$. If $G$ have an atom at $t_0(G)$, then we even have $\Lambda(v)=v+t_0$ for all $v\ge  (1-G(t_0))/G(t_0)$.

	\[
		\lim_{L\to\infty} \frac{\#\{[\gamma] \in \Pi(L) : |\val_f(\gamma)-\alpha_f| < \varepsilon\}}{\#\Pi(L)} =1.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let $p \in (1, \infty)$ and $N \in \N$. Let $0 \leq \xi_N(x) \leq 1$ be a sequence of finitely supported functions on $\Z$, such that 
$$\xi_N (x)  \rightarrow 1, \quad x \in \Z, \quad \operatorname{and} \quad \sup_{N \in \N} \mathcal{M}_{p, \sigma, \alpha}(\xi_N) < \infty.$$ 
Then there exists a finitely supported sequence $0 \leq e_N (x) \leq 1$, converging pointwise to $1$, such that 
$$
\mathcal{M}_{p, \sigma, \alpha} (e_N) \rightarrow 0 \quad \text{as} \quad N \rightarrow \infty.

body: In probability theory and mathematical physics, a random matrix is a matrix-valued random variable—that is, a matrix in which some or all of its entries are sampled randomly from a probability distribution. Random matrix theory (RMT) is the study of properties of random matrices, often as they become large. RMT provides techniques like mean-field theory, diagrammatic methods, the cavity method, or the replica method to compute quantities like traces, spectral densities, or scalar products between eigenvectors. Many physical phenomena, such as the spectrum of nuclei of heavy atoms, the thermal conductivity of a lattice, or the emergence of quantum chaos, can be modeled mathematically as problems concerning large, random matrices.
title: Random matrix

body:
[Proposition 133 (Value-process compression on a nonlinear solver range) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let
\[
 \mathscr S_{\rm sol}\subset\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}
\]
be a closed, not necessarily linear, solver range invariant under the
first-jet truncations, and give
$\mathscr Y_{\rm sol}:=\pi_Y(\mathscr S_{\rm sol})$ the topology inherited
from $\mathbb S_{\cP}^2$.  The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item the restricted value projection
\[
 \pi_Y|_{\mathscr S_{\rm sol}}:
 \mathscr S_{\rm sol}\longrightarrow\mathscr Y_{\rm sol}
\]
is injective and has a stable-causal inverse;
\item there is a unique stable-causal map
\[
 \mathcal Z_{\rm sol}:\mathscr Y_{\rm sol}
 \longrightarrow\mathbb H_{\cP}^2
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr S_{\rm sol}
 =\{(Y,\mathcal Z_{\rm sol}(Y)):Y\in\mathscr Y_{\rm sol}\};
\end{equation}
\item the complete response restricted to $\mathscr S_{\rm sol}$ admits a
lossless realization on the value-process state with its inherited topology.
\end{enumerate}
If $\mathscr S_{\rm sol}$ is in addition a closed linear relation, these
conditions reduce to vanishing of its vertical space together with closedness
of its value domain.  Thus
\Cref{thm:backward-compression-retention} is the linear special case, not
an automatic criterion for a nonlinear solver image.  In particular, a fixed
nonlinear dynamics may admit continuous recovery on its own solution range
even when the ambient covariance differential is unbounded.

body:
Egorov's theorem states that on a FINITE measure space, almost everywhere convergence of measurable functions implies almost uniform convergence: for every eps > 0 there is a measurable E with mu(E) < eps such that the convergence is uniform on the complement of E. Finiteness cannot be dropped. On R with Lebesgue measure let f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}; then f_n -> 0 at every point, but for ANY set E of finite measure the complement meets [n, n+1] for infinitely many n, so sup over the complement of E of |f_n| equals 1 for infinitely many n and the convergence is not uniform off any set of small measure. What survives on a sigma-finite space is the LOCAL statement: for every measurable A with mu(A) < infinity and every eps > 0 there is E contained in A with mu(E) < eps and uniform convergence on A minus E; equivalently, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence on each set of finite measure. The converse implication holds in general: almost uniform convergence always implies convergence almost everywhere and in measure, on any measure space. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.33 and Exercise 2.39]
mu(Omega) < infinity for the global statement; a set of finite measure for the local statement
f_n measurable, f_n -> f mu-almost everywhere, all functions finite a.e.

body: Classical Schwarz lemma: if f maps the open unit disk holomorphically into itself and f(0)=0, then |f(z)|<=|z| and |f'(0)|<=1. Equality at a nonzero point or in the derivative bound forces f(z)=az with |a|=1. A distinct higher-dimensional result is Royden's Theorem1 (1980): let M be complete Kaehler with Ricci curvature at least k<=0, and N be Kaehler with holomorphic sectional curvature at most K<0. For a nonconstant holomorphic f:M->N, let nu be the maximal complex rank of df. In the paper's curvature convention, ||df||_op^2 <= Lambda(f) <= (2nu/(nu+1)) k/K, where Lambda(f)=trace_g(f*h) is the sum of squared singular values. Constant maps satisfy zero derivative directly. Trace energy and squared operator norm are distinct when rank exceeds one. This note does not assert the same conclusion for arbitrary Hermitian targets or remove the rank factor from the trace bound.

body:
[Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}=\{R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $1$, with drift $-\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$, for each $i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$.
We consider the O'Connell-Yor polymer partition function (see [OYbb]) across $\{\mathcal{B}_i\}_{i=1}^{2k}$, defined as
\[
Z_{\mathcal{B}}(x,i;y,j) = \idotsint_{x=x_i\le \cdots \le x_j \le x_{j+1}=y} \exp\left( \sum_{i'=i}^j \mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'+1})-\mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'}) \right) dx_{i+1}\cdots dx_j,
\]
for any $1\le i \le j \le 2k$, and $0\le x \le y$.

Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j\in\llbracketi, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of inverse gamma random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal{B}$, satisfying 
\[X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
1 & j =i,\\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_j-\gamma_i), \qquad &j\in\llbracket i + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i- \gamma_{2k + 1 -j}), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i+\alpha), \qquad &j =  2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
\[
R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in P[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; x, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in P[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x\ge 0,\\
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; |x|, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x< 0,
\end{cases}
\]
where $P[i,\ell]$ is the collection of all up-right paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(-i,i)$ to $(-1,\ell)$, and  
$\hat{P}[i,\ell]$ is the subset of such paths that intersect $\{(x,x+2k+1): x\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020

		\ee
		where $$T(f,h)=(\|h\|_{\mL^{\infty}([0,1])}+\|h\|_{\mH_{1,p}^{q}([0,1])})\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}.$$
		Particularly 
		\be 
		&&\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\int_{0}^{t}(f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(r,\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr|\|_{L_{\bar{p}(\Omega)}}\no\\
		&\leq &N\bigg\{\gamma_n(f)(1/n)^{1-\frac{1}{q}}+[(1/n)^{\alpha/2}+(1/n)^{ 1-\beta/2}+(1/n)^{1/2}\log(n)]\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}\bigg\}.
		\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem ww1-1-intro of arXiv:2512.17727, 'Stochastic transport equation with L\'evy noise'] Let us assume that $T>0$,   $\alpha \in (0,2)$ and  $\beta \in (0,1) $ satisfy condition (equation eqn-alphabeta of the paper). 
Then there exists a $\mathbb{P}$-full event $\Omega^{\prime\prime} \subset \Omega$ and a map 
\[
\phi:[0,T]\times [0,T] \times \mathbb{R}^d\times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d, \;\; 
\]
here $\Omega^{\prime\prime}$ is independent of $(s,t,x)\in[0,T]\times[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, such that,  for every $(s,x)\in [0,T] \times \mathbb R^d$, the process 
\[
\mbox{$[s,T] \times  \Omega \ni (t,\omega) \mapsto \phi_{s,t}(x, \omega) \in \mathbb{R}^d$, }
\]
is the unique solution to  SDE
(equation eqn-SDE-intro of the paper)   and for all  $\omega \in \Omega^{\prime\prime}$,  $0\le s \le  t \le T$,
the mapping 
\begin{align}
\mathbb R^d \ni x \mapsto \phi_{s,t}(x) =\phi_{s,t}(x, \omega) \in \mathbb R^d
\end{align}
is  a surjective diffeomorphism of class $C^{1+\delta}$ for any $\delta\in [0,\frac\alpha2+\beta-1)$. More precisely, both $\phi_{s,t}(x)$ and its inverse $\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)$ satisfy the sharp c\`adl\`ag property  in $(s,t,x)$ separately:
\begin{trivlist}
\item[(scp)] for every $\omega \in \Omega''$,             
            the maps  
\[ (s,t,x)\mapsto \phi_{s,t}(x, \omega) \in \mathbb{R}^d,\quad\quad  (s,t,x)\mapsto \phi^{-1}_{s,t}(x, \omega) \in \mathbb{R}^d
\]
are c{\`a}dl{\`a}g w.r.t. $s$,  for all $(t,x)$  fixed, c{\`a}dl{\`a}g  w.r.t. $t$, for all  $(s,x)$ fixed,  and  continuous w.r.t. $x$,  for all $(s,t)$ fixed; 
\end{trivlist}
moreover, for every  $\omega \in \Omega^{\prime\prime}$ and $\delta \in (0,\frac{\alpha}2+\beta-1)$,
the derivative functions
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{R}^d \ni x \mapsto D \phi_{s,t}(x)   \in \mathscr{L}(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d) \\
& \mathbb{R}^d \ni x \mapsto  D (\phi_{s,t}^{-1} )(x) \in \mathscr{L}(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d) 
\end{align*}
  are     locally $\delta$-H\"older continuous  uniformly in $(s,t) \in [0,T] \times [0,T]$;
  and 
   $ D \phi_{s,t}(x),  D (\phi_{s,t}^{-1} )(x) $
exhibit the \textit{sharp c\`adl\`ag property} in $(s,t,x)$ separately. 

Let $(b^{n})_{n=1}^\infty\subset C_{\mathrm{b}}^{\beta}(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^d)$
be a sequence of vector fields and $\phi^{n}$ the corresponding
stochastic flows. 
 Let $b^{n}\to b$ in $C_{\mathrm{b}}^{\beta}(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^d)$.
Then, for every $p\geq 1$ and any compact set $K \subset \mathbb R^d$, we have:
\begin{align}
&\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}} \sup_{s\in [0,T]}
\mathbb{E}[ \sup_{t \in [s,T]} |\phi_{s,t}^{n}(x)-\phi_{s,t}(x)\vert^{p}]=0;\\
&\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\sup_{s\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{t \in [s,T]} \Vert D\phi_{s,t}^{n}(x)\Vert^{p}]
+
\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\sup_{s\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{t \in [s,T]} \Vert D\phi_{s,t}(x)\Vert^{p}]
<\infty;\\
&   \,  \lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in K}\sup_{s\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{t \in [s,T]} \Vert D\phi_{s,t}^{n}(x)-D\phi_{s,t}(x)\Vert^{p}]=0.
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
&\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}} \sup_{t\in [0,T]}
\mathbb{E}[ \sup_{s \in [0,t]} |(\phi_{s,t}^{n})^{-1}(x)-\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)\vert^{p}]=0,\\
&\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\sup_{t\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{s \in [0,t]}\Vert D(\phi_{s,t}^{n})^{-1}(x)\Vert^{p}]
+
\sup_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}}\sup_{t\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{s \in [0,t]}\Vert D\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)\Vert^{p}]
<\infty,\\
&  \, \lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in K } \sup_{t\in [0,T]} \mathbb{E}[  \sup_{s \in [0,t]} \Vert D(\phi_{s,t}^{n})^{-1}(x)-D\phi_{s,t}^{-1}(x)\Vert^{p}]=0.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2608.31145, 'Gauge-compatible tensors on statistical manifolds: splitting and submanifold geometry'] Let $M$ be a $\Theta$-CR submanifold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Assume
\[
\ker(F_{\Theta}|_{TM})=D_{\Theta}.
\]
Then $D_{\Theta}$ is $\nabla^{*}$-autoparallel if and only if
\begin{equation}
h(X,\Theta Y)
=
f_{\Theta}(h^{*}(X,Y))
\end{equation}
for all $X,Y\in\Gamma(D_{\Theta})$.

\item Assume
\[
\ker(P_{\Theta}|_{TM})=D_{\Theta}^{\perp}.
\]
Then $D_{\Theta}^{\perp}$ is $\nabla^{*}$-autoparallel if and only if
\begin{equation}
A_{\Theta V}U
+
t_{\Theta}(h^{*}(U,V))
=
0
\end{equation}
for all $U,V\in\Gamma(D_{\Theta}^{\perp})$.
\end{enumerate}

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2608.15379, 'Stochastic Jacobi fields along discontinuous martingales on Riemannian submanifolds'] Define the map $\gamma^{\bcl} \colon TM\times TM \to TTM$ by
\[
\gamma^{\bcl} (\bU,\bV):=s_M(d\gamma (\bU,\bV)).
\]
Then for $\bU \in T_xM,\bV \in T_yM$,
\begin{align}
\gamma^{\bcl} (\bU,\bV)=(\gamma (x, y), \II(\gamma(x,y),\bU)) + (0,-A_{\Pi_x^{\perp}(y-x)}\bU+ \Pi_x(\bV-\bU)))
\end{align}
and $\gamma^{\bcl}$ is a connection rule on $TM$.

[Lemma compare_towers_final of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'] Let $s\geq r\geq 1$ be integers and let $a_1, \dots a_r$ and $ b_1,\dots, b_s>0$ be (strictly) positive real numbers.
	Let 
\begin{align}
	h_a(u)&=f(a_1f(a_2\dots f(a_r u)\dots))\\ h_b(u)&=f(b_1f(b_2\dots f(b_s u)\dots)).
\end{align}	
	Then if $r<s$, we have $h_a(u)\lll h_b(u)$. 
	The same is true if $r=s$ and if the largest $i\in [r]$ such $a_i\neq b_i$ is such that $a_i<b_i$ and $i>1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.00680, 'Sharp embeddings between quasi-Banach Besov spaces and shallow ReLU Variation spaces'] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Then
\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\hookrightarrow B_{p,2}^{k+1}(\Omega),
 \qquad 0<p<1.
\]
For every $0<q<2$,
\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\not\hookrightarrow B_{p,q}^{k+1}(\Omega),
\]
and for every $s>k+1$ and $0<q\leq\infty$,
\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\not\hookrightarrow B_{p,q}^s(\Omega).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.00680

STATUS: proof (unaudited). For the exact critical tanh infinitesimal-angle kernel of C050, n Cov(log M_q,log H_q) converges uniformly for 0<q<=C/n to [[2,-1],[-1,1]]. Conditional eigenvalue coupling preserves the joint norm/tangent law and compares it to independent chi-square variables with L2 log errors <=C*q*log(2n); covariance error is O_C(log(n)/sqrt(n)+log(n)^2/n). Reciprocal-angle logarithms reverse the off-diagonal signs. Assumptions: Fixed finite C; n->infinity; equal variances q in (0,C/n]; n>=2; angular derivative at zero taken before n limit. Scope: Leading centered one-step noise only, not drift, finite-angle evolution, entrance convergence, or all-order cumulant remainders; proof unaudited.
Fixed finite C; n->infinity; equal variances q in (0,C/n]; n>=2; angular derivative at zero taken before n limit.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/1a/1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7c673ab1f544f0e3955fcd92879e554a7907834c68728a34330c1cedd7cbda10","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","bundle_id":"population.t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise-017","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_017.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Critical tanh: exact tangent kernel and its shared Wishart noise

20 October 2026. C050/C051; Target 3. Proof drafts, unaudited.
These are infinitesimal-angle one-step results, not a two-input tanh
diffusion theorem or an all-order cumulant expansion. No novelty asserted.

## C050: exact positive-variance kernel

Fix n>=2 and q>0. Let g,h be independent N(0,I_n) vectors. For two inputs
with equal preactivation variance q and angle theta, the next activated
vectors are exactly distributed as

    x = tanh(sqrt(q) g),
    y(theta) = tanh(sqrt(q)(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h)).

The independent Gaussian weight rows give these conditional marginals
given the present Gram matrix. The tanh critical weight variance is 1/n;
thus the next diagonal variance is K'=||x||^2/n and the radial multiplier
is M_q=||x||^2/(nq). There is no width-dependent shaping normalizer.

Set D=diag(sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i)), P_x=I-xx^T/||x||^2. Then the right-hand
derivative H_q of the angle between x and y(theta) at theta=0 is

    H_q^2 = q h^T D P_x D h / ||x||^2.

Proof: y(0)=x and y'(0)=sqrt(q)Dh. The derivative of y/||y|| is
sqrt(q)P_x Dh/||x||, whose norm is the nonnegative angular speed.
Almost surely x is nonzero and this speed is positive for n>=2.

Conditionally on g, Q_q=h^T D P_x D h is a sum of n-1 independent
chi-square_1 variables with positive weights equal to the nonzero
eigenvalues lambda_j of D P_x D. These satisfy

    d_min^2 <= lambda_j <= 1,
    d_min = min_i sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i).

Indeed these nonzero eigenvalues equal those of P_x D^2 P_x restricted
to x-perp, whose Rayleigh quotients lie in that interval. Both M_q and
the conditional weights depend on the same g. In particular the exact
positive-q model must retain this conditioning; replacing Q_q by an
independent chi-square is a different kernel. Even the radial sum
||x||^2/q is bounded above by n/q, unlike a chi-square variable.

For fixed n, q decreases to zero gives jointly, almost surely under the
original (g,h) coupling,

    M_q -> S/n,      H_q -> sqrt(R/S),
    S=||g||^2 ~ chi-square_n,
    R=h^T P_g h ~ chi-square_(n-1),  R independent of g and hence of S.

The independence follows because the conditional law of R given g is
the same chi-square_(n-1) law for every nonzero g. The SAME S appears in
the radial multiplier and angular denominator. For n=1 the tangent
speed is zero, so logarithmic angular statements below exclude n=1.

## C051: uniform leading noise at the critical variance scale

For every fixed C<infinity, uniformly over 0<q<=C/n, define

    A_q=log M_q,       B_q=log H_q.

As n increases,

    n Cov((A_q,B_q)) -> [[2,-1],[-1,1]].

Here Cov is centered covariance. Equivalently, replacing B_q by the
logarithmic reciprocal-angle multiplier -B_q changes both off-diagonal
entries to +1. This only identifies one-step noise, not a drift limit.

### Coupling and quantitative error

Draw g and, independently, eta_1,...,eta_(n-1) iid standard normals.
Use a measurable ordering of the eigenvalues above and put

    Q_q^* = sum_j lambda_j(g) eta_j^2,
    R^* = sum_j eta_j^2,       S=||g||^2.

The pair (M_q, sqrt(q Q_q^*/||x||^2)) has EXACTLY the required joint
law (M_q,H_q), by the conditional quadratic-form law. Also S and R^*
are independent chi-squares with the stated degrees of freedom.
Thus this construction verifies both coupled marginals. No pointwise
comparison with the original h projection is being asserted.

For z>=0, sech^2(z) <= tanh(z)/z <= 1, with the continuous value at zero.
Consequently, with Z=max_i |g_i|,

    d_min^2 <= ||x||^2/(qS) <= 1,
    d_min^2 <= Q_q^*/R^* <= 1.

Since log(cosh z)<=z^2/2, this yields the deterministic coupling bounds

    |A_q-log(S/n)| <= 2q Z^2,
    |B_q-(1/2)log(R^*/S)| <= q Z^2.

A Gaussian union bound P(Z^2>r)<=min(1,2n exp(-r/2)), integrated as
E Z^4=integral_0^infinity 2r P(Z^2>r)dr, gives
||Z^2||_2 <= C_0 log(2n). Hence each logarithmic error has L2 norm at
most C_1 q log(2n), without deleting any event or inverse tail.

### Covariance calculation

Let A_0=log(S/n), B_0=(log R^*-log S)/2. Gamma integration gives

    Var A_0 = psi_1(n/2),
    Cov(A_0,B_0) = -(1/2)psi_1(n/2),
    Var B_0 = (psi_1((n-1)/2)+psi_1(n/2))/4.

The trigamma series psi_1(z)=sum_(k>=0)(z+k)^(-2) and integral comparison
give psi_1(z)=1/z+O(z^-2). These identities can alternatively be obtained
by differentiating E S^t=2^t Gamma(n/2+t)/Gamma(n/2) at t=0.
The displayed baseline covariance therefore has the claimed limit
after multiplying by n, and its centered L2 norms are O(n^-1/2).

For centered random variables, covariance perturbation by L2 errors e
has size at most C(n^-1/2 ||e||_2 + ||e||_2^2); centering an error costs
no more than its L2 norm. After multiplying by n, our bound is

    O(sqrt(n) q log(2n) + n q^2 log(2n)^2)
       = O_C(log(2n)/sqrt(n) + log(2n)^2/n),

uniformly over 0<q<=C/n. This tends to zero and proves C051.

## Scope left open

The limits are: first the angle derivative at zero for fixed n,q,
then n -> infinity with q<=C/n. C051 does not justify exchanging the
infinitesimal-angle limit with a finite-angle network evolution, does
not give the order-1/n drift, and does not establish that actual tanh
input correlations approach one. The scalar critical-tanh diffusion
and cumulant-rate work remain separate claims C026-C027 and C044-C047.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:22c6d532d863fd81ef53240a00570657817f6c17e8e5fb0515c76a33cfbda523","revision_digest":"sha256:fc88eab43dde02de84f288e293b9f37cf1114c075d6075db6c02f0a27cabfd4e","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C051:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T13:53:12.705197","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: [Theorem 3.11 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,k,N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ be partial permutations, let $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, let $Y$ be the matrix resulting from the partial trace evaluation $(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{k}})(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})$, and let $q=\sum_{j=1}^{k}(m-|D(\sigma_{j})|)$ with $D(\sigma_{j})$ the domain of $\sigma_{j}$, so that $Y$ acts on a space of dimension $N^{q}$. For every $p\in\mathbb{N}$, $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\mathrm{Tr}((YY^{*})^{p})\leq N^{2pC(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}.$ (3.2) Moreover, for any configuration $\bm{\pi}_{0}$ with $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};\bm{\pi}_{0})=M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$, it holds that $Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*}=N^{2M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}I_{N^{q}},\qquad\mathrm{Tr}((Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*})^{p})=N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\quad(p\in\mathbb{N}).$ Thus, the tuple $(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})=(E_{\pi_{1}},\ldots,E_{\pi_{m}})$, which is independent of $p$, attains every lower moment bound $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}$. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

[Lem l1-lemma of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] For all $\beta \in (-1/2,-1/4)$ we have: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item  $L^1(\mathbb{T}) \subset \mathcal{B}_{\beta,2}$ and $\|u\|_\beta \lesssim \|u\|_{L^1}$ for all $u \in L^1(\mathbb{T})$.
        \item  If $f,g \in C(\overline D)_+$ then
        $$\|f\|_{L^1}\|g\|_{L^1} \lesssim \ip{f}{g}_\beta \lesssim \|f\|_{L^1}\|g\|_{L^1} \,.$$
    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:concave_profile_contract}
Let \(P_t\) have curvature at least \(\kappa\).
If an increasing concave function \(\psi:[0,D]\to[0,\infty)\) controls the increments of \(H\), then
\[
\|P_tH(x)-P_tH(y)\|_{\op}\le \psi((1-\kappa)d(x,y))
\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in\Omega.
\]

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] The localisation $p^l\colon \cal{C} \to \cal{B}^l$ admits a left calculus of fractions, that is, for $x,y \in \cal{C}$ the map
\[ \colim_{[y \mono y'] \in y\rtimes \cal{A}}\Map_{\cal{C}}(x,y') \to \Map_{\cal{B}^l}(p(x),p(y)) \]
is an equivalence, where $y\rtimes \cal{A} \subseteq \cal{C}_{y/}$ is the full subcategory spanned by the inclusions $y \mono y'$ with cofibre in $\cal{A}$. 
In particular, if $f\colon x \to y$ is a map in $\cal{B}^l$ then for every $\tilde x\in \cal{C}$ lifting $x$ we can lift $f$ to a map $\tilde f\colon \tilde x \to \tilde y$ with domain $\tilde x$. Dually, the localisation $p^r\colon \cal{C} \to \cal{B}^r$ admits a right calculus of fractions and every map in $\cal{B}^r$ admits a lift in $\cal{C}$ given any prescribed lift of its codomain.

[Lemma lem:complete-collision of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] In a fresh Kac frame put $\mathsf P_i=a_ia_i^*$ and
$W_i=\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W$.  Before any ancillary boundary routing, the intact
coordinate-plane average obeys, for arbitrary real
$|\epsilon_i|\le1$,
\[
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i\epsilon_iW_i\right\|_\mathrm{op}\le\frac2N.
\tag{3.2.10f}
\]
The exact scalar identities are
\[
 W_i^2=\left(1-\frac2N\right)W_i+\frac{N-1}{N^2}I,
 \qquad [A_i,\mathsf P_i]=0.
\tag{3.2.10g}
\]
If a passive map separates equal labels, then
\[
 \mathsf P_iT\mathsf P_i=\langle a_i,Ta_i\rangle \mathsf P_i;
\tag{3.2.10h}
\]
this expression remains in the intact collision block and is not replaced
by a scalar unless $T$ itself is scalar.  Relative to the Jacobi
coefficients $1,\gamma$, the only naked finite-$N$ residuals in (eq:3.2.10g of the paper)
are $-2N^{-1}W_i$ and $-\gamma N^{-1}I$.  The first child remains
time-indexed.  The second is formed only after the $m-1$ collision labels
have been summed; before residual temporal components are defined it is
removed from the temporal word, with $\gamma$ retained in the
monomer--dimer ledger and the remaining $N^{-1}$ kept as a favorable
scalar coefficient carrying no time, gap, anchor, or translation.
