[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \((M^{n},g)\), \(n\geq4\), be a closed, connected, oriented,
locally conformally flat manifold with scalar curvature
\(\mathrm{Sc}_{g}\geq n(n-1)\). Identify
\(\Gamma:=\pi_1(M)\) with its holonomy Kleinian group, and suppose that
\(\Gamma\) is elementary. If there exists a smooth distance-nonincreasing (i.e.,
\(1\)-Lipschitz) map
\(
f\colon(M^n,g)\to (S^{n},g_{st})
\)
of nonzero degree, then \(f\) is a Riemannian isometry.

body:
[Corollary cor: double well of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Under the same conditions as the previous theorem,
let $d=1$, and consider the choice of confinement potential of the form
\begin{equation}

 V(x)
 =
 \frac{x^4}{4} - \lambda\frac{x^2}{2}
 ,\qquad
 x,y,\lambda\in\R,
\end{equation}
or more generally suppose  that $V$ is in the GHS class, i.e.~satisfies Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper) below.
Then for any $T>T_c$ (defined in (equation eq_def_beta_c of the paper)), 
the measure $m^N_T$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with a constant independent of $N$.  
Moreover, the log-Sobolev constant vanishes  linearly at $T_c$: 
\begin{equation} 	
\limsup_{N\to\infty} \gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	
\leq 
c_1 (T-T_c)
,\qquad
\gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	\geq 
c_2 (T-T_c)
,\quad 
N\geq 1,
\end{equation}
for some  constants $c_1, c_2>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Double well confinement potentials

[Lemma Order of sums associated to deterministic matrices of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] Let $\pi\in \mathcal{P}(2m)$ and let $S_{\pi}(N)$ be the sum in ((Equation: Sum associated to product of deterministic matrices in terms of graph of the paper)). Then,
$$|S_\pi(N)|\leq N^{t(G^\pi)}\prod_{i=1}^m ||D_i||.$$
Here  $G^\pi$ is the quotient graph of $G$ defined as before, and $t(G^\pi)$ is determined by the forest of two edge connected components $\mathcal{F}(G^\pi)$ as follows
$$t(G^\pi)=\sum_{L\text{ leaf of }\mathcal{F}(G^\pi)}t(L),$$
where
$$t(L)= \left\{ \begin{array}{lc} 1 & \text{if } L\text{ is an isolate vertex}, \\ \\ 
1/2 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array} \right.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.29872, 'Local Laws and Outlier Eigenvalues for Spiked Separable Covariance Matrices'] Let $\{\xi(u),u\in U\}$ be a family of random variables with $|U|\leq n^C$ for some constant $C$, and let $\psi$ be a non-negative deterministic parameter. If
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\abs{\xi(u)}^{2k}\right]\prec\psi^{2k}$$
uniformly in $u$ holds for all $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$, then we have $\max_{u\in U}\abs{\xi(u)}\prec\psi$.

body:
[Corollary 15 (Weighted stable representation) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $0<p\le q$, and let $V_{p,q}$ be the unique factor of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Then, for every bounded measurable $h:\R\to\R$,
\[
\E h(X_p)=\E h(V_{p,q}X_q).
\]
If $p<q$, put $a=1/p$, $b=1/q$, let $S_{p/q}$ be independent of $X_q$, and set
\[
W_0=S_{p/q}^{-b}.
\]
Then
\[
\E W_0=\frac{\Gamma(a)}{(p/q)\Gamma(b)}=\frac{a\Gamma(a)}{b\Gamma(b)}<\infty,
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\E h(X_p)=\frac{\E\left[W_0 h\left(2^{a-b}W_0X_q\right)\right]}{\E W_0}.

\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\varkappa:=\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}.
\]
Then, for every mapping $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ with $f_j\in \mathcal{P}_d(\gamma)$, satisfying
\[
\int_E \Delta_f\,d\gamma \ge a
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(f_j)\le b,
\]
and for every $\alpha\in(0,\varkappa)$, one has
\[
\sigma_f(t)
\le
C_1kd(\varkappa-\alpha)^{-\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}}
\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)^\alpha
\quad \forall t>0,
\]
where $C_1>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, optimizing over $\alpha$, we obtain
\[
\sigma_f(t)
\le
C_2kd
\bigl(1+\bigl|\ln\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)\bigr|\bigr)^{\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}}
\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)^\varkappa
\quad \forall t>0,
\]
for some absolute constant $C_2>0$.

[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.03361, 'Grassmann--Pl\"ucker Parametrization of Convolutional Filter Subspaces:\ Regularity and Cl'] Let $\cK=\CC^k$, let $H=\Hom(E,F)$, and let
$\cC:\cK\to H$ be the linear map induced by the finite-stride convolution in
Definition~\ref{def:convolution}. For every $1\leq q\leq k$, the parametrization
\[
  \Phi=\Pl_H\circ\Gamma_{\cC}:
  \Gr(q,\cK)\longrightarrow\PP(\wedge^qH)
\]
is a closed embedding. If $X=\Gr(q,\cK)$ and $Y=\Phi(X)$, then
$\Phi:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ is an isomorphism. In particular, $\Phi$ is finite
and birational onto its image, $\#\Phi^{-1}(y)=1$ for every $y\in Y$, and
\[
  \dim Y=q(k-q),\qquad \Sing(Y)=\varnothing.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main theorem

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two. Verification as the source words it: both bounds are uniform over the whole admissible range of R (measured max F(0) = 0.099010, min F(a) = 0.129901), so this is a proof and not a numerical observation; and a control both ways - on the three cases where the authors' Theorem 4.4 applies (alpha = 1, beta = 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3) the same root counter returns at most 2 roots at t = 1.01 D and t = 10 D, agreeing with their proved theorem. Prior art not cleared. nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2, supported on [1/10, 10] sigma_t the free positive multiplicative Brownian motion t >= 5 pi

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] Let $\overline\Cc$ be the class of two-dimensional Alexandrov surfaces of curvature
$\ge1$, each written $e^{2u}\round$ (the conformal representation being
Reshetnyak's \cite{Reshetnyak}, as recalled above), with curvature measure
$\omega=(1+\Delta_0 u)\,\dd\ \ge\ e^{2u}\dd$ of total mass $\omega(\Sph^2)=4\pi$. A
\emph{spherical cone metric} is a member of $\overline\Cc$ whose absolutely continuous
curvature density is $1$ almost everywhere, so that $\omega=e^{2u}\dd$ together with
finitely many atoms; the spindles \eqref{eq:spindle} are the cone metrics with two
antipodal atoms.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02808

body:
[Lem relative-orbifold-degeneration of arXiv:2609.01300, 'Virasoro Constraints for Orbifold Curves'] With the notation fixed above,
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
\left\langle
\prod_{i\in N}\tau_{k_i}(\gamma_i)
\ \middle|\
\boldsymbol\eta',\boldsymbol\eta_0
\right\rangle^{\bullet,\,\mathcal C/Q}_{d}
={}&
\sum_{\mu\vdash d}\mathfrak z(\mu)
\sum_{N=N'\sqcup N_0}(-1)^{\epsilon(N',N_0)}
\\[-1mm]
&\hspace{-35mm}\cdot
\left\langle
\prod_{i\in N'}\tau_{k_i}(\gamma_i)
\ \middle|\
\boldsymbol\eta',\mu
\right\rangle^{\bullet,\,\mathcal C'/(Q'\cup\{p\})}_{d}
\left\langle
\prod_{i\in N_0}\tau_{k_i}(\gamma_{i})
\ \middle|\
\boldsymbol\eta_0,\mu
\right\rangle^{\bullet,\,\mathcal C_0/(Q_0\cup\{p\})}_{d}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here \(
\mathfrak z(\mu)
=
|\mathrm{Aut}(\mu)|
\prod_{j=1}^{\ell(\mu)}\mu_j
\). For each $\gamma_i\in H^*_{\mathrm{CR}}(\mathcal C)$ we fix its specializations in $H^*_{\mathrm{CR}}(\mathcal C')$ and $H^*_{\mathrm{CR}}(\mathcal C_0)$. The subsets \(N'\) and \(N_0\) are the sets of the absolute markings
specialized to \(\mathcal C'\) and \(\mathcal C_0\), respectively, and the sign \((-1)^{\epsilon(N',N_0)}\) is fixed in terms of the parity of insertions so that we formally have \[\prod_{i\in N}\gamma_i=(-1)^{\epsilon(N',N_0)}\prod_{i\in N'}\gamma_i\prod_{i\in N_0}\gamma_i,\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem relative-orbifold-degeneration of arXiv:2609.01300

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2609.00719, 'On the Aleksandrov--Bakelman--Pucci estimates for the weighted $1$-Laplacian'] Let $u\in\mathrm{USC}(\R^n)$ be nonnegative with $\operatorname{supp}u\subseteq\overline\Omega$. Assume that $F\in C(\R^n\times\mathcal S^n)$ satisfies $F(x,0)=0$ for every $x\in\R^n$ and is uniformly elliptic with constants $\lambda,\Lambda$, that $f\in C(\R^n)$, and that $u$ is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{F} in $\{u>0\}$. Then
        \[
        \sup_{\R^n}u
        \leq
        \frac{1}{\lambda^{n-1}(n-1)^{n-1}\mathcal H^{n-1}(\partial B_1)}
        \int_{\Theta(u)\cap\{u>0\}}(f^-)^{n-1}\,dx.
        \]

[Corollary of arXiv:2608.16170, '\bf On hitting time distributions of Markov processes with sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds'] Let $p^-_\sigma(t,x,y):=p(t,x,y)-p^+_\sigma(t,x,y)$ for $t>0$ and $x,y\in E$. Then $p^-_\sigma(\cdot, \cdot,\cdot)\in \mathscr{B}((0,\infty))\times \mathscr{B}^*(E)\times \mathscr{B}(E)$ satisfies 
    \[
        \mathbb{E}^x\left[f(X_t);t\leq \sigma \right]=\int_E p^-_\sigma(t,x,y)f(y)\mu(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall t>0,x\in E, f\in \mathrm{b}\mathscr{B}(E). 
    \]
In particular, 
\[
    p(t,x,y)=p^-_\sigma(t,x,y)+p^+_\sigma(t,x,y),\quad \forall t>0, x,y\in E 
\]
provides a decomposition of transition density function into the contributions before and after $\sigma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered corollary of arXiv:2608.16170, '\bf On hitting time distributions of Markov processes with s'

body:
[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] Let $g_0$ be a stretching morphism from some capacity $\lambda$ on an interval $I$ to the constant capacity 1, and fix $x_0\in\overline I$. This means that for $z_0:=g_0(x_0)\in\overline\R$, $g_0$ is a $\mathcal C ^1$-diffeomorphism from $I$ to $\R$ of the form $g_0 : x\in I \mapsto z_0+\int_{x_0}^x {\dd r} / \lambda(r) \in \R $ (understood as a limit when $z_0=\pm\infty$). Let $(D_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ be a continuous process with strictly increasing quadratic variation, taking values in $\overline \R = \R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ (defined up to time-change) and verifying the following two conditions.

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(i) Well-posedness of the flow.}
For every $x\in I$, the integral equation
$$g_t(x)=g_0(x)+\int_0^t\1_{(z_0,g_s(x))}(D_s)\dd[D]_s$$
admits a unique solution until time $T(x):=\inf\{t\geq 0, g_t(x)=\pm\infty\}$, and the map
$(t,x)\mapsto g_t(x)$
is continuous on its domain $\{(t,x), x\in I, 0\le t < T(x)\}$. 

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(ii) Jointly continuous local times along the flow.}
For $x\in I$, assume that the family of processes $(R_t^x)_{0\leq t <T(x)} :=(D_t-g_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(x)} $ admits jointly continuous local
times: namely, assume that there exists a nonnegative field
$(L_t^x(a))_{x\in I,a\in\R,\, 0\leq t<T(x)}$, jointly continuous (at least in a neighborhood of $a=0$)
in $(t,x,a)$, such that for every $x\in I$, every $0\leq t<T(x)$,
and every bounded Borel function $f$,
$$\int_0^t f(R_s^x)\dd[R^x]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(a)L_t^x(a)\dd a.
$$

\ms

Write   
$L_t(x):=L_t^x(0).$ For $0\leq t \leq T$, let $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$, and finally let us define for such a process $D$ its final time $T(D) := \inf\{s\leq T,\, \mathring I_s=\emptyset\}\wedge T $.
Then the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $0 \leq t < T(D)$, the map $x\mapsto g_t(x)$ is an increasing $C^1$-diffeomorphism from the open interval $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$ to $\R$, with
$$\partial_x g_t(x)=({\exp(L_t(x))}) / {\lambda(x)}.$$

\item  The process $X$ defined for $0\leq t< T(D)$ by
$X_t:=g_t^{-1}(D_t)\in \overline I_t$
is continuous and admits a bicontinuous local time $(\Lambda_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(D),\,x\in I}$, where
$\Lambda_t(x)=\lambda(x)\left(1-\exp\bigl(-L_t(x)\bigr)\right)$, i.e.\ for every bounded Borel function $f$, 
$$\int_0^t f(X_s)\dd[X]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Lambda_t(x)\dd x.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 10 (Classification of autonomous C-S posteriors) of arXiv:2607.20373, 'Embedding martingale diffusions as binary posteriors in sequential inference'] \emph{(i)} There exists $\gamma\in C(J;(0,1))$ with $P_t=\gamma(X_t)$ for $t<\zeta$
if and only if $\kappa=0$. In this case, either $\delta\equiv0$ and $P\equiv p$, or
$\delta$ has no zeros, $\gamma$ is a $C^2$--diffeomorphism onto $\gamma(J)$ with
inverse $f$, and
\begin{equation}
  dP_t=P_t(1-P_t)\,\delta(f(P_t))\,d\overline W_t,\qquad t<\zeta.
\end{equation}
\emph{(ii)} Let $\kappa\neq0$. Then $P$ satisfies \eqref{eq:intro-target} for
$t<\zeta$ if and only if $\delta$ is constant. In this case $\delta\equiv\Delta\neq0$ and $dP_t=\Delta P_t(1-P_t)\,d\overline W_t$,  $t<\zeta$.

[Lemma 30 (Lyapunov drift for the forward and adjoint chains) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:U} and~\ref{ass:whole-space-growth}.  Write
$\calL_\eps^{(+)}=\calL_\eps$ and
$\calL_\eps^{(-)}=\calL_\eps^*$.  Equivalently,
\[
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)} f
    =
    \sigma p\cdot\nabla_\theta f
    +\left(-\sigma L^{-1}\nabla U(\theta)+\sigma\gamma r\right)
        \cdot\nabla_p f
    +(-\sigma\gamma p-\gamma r)\cdot\nabla_r f
    +\frac{\gamma\eps}{L}\Delta_r f,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\]
There exist constants $\kappa,\alpha,\eta,C_V,c,C>0$, with
$\eta=\kappa\alpha$, such that the functions
\[
    V_\sigma(\theta,p,r)
    =
    C_V+H(\theta,p,r)+\eta H(\theta,p,r)^2
    +\alpha K_\sigma(\theta,p,r),
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\},
\]
where
\[
    K_\sigma
    =
    \sigma\theta\cdot p+\theta\cdot r
    +\frac{2\sigma}{\gamma}p\cdot r
    +\frac{\gamma}{2}|\theta|^2,
\]
are nonnegative, have compact sublevel sets, and satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)}V_\sigma
    \le
    -c\left(U(\theta)+|p|^2+|r|^2+H(\theta,p,r)|r|^2\right)+C,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every
\[
    R\ge \frac{C+1}{c},
\]
the compact set $\mathsf K_R$ defined in
\eqref{eq:whole-space-lyapunov-set} satisfies
$\calL_\eps^{(\sigma)}V_\sigma\le -1$ on
$\mathsf K_R^c$ for both signs $\sigma$.

[Lemma 6 (Bousquet's inequality) of arXiv:2608.24858, 'Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learnin'] Let \(\mathcal G\) be a countable class of measurable functions satisfying
\(Pg=0\), \(\|g\|_\infty\le b\), and \(Pg^2\le v\) for all
\(g\in\mathcal G\). Then, for every \(u\ge0\), with probability at least
\(1-e^{-u}\),
\[
  \sup_{g\in\mathcal G}|(P_N-P)g|
  \le
  \mathbb E\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}|(P_N-P)g|
  +
  \sqrt{
    \frac{2u}{N}
    \left\{
      v+2b\mathbb E\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}|(P_N-P)g|
    \right\}
  }
  +
  \frac{bu}{3N}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The fixed-domain perturbation formulas used later are collected here.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}, so that the principal eigenvalue is simple in the positive cone. Let $h\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $h\ge0$ and $h\not\equiv0$. Then $\Lp(\cA_\R+h)<\Lp(\cA_\R)$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $b\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $b\ge0$ and $b\not\equiv0$, and assume that the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore} hold for every operator $\cA_\R+rb$ under consideration. Then $r\longmapsto\Lp(\cA_\R+rb)$
is strictly decreasing and locally Lipschitz. If there exist $r_-<r_+$ such that the two values have opposite signs, there is a unique $r_*$ with $\Lp(\cA_\R+r_*b)=0$.

\textup{(iii)} Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be fixed. Let
\[
\cA_\tau u=d\int_\Omega\big(J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)\big)u(y)\,dy+\big(q(x)+\tau r(x)\big)u'(x)+\big(b(x)+\tau h(x)\big)u(x),
\]
where $q,r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$, $b,h\in C(\overline \Omega)$ and $H\in C(\overline \Omega^2)$.  We restrict $\tau$ to a real interval on which the drift is bounded away from zero and the kernels $J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)$ are nonnegative and satisfy a common positivity condition in a neighborhood of the diagonal. Let $\lambda(\tau)=\Lp(\cA_\tau)$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized principal eigenfunction are real analytic in $\tau$ on that interval. If $\phi,\phi^*>0$ are the direct and adjoint principal eigenfunctions at $\tau=0$, normalized by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*\,dx=1$,
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda'(0)={}&-d\int_\Omega\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)H(x,y)\phi(y)\,dy\,dx\\
&-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx
-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for a potential perturbation alone,
\[
\lambda'(0)=-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]

\textup{(iv)} On a fixed bounded interval let
\[
\cA_{d,c}u=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+c\,r(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
where $d>0$, $c$ ranges in an interval on which $cr(x)$ has a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and $r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Normalize the direct and adjoint eigenfunctions by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized eigenfunction are real analytic in $(d,c)$ on every connected parameter region on which $d>0$ and $cr$ keeps a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and
\[
\partial_d\Lp=-\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)\phi(y)\,dy-\phi(x)\right)dx,
\]
\[
\partial_c\Lp=-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]
No sign is asserted for these derivatives in general.

\textup{(v)} For the scaled operator
\[
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}u=\frac1{\sigma^m}\left(\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+q(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
put $\rho=\sigma/L$ and $v(\xi)=u(L\xi)$. Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\Lp\left(L^{-m}\rho^{-m}(\mathcal J_\rho-I)+L^{-1}q(L\cdot)\partial_\xi+a(L\cdot),(-1,1)\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal J_\rho v(\xi)=\int_{-1}^{1}J_\rho(\xi-\eta)v(\eta)\,d\eta.
\]

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] The Klein geometry $\operatorname{Euc}(n)/O(n)$ is first-order and reductive. More precisely, under the identification \eqref{eq:euc-quotient-on},
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Ad}}(A)(v)=Av,
\qquad A\in O(n),\quad v\in\mathbb{R}^{n},
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak{euc}(n)=\mathfrak{o}(n)\oplus\mathfrak{t},
\qquad
\mathfrak{t}:=
\left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0\\
v&0
\end{pmatrix}: v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
\right\},
\]
with $\mathrm{Ad}(O(n))(\mathfrak{t})\subset\mathfrak{t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Main2 3 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Let $p\ge2$ and let $S_w(0)\subseteq\mathbb Z_p^m$ be a set of vectors of Hamming weight $w$. There exists an embedding
$f:S_w(0)\hookrightarrow S^{(p-1)m-1}\subset\mathbb R^{(p-1)m}$
such that if $b\le m$ is an integer satisfying
$\frac{w}{m}<J_p\!\left(\frac{b}{m}\right)$
and $\mathcal C$ is any subset of $S_w(0)$ that satisfies $d(x,y)\ge b$ for all distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C$, then

\begin{enumerate}
\item For all distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C$, $\langle f(x),f(y)\rangle<0$, where $\langle \,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denotes the Euclidean inner product; and
\item $|\mathcal C|\le\min\left\{(p-1)m+1,\gamma(p,b,w,m)\right\}$,
where \begin{equation}
\gamma(p,b,w,m)
:=
\floor{\frac{b}{\,b-mJ_p^{-1}(\frac{w}{m})\,}}.
\end{equation}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:LR-input of arXiv:2607.03639, '\vspace{-0.6in}An AI-Assisted Solution to the Signed BAR Conjecture: Uniqueness in the Har'] In the setting just described, fix $\alpha\in U$.  Assume the following
hypotheses.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.1em]
\item $G$ is minimally represented and simple, $U$ is open, and
$\alpha\mapsto d_i(\alpha)$, $b(\alpha)$, and $\sigma(\alpha)$ are $C^1$ with
bounded first derivatives and local H\"older regularity.

\item $a(\alpha)$ is uniformly elliptic: $v^Ta(\alpha)v\ge\theta|v|^2$ for some
$\theta>0$ and all $v\in\mathbb R^d$.

\item $N^T\mathcal D(\alpha)$ is a nonsingular $M$-matrix.

\item The reflection matrix is constant in the parameter, or more generally
$\partial_\alpha\mathcal D(\alpha)$ is bounded.
\end{enumerate}

Then the following conclusions are available under the assumptions indicated.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.1em]
\item \emph{(Well posedness; uses \textup{(A1)} and \textup{(A3)},
[LipshutzRamanan2021].)}
For each $x\in G$ and each prescribed Brownian motion, there is a pathwise
unique reflected diffusion $Z^{\alpha,x}$, and it is strong Markov.

\item \emph{(Lipschitz extended Skorokhod map; uses \textup{(A1)} and
\textup{(A3)}, [LipshutzRamanan2019].)}
The extended Skorokhod problem associated with $(G,d_i(\alpha))$ is well posed,
and its extended Skorokhod map $\bar\Gamma^\alpha$ is Lipschitz on compact time
intervals: $\sup_{s\le t}\left\lvert \bar\Gamma^\alpha(f)(s)-\bar\Gamma^\alpha(g)(s)\right\rvert
\le K_\Gamma\sup_{s\le t}\left\lvert f(s)-g(s)\right\rvert$ for some $K_\Gamma<\infty$, all
continuous inputs $f,g$, and all $t\ge0$.

\item \emph{(Boundary jitter; uses \textup{(A2)} in the above setting,
[LipshutzRamanan2019].)}
Uniform ellipticity implies the boundary jitter property required for the
pathwise derivative theorem.

\item \emph{(Derivative projection; uses \textup{(A1)} and \textup{(A3)},
[LipshutzRamanan2019].)}
For each $x\in G$ there is a unique linear projection
$\mathcal L_x^\alpha:\mathbb R^d\to H_G(x)$ such that
$\mathcal L_x^\alpha v-v\in
\operatorname{span}\{d_i(\alpha):i\in I_G(x)\}$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$.

\item \emph{(Pathwise differentiability; uses \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A4)} and
\textup{(C3)}--\textup{(C4)}, [LipshutzRamanan2019].)}
For this theorem, note that \textup{(A3)} implies Condition~2.10 of
[LipshutzRamanan2019]: if $A\subset J$ and
$\sum_{i\in A}c_i d_i(\alpha)=0$, then
$(N^T\mathcal D(\alpha))_{AA}c_A=0$, and every principal submatrix of a
nonsingular $M$-matrix is nonsingular, so $c_A=0$.  Hence
[LipshutzRamanan2019] gives the exceptional set of this theorem $\mathcal W^\alpha=\varnothing$.  Therefore,
for each $x\in G\backslash \mathcal W^\alpha=G$ there is an adapted RCLL derivative process
$J_t^{\alpha,x}\in\operatorname{Lin}(H_G(x),\mathbb R^d)$.  For every fixed
$w\in C_G(x)$, we have almost surely,
$\partial_w Z_t^{\alpha,x}:=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\varepsilon^{-1}(Z_t^{\alpha,x+\varepsilon w}-Z_t^{\alpha,x})$ exists for every
$t\ge0$, is continuous at every
$t>0$ such that $Z_t^{\alpha,x}\in G^\circ$, and its right-continuous regularization satisfies
$\lim_{s\downarrow t}\partial_w Z_s^{\alpha,x}
=J_t^{\alpha,x}[\mathcal L_x^\alpha w]$ for all $t\ge0$.

\item \emph{(Fixed-time interior statement; uses \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A4)}
and \textup{(C3)}--\textup{(C4)}, [LipshutzRamanan2019].)}
For every fixed $t>0$, $\mathbb P(Z_t^{\alpha,x}\in G^\circ)=1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth exponents in the spatial city-formation model structural calculation Result: A rigorous one-sided bound supports the balanced exponent when0<alpha<1 and beta>2alpha. Write d=beta/2-alpha>0. A union bound over influence disks gives area{I(y,t)>u}<=pi*c0^(2/beta)*u^(-2/beta)*M_t^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta), using concavity of the population power. Thus the conditional founding probability is at least1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*M_t^d)], K=(2pi)^(beta/2)*c0. Put theta=(1-alpha)/(1+d) and m=floor(kappa*t^theta). Until M reaches m, each of the last floor(t/2) arrivals has founding chance at least p=1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*m^d)]. Choose kappa small so this Bernoulli count has mean at least2m. A stopped coupling and Chernoff then give P(M_t<m)<=exp(-c*m) for large t. Check: The disk estimate is valid even at the square boundary because clipping only reduces area. Sum_i N_i^(2alpha/beta)<=M^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta). On the event M_t<m the threshold has never been reached, so domination by independent Bernoulli(p) increments throughout the half-interval is legitimate. The exponent identity theta*(1+d)=1-alpha makes the mean comparable to m. Obstruction: This proves a lower city-count growth bound in the balanced regime, not the matching upper bound, comparable populations, unbalanced regime, or alpha1 logarithmic law. The upper bound requires control of spatial clustering and influence overlap that the union bound does not supply.

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.04143, 'The Geometry of Real Anisotropic Bohnenblust--Hille Constants'] Let $\mathbf q$ be an $m$-linear Bohnenblust--Hille exponent. Write
\[
 q_{\min}:=\min_i q_i,\qquad q_{\max}:=\max_i q_i,
\]
let $d=d(\mathbf q)$, and set
\[
 \varepsilon=d+\frac{2}{m+1}.
\]
Assume $\varepsilon\le2/3$ and define
\begin{equation}
 k=\left\lfloor\frac{2}{\varepsilon}\right\rfloor-1.
\end{equation}
Then $2\le k\le m$, $p_k\le q_{\min}$, and
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}\le
 A_{p_k}^{-(m-k)}B_{\R,k}^{\mult}.
\end{equation}
If $\varepsilon\le1/4$, then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}\le
 M\left(\frac{2}{\varepsilon}\right)^\vartheta
 \exp\left(\frac{m\varepsilon}{4(1-\varepsilon)}\right).
\end{equation}

[Definition 26 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] A module \(M\in {}_S\mathcal{M}^{\mathsf{DG}}\) is said to be \emph{cellular} if it satisfies the following additional conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{(S\arabic*)},ref=S\arabic*,nosep,labelsep=.5em,align=left]
\item For each $ 0 \leq q \leq n $, there is a decomposition \( M^q=\bigoplus_{\tau\in S_q} M(\tau)\), where each $M(\tau)$ is finite-dimensional over \(\Bbbk\), and, for $\tau= [v_0,\ldots,v_q],$ \( M(\tau)\subseteq M_{v_0}=M_{s(\tau)}.\) Moreover, \(M^q=0\) for \(q>n\). We write \[ \iota_\tau : M(\tau) \hookrightarrow M^q, \qquad
\pi_\tau : M^q\twoheadrightarrow M(\tau) \] for the natural inclusions and projections, respectively. 
\item For each $\tau\in S_q$, $\zeta\in S_{q+1}$, let \(D_{\tau\rightarrow\zeta} \coloneq \pi_\zeta\circ d_M\circ \iota_\tau.\) Then
\[d_M\big\lvert _{M(\tau)}=\sum_{i=0}^{q+1} \sum_{\substack{\zeta\in S_{q+1}\\ d_i\zeta=\tau }}
D_{\tau\rightarrow \zeta}.\]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm.HLP of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $X, Y, Z_1, \dots, Z_n$ be integer random variables.

  Suppose the symmetric
  decreasing arrangement $Z_i^*$ exists
  for each $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$. Then
  \[

[Theorem 4 (Peskun--Tierney optimality of the $N$-vote rule) of arXiv:2609.00905, 'When Metropolis and Hastings Meet Bradley and Terry: Exact MCMC From Preference Voting'] Fix a proposal kernel $q$ and a comparison budget $N\geq 1$. Among all exact acceptance rules satisfying detailed balance with respect to $\pi$, that use the same proposal kernel and only the outcomes of exactly $N$ judge
queries per proposal, the $N$-vote rule Peskun--Tierney dominates every
competitor. Equivalently, for every proposed move $x\to x'$, we have 
$\mathbb P_{\text{$N$-vote}}(\textup{accept }x'\mid x,x'\textup{ proposed})
\geq
\mathbb P_{\text{competitor}}(\textup{accept }x'\mid x,x'\textup{ proposed}).
$

The proof is given in Appx. \ref{app:optimality-proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Peskun--Tierney optimality of the $N$-vote rule

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $d = o(\sqrt n)$. Suppose the exchangeable unconditional base vector $\mathbf X$ satisfies \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item  $\E X_1^2 = 1$,
        \item  $\frac{1}{n^{4d}}\E\nm{\mathbf X}_2^{8d} \to 1$, and 
        \item  there exists a sequence $L = L_n$ satisfying $Ld^2 / n \to 0$ such that $\E(X_1^8\dotsm X_r^8) \leq L^{2r}$ for all $1 \leq r\leq d$.
        
        
    \end{enumerate} then the three conditions in \cref{thm:main} are satisfied, and we have with probability $1$ that \[\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}.\]

    Alternatively, \cref{cond:8th-block-mmt} may be replaced by 
    \begin{enumerate}[resume,label=(iii')]
        \item  there exists a sequence $L = L_n$ satisfying $Ld^2 / n \to 0$ such that $\frac{1}{n^{2r}} \E\nm{\mathbf X}_4^{8r} \leq L^{2r}$ for all $1 \leq r \leq d$.\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 6 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Defn definition:W of arXiv:2606.02340, 'Transitivity in Inhomogeneous Random Tournaments'] Given a tournamenton \(W:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]\), a \(W\)-\emph{random tournament} on the vertex set \([n]:=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\) is obtained by orienting the edge \(u\to v\) with probability \(W(\eta_u,\eta_v)\), independently for \(1\le u<v\le n\), where \(\{\eta_u:1\le u\le n\}\) is an i.i.d. collection of \(\mathrm{Unif}([0,1])\) random variables. Equivalently, it is a tournament with adjacency matrix \(((a_{uv}))_{1\le u,v\le n}\), where
\[
a_{uv}\sim \mathrm{Ber}\bigl(W(\eta_u,\eta_v)\bigr)
\quad\text{and}\quad
a_{vu}=1-a_{uv},
\]
independently for \(1\le u<v\le n\). We denote this model by $T(n,W)$, and write $T_n \sim T(n,W)$ to indicate that $T_n$ is a random tournament sampled from this model.
title: $W$-random tournament model

body:
[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] If \(Z\) is uniform on the \(p\)-th roots of unity and
\(W=|\Impart Z|\), then
\[
 \E W^2=\frac12,\qquad \E W\geq\frac12,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(W)\leq\frac14.
\]
Consequently, for independent copies \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\),
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N W_j<N/4\right\}\leq\frac4N.
\end{equation}
All these bounds are independent of \(p\).

for $n$ large enough uniformly over

[Defn Infinitesimal holonomy of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a cooriented $C^0$-foliation on $M$, and $\gamma : S^1 \rightarrow L$ be a smooth closed curve tangent to a leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$, inducing a holonomy map 
    $$h : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \rightarrow (-1,1)$$
    for some $\varepsilon > 0$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ has \textbf{infinitesimal attracting holonomy} around $\gamma$ if for every open interval $\{0\} \subset I \subset (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$, there exists a smaller open interval $\{0\} \subset J \subset I$ such that 
    $$\overline{h(J)} \subset J.$$

body:
[Theorem 22 (Empirical Fourier CLT) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] There is a $\lambda_d$-conull set $E_\eta\subset\bR^d$ such that, for every
$\xi\in E_\eta$, every $m\geq1$, and every
$h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C_c^\infty(\bR^d;\bC)$,
\begin{equation}

    \bigl(Z_R(\xi;h_1),\ldots,Z_R(\xi;h_m)\bigr)
    \dto \bigl(G_\xi(h_1),\ldots,G_\xi(h_m)\bigr)
    \qquad\text{in }\bC^m,
\end{equation}
where the vector on the right is complex Gaussian with mean zero and
\begin{align}

    \E\!\left[G_\xi(h_a)\overline{G_\xi(h_b)}\right]
    &=s_\eta(\xi)
      \int_{\bR^d}h_a\overline{h_b}\,d\lambda_d,\\

    \E\!\left[G_\xi(h_a)G_\xi(h_b)\right]&=0.
\end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation}

    Z_R(\xi;h)
    \dto \mathcal{CN}\bigl(0,s_\eta(\xi)\|h\|_2^2\bigr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Empirical Fourier CLT

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \( (M^n,g) \), \(n\geq5\), be a closed, connected, oriented, locally conformally flat Riemannian manifold with positive scalar curvature and infinite fundamental group. Then \(M\) can be realized as a quotient \(\Omega/\Gamma\), as described above, with \(\Gamma\cong\pi_1(M)\). There exists an integer
$i \geq \Big\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \Big\rfloor + 1$
such that $\pi_i(M^n) \neq 0$.

If, in addition, \( H_1(M^n;\mathbb{Z}) = 0 \), then \( \Gamma \) is non-elementary.

If, moreover, \(\Gamma\) is torsion-free, then the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set satisfies
\[
1 < \dim_{\mathcal H}\Lambda(\Gamma) < \frac{n-2}{2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02267

body:
[Theorem 4 (The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $u \in \R^n$. Let $f \in \mathcal{F}(\conbodI)$. Then, for every measurable function $g:\R^n\to\R_+$ and measurable, non-increasing function $\Omega : (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that 
    \[
    f(x)g(y) \leq \Omega^2(\langle x, y \rangle), \qquad \forall \,\,x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } \langle x,y \rangle>0,
    \] 
    it holds
    \begin{equation}
    
        \left(\int_{\R^n} f(x) \langle x,u \rangle^2 dx \right) \left(\int_{\R^n} g(y) \langle y,u \rangle^2 dy \right) \leq \left(\int_{\R^n} \Omega(|z|^2) \langle z,u \rangle^2 dz \right)^2.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality

[Definition see, e.g., \cite{wijesekera_constructive_1990, simpson_proof_1994} of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For an f-model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, we define an \emph{intrinsic satisfaction relation} $\Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M}$ on $W \times \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ by:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, (x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi     \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, \forall y' \sqsupset x'\, (y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, \exists y' \sqsupset x'\, (y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item The other cases are identical to the classical $\Vdash_\mathfrak{M}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We write $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^i \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(i-)valid in} $\mathfrak{M}$'') to mean $\forall x \in W\,(x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$,
  and $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^i \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(i-)valid on} $\mathfrak{F}$'') to mean that $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^i \varphi$ for every $\mathfrak{M}$ based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
title: see, e.g., \cite{wijesekera_constructive_1990, simpson_proof_1994}

Own work draft, proof (unaudited); no independent PASS. In the C003 max-margin limit, let T have a fixed law with T>0 almost surely, essential infimum zero and E T^2 finite. Let n/(d-1)->alpha>0 and let the orthogonal block G have independent standard Gaussian entries, independent of iid T. Maximize min_i(a*T_i+(Gv)_i) on a^2+||v||^2<=1. The limiting margin and teacher coefficient are K and a*, the unique positive-margin optimizer of max k subject to k,a,s>=0, a^2+s^2<=1 and sqrt(alpha E[(k-aT-sH)_+^2])<=s, H independent standard Gaussian. In the isotropic Gaussian test model its limiting disagreement is acos(a*)/pi. This includes unpruned T=|Z|. Proof extends empirical envelopes and uses endpoint secants for uniform concave-profile convergence; it relies on the unaudited conditional-CGMT argument. Independent mathematical and novelty review pending.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Let
\[     A^{(n)}_{ij}:=\Cov(\xi_{n,i},\xi_{n,j}),     \qquad 0\le i,j\le b^n-1.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}     b^{-2n}\sum_{i,j=0}^{b^n-1}\abs{A^{(n)}_{ij}}^2\le C     \qquad\text{for all }n.                                    
\end{equation}
Also,
\begin{equation}     \Var(\xi_{n,k})\le Cn     \qquad\text{for all }n\text{ and }0\le k\le b^n-1.          
\end{equation}

[Theorem 11 (Gaussian-core Hermite approximation) of arXiv:2607.07712, 'Parameter-Space Heat Flow, Gaussian Density Ratios, and Sharp Hermite Truncation Rates'] Assume \(S=S^T\), \(I+S>0\), and
\[
\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1.
\]
Let \(r\) satisfy
\[
\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}<r<1.
\]
Then there exists \(C=C(u,S,r)>0\) such that, for every \(M\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
\|g-\Pi_{\le M}g\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}
\le
\rho C r^M
+
\|(I-\Pi_{\le M})h\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}.

\end{equation}
If, in addition, \(h\in\mathcal D(N^\beta)\) for some \(\beta>0\), then
\begin{equation}
\|g-\Pi_{\le M}g\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}
\le
\rho C r^M
+
(M+1)^{-\beta}
\|N^\beta h\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}.

\end{equation}

[Lemma eq:compact-support-joint-energy of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Suppose Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and
(ass:bochner-regularity of the paper) hold.  Let $w$ be a regular weight, let
$I=(r_0,r_1)$, and suppose
$h\in W_{p,\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(I\times\mathbb R^d)$ for some $p>d+2$.  If, for every compact
positive strip $J\Subset I$, there is a compact set $K_J\Subset\mathbb R^d$ such
that
$
 h=0\,\text{on }J\times(\mathbb R^d\setminus K_J),
$
then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak B_{J,w}(h)<\infty
 \qquad\text{for every compact positive strip }J\Subset I.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, if, in addition, $h=S_IF$ for some $F\in L_w^2(I)$ and $h$ has
an upper terminal gap, then
\begin{equation}
 h\in\mathfrak C_{\rm B}(I,w).

body:
Let γ : [α,β] → C be a closed piecewise C^1 curve and let a be a point not on the trace of γ. The winding number (index) of γ about a is n(γ,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ dz/(z - a). It is always an integer; as a function of a it is constant on each connected component of the complement of the trace of γ, and it is 0 on the unbounded component. The definition extends additively to cycles (finite formal integer combinations of closed curves) and, via continuous branches of the argument, to merely continuous closed curves. A cycle γ lying in an open set U is called null-homologous in U (homologous to zero) if n(γ,w) = 0 for every w in C minus U. An open connected U ⊂ C is simply connected if and only if every cycle in U is null-homologous in U, if and only if the complement of U in the Riemann sphere is connected. The homology form of Cauchy's theorem reads: if f is holomorphic on U and γ is a cycle null-homologous in U, then ∫_γ f(z) dz = 0 and n(γ,z) f(z) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ - z) dζ for every z in U off the trace of γ.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] Let \(A\) be a \(\Bbbk\)-algebra. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item \(A\) admits a universal connected FODC \((\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A),d_{\mathrm{uni}})\) given by
\[
\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)  \coloneq  \ker(\mu)\subseteq A\otimes_\Bbbk A,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{uni}}(a)=1_A\otimes a -a\otimes 1_A, \quad \forall a\in A, \]
where \(\mu\colon A\otimes_\Bbbk A\rightarrow A\) denotes the algebra multiplication.
\item Any FODC \(\Omega^1_A\) is isomorphic to a quotient \(\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)/N\), for some sub-bimodule \(N\subseteq\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)\), with differential induced by \(d_{\mathrm{uni}}\). 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tilted_gen_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $k\in\mathbb{R}$ and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold, in particular, 
assume additive noise $D=\sigma\sigma^\top/2$. The semigroup
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t \geq 0}$ is a strongly continuous semigroup on $L^2(\mu)$ whose
infinitesimal generator acts on $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ as
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J
  &=
  b \cdot (\nabla + kU)
  +
  (\nabla + kU) \cdot D(\nabla + kU),
  
\end{align}
or equivalently, expanding for $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ yields
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J f
  &=
  \mathcal{L}f
  +
  k\bigl(b \cdot U + \nabla \cdot DU\bigr) f + 2kU \cdot D \nabla f
  +
  k^2(U \cdot DU)f.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 24 (Joint fixed-index distributional and moment limit) of arXiv:2606.29635, 'Extremality and Limit Laws for the Siblings of the Coupon Collector'] Fix $J\ge2$ and set $a_{N,j}=(\log N)^{j-1}/(j-1)!$. In the equal-probability model,
\[
        \left(\frac{U_2^N}{a_{N,2}},\frac{U_3^N}{a_{N,3}},\ldots,\frac{U_J^N}{a_{N,J}}\right)
        \Rightarrow (W,W,\ldots,W),\qquad W\sim\Exp(1).
\]
For every fixed nonnegative integer vector $\mathbf m=(m_2,\ldots,m_J)$,
\[
        \E\prod_{j=2}^J\left(\frac{U_j^N}{a_{N,j}}\right)^{m_j}
        \to (m_2+\cdots+m_J)!.
\]
For $J=2$ this recovers the Papanicolaou--Doumas limit theorem \cite{PapanicolaouDoumas}.

body:
[Lemma lem:fkg of arXiv:2608.12954, 'Rainbow percolation'] Let $A_1,\dots,A_k$ be decreasing events of $\mathcal X$. Then
\[
   \mathbb P(A_1\cap\dots\cap A_k)\ \ge\ \prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb P(A_i).
\]
The same holds for the restriction of $\mathcal X$ to any measurable region,
in particular conditionally on the configuration in the complementary
region.

[Lemma lem:recovery-nonempty of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Fix $t>0$ and set $\bar F:=\bar A^{-1}\bar\gamma$. Suppose (lem:hk_ss_finite of the paper) holds. Then there exists a sequence $(\psi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset C_b^\infty(\bar E;\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that

\begin{equation}
  \int_{\bar E}\bar u(t,x)\,
  \big(\psi_k(x)-\bar F(x)\big)^\top\bar A(x)\big(\psi_k(x)-\bar F(x)\big)\,d\bar\pi(x)
  \longrightarrow 0,
\end{equation}

Then there are a neighborhood V of x* and a homeomorphism h: V -> h(V) in R^n with h(x*) = 0 that conjugates the nonlinear flow phi_t near x* to the linear flow exp(tA): h(phi_t(x)) = exp(tA) h(x) for x in V and every t with phi_s(x) in V for s between 0 and t, so orbits go to orbits with the direction of time kept. The discrete-time analogue holds for a diffeomorphism g with a hyperbolic fixed point x* (Dg(x*) has no eigenvalue of modulus 1): g is locally topologically conjugate near x* to Dg(x*).

body: Seifert-Van Kampen theorem: Let X be a topological space written as X = U union V, where U and V are open and path-connected and the intersection U intersect V is nonempty and path-connected, and choose a basepoint x_0 in U intersect V. Let i and j denote the homomorphisms pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(U, x_0) and pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(V, x_0) induced by inclusion. Then pi_1(X, x_0) is the pushout of i and j, i.e. the free product with amalgamation pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0) modulo the normal subgroup generated by all elements i(g) j(g)^{-1} with g in pi_1(U intersect V, x_0). In particular, if U intersect V is simply connected then pi_1(X, x_0) is the free product pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0). This lets one compute fundamental groups of spaces built from simpler pieces.
title: Seifert–Van Kampen theorem

body: [Lemma lem:component_jordan_domain of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $z \in \mathbf{H}$ and let $U$ be the connected component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus {\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ containing $z$. Then $\mathbf{F}(z)$ is a.s. the union of a simple curve $\eta_a$ from $0$ to $x(U)$, two simple curves $\eta_L$ and $\eta_R$ from $x(U)$ to $y(U)$ which form, respectively, the clockwise and counterclockwise boundary arcs of $\partial U$ from $x(U)$ to $y(U)$, and a simple curve $\eta_b$ from $y(U)$ to $\infty$. The curves $\eta_a, \eta_L, \eta_R$ and $\eta_b$ do not intersect except at $x(U)$ and $y(U)$, and the boundary conditions of $h$ given $\mathbf{F}(z)$ are those of the left (resp.\ right) side of a flow line of angle $\theta(U)$ on the left (resp.\ right) side of each of these curves.

[Theorem thm:finite-bank-bridge of arXiv:2608.20295, 'Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries'] Assume the sandwich relation
in Equation~(equation eq:aeb-sandwich of the paper).

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]

\item
If a truth-level assertion $g$ satisfies
Equation~(equation eq:universal-truth-predicate of the paper), then $g$ holds for every explanation in
the exhaustive finite-bank profile
$\mathcal A_{\mathcal B}(W)$.

\item
If opposing ambiguity witnesses belong to $L_k$, then both belong to
$\mathcal A_{\mathcal B}(W)$, so the exhaustive finite-bank profile contains
the corresponding ambiguity.

\item
If $F\subseteq C$, certification of a fine-cell assertion for $F$ also
certifies the corresponding sector assertion for $C$.

\end{enumerate}

These statements hold at every reached query prefix, including a
data-dependent stopping prefix. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[ \left|\frac{d^m}{d\xi^m} \varphi(\xi)\right| \le \|r_D\|_{\mu} \|x^m\|_{\mu}. \]

[Lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\mu_t$ be the distribution after running stochastic localization with the $\Id$ driving matrix for time $t$ initialized at $\mu_{H_N}$.
    Then $\mu_t$ arises as the Gibbs distribution of the Hamiltonian $H_{N,t}(\sigma)$:
    \[
        H_{N,t}(\sigma) = H_N(\sigma) + \angles*{\by_t, \sigma}\mcom
    \]
    where 
    \[
        (H_N, \by_t) \stacker{law}{=} (H_N, t\bx + \sqrt{t} \bg)\mcom
    \]
    where $\bx \sim \ScS_N$, $H_N \sim \mu_{\pl}(\cdot | \bx)$, and $\bg\sim\calN(0,\Id_N)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sam'

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $\msp \in X$ be a point, $Z_1, \dots, Z_k$ irreducible closed subsets of $X$ such that $\msp \in Z_i$ and $\dim Z_i > 0$ for any $i$, and let $g_1, \dots, g_m \in R$ be homogeneous polynomials.
Suppose that $X$ is quasismooth at $\msp$ and that $\{g_1, \dots, g_m\}$ isolates $\msp$.
We set $G_i \coloneq (g_i = 0)_X$, and we set
\[
\mu \coloneq \min \Set{ \frac{\omult_{\msp} (G_i)}{\deg g_i} | 1 \le i \le m}.
\]
Then, there exists an effective $\mbQ$-divisor $T \sim_{\mbQ} A$ such that $\omult_{\msp} (T) \ge \mu$ and $T$ does not contain any $Z_i$ in its support.
In particular, there exists an effective $\mbQ$-divisor $T' \sim_{\mbQ} d A$, where
\[
d \coloneq \max \Set{ \deg (g_i) | 1 \le i \le m},
\]
such that $\omult_{\msp} (T') \ge 1$ and $T'$ does not contain any $Z_i$ in its support.

body:
Let k be an algebraically closed field and R = k[x_1, ..., x_n]. Weak form: every proper ideal I of R has a common zero, that is, V(I) = {a in k^n : f(a) = 0 for all f in I} is nonempty; equivalently every maximal ideal of R has the form (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n). Strong form: for every ideal I, the ideal of polynomials vanishing on V(I) is the radical of I: if g in R vanishes on V(I) then g^m in I for some m >= 1. Hence V and I give an inclusion-reversing bijection between radical ideals of R and algebraic subsets of k^n.
k algebraically closed (over R, for example, x^2 + 1 has no zero and the weak form fails)

body:
[Proposition 19 (Critical local linear BSDE) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Let \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), and \(r\) be progressively measurable on
\(\Omega\times I\), with values in \(\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb R^m\), and
\(\mathbb R\), respectively.  Assume that \(\beta\mathbin{\cdot}W\in
\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb P;I)\), and let
\[
 L_t^\beta
 :=\exp\left(
  \int_u^t\beta_s\,dW_s
  -\frac12\int_u^t\lvert\beta_s\rvert^2\,ds
 \right),\qquad
 \frac{d\mathbb Q}{d\mathbb P}\bigg|_{\mathcal F_v}=L_v^\beta .
\]
Thus \(L_u^\beta=1\).  Suppose the BMO--Girsanov constants are those of
Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-bmo-girsanov}.  Let
\(r_A>1\), set \(p_A=r_A/(r_A-1)\), and assume
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\tau\in\mathcal T_I}
 \left\|
  \mathbb E_\tau^{\mathbb Q}
  \exp\left(r_A\int_\tau^v\alpha_s^+\,ds\right)
 \right\|_\infty
 \leq K_A<\infty .
 
\end{equation}
Assume also that \(\int_u^v\lvert\alpha_s\rvert ds<\infty\) almost surely,
\(\eta\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_v)\), and
\(r\in\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)\).  Then
\eqref{eq:critical-linear-bsde} has a unique solution in
\(\mathbb S^\infty(I)\times\mathbb H^2_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb P;I)\), and
\begin{equation}
 \|R\|_{\mathbb S^\infty(I)}
 \leq K_A^{1/r_A}
 \left(
  \|\eta\|_\infty+
  \|r\|_{\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)}
 \right).
 
\end{equation}
Under \(\mathbb Q\), one admissible BMO bound is
\begin{equation}
 \|S\mathbin{\cdot}W^{\mathbb Q}\|_{
       \mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb Q;I)}^2
 \leq
 \|\eta\|_\infty^2
 +\frac{2\|R\|_\infty^2}{r_A}\log K_A
 +2\|R\|_\infty
   \|r\|_{\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)}.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, \eqref{eq:bmo-norm-equivalence} gives a deterministic bound
for \(S\mathbin{\cdot}W\) under \(\mathbb P\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Critical local linear BSDE

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Given $V\in\cC^{7}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ a $0$-regular potential (see Definition \ref{definition:kregular}), and $f\in\cC^{0}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$. Let $Y^N$ be a multimatrix model with potential $V$ (see Definition \ref{def:randompot}). Then, almost surely, 
$$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \norm{f(Y^N)} = \norm{f\circ T^0(x)}, $$
where $x$ is a $d$-tuple of free semicircular variables, and $T^0$ is the map from Theorem \ref{mainthm}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:cone of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] For any $u_1>1$, we choose a small constant $d_0>0$ and a large constant $n_1>64\, d_0^2$ such that the following construction is possible for all $n>n_1$ and $1\le m\le n$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$]
        \item On the unit sphere, we pick $n$ unit vectors $(v_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ such that $|v_i-v_{i'}|>12\,d_0\,n^{-1/2}$ for any $1\le i<i'\le n$. Let $S_i:=\mathsf{C}(v_i,d_0/\sqrt n)$, $1\le i\le n$, be $n$ disjoint cones.
        \item On each surface $S_i\cap\partial \mathcal{B}_0$, we further pick $m$ points $v_{i,j}$ along an arc such that the following properties hold.
        Let $c_0$ and $c_1$ be two small positive constants. Consider two smaller cones
        \[
        T_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},u_1^{-n}) \quad \text{and} \quad V_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},c_0m^{-1}n^{-1/2}).
        \]
        For any $i,j$, we have $T_{i,j}\subseteq V_{i,j}\subseteq S_i$, $\mathrm{dist}(v_{i,j},\partial S_i)\ge c_1\, n^{-1/2}$, and $V_{i,j}\cap V_{i,l}=\varnothing$ if $j\neq l$. Moreover, if $1\le j<l\le m$, then $ |z/|z|-v_{i,l}|\geq c_1|j-l|/(m\sqrt n)$  for every $z\in V_{i,j}$.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition prop:two_r of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l')
\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Then, for each $1 \le s \le n$, the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} |r_{ss}|^2 \bigr]
\]
 vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\begin{align*}
&\alpha_1 ! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow (m+1)} n^{\uparrow (l+1)}} \\
& \qquad \times
\begin{cases}
 ( (n+m)(n+l) -(\alpha_s+1)(2n+m+l) +(\alpha_s+1)(\alpha_s+2) ) & \text{if $s<n$},
\\
 ( n +(m-\alpha_n)(l-\alpha_n) + \alpha_n ) & \text{if $s=n$},
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
where $\alpha_k:=\mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j}\sqcup\bm{i}')$
for all $k=1,2,\dots, n$.

[Theorem 42 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Assume that $\Gamma_{\mu}$ is strongly irreducible 
and that the image of $\Gamma_{\mu}$ in the projective linear group 
${\rm PGL}(V)$ is not contained in any compact subgroup of ${\rm PGL}(V)$. 
Assume also that $\mu$ admits a finite exponential moment \eqref{Exponential-moment}. 
Let $f$ be a compactly supported continuous function on $\bb R$. 
Then, uniformly in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,   
\begin{align*}
\upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  \bb E  \Big( f (\log \|g_n \cdots g_1 \| - n \lambda_{\mu} - w_n)  \Big) 
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  \int_{\bb R} f(u) du. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 42 of arXiv:2607.19873

    \E\sup_{v\in T}\abs*{\sum_{i=1}^N \ip{Z_i}{v}^p - N \E \ip{Z}{v}^p} 
    \lesssim_{K,p} \gamma(T)^p + \sqrt{N}\gamma(T)\rad(T)^{p-1},
    $$
    where the sign $\lesssim_{K,p}$ hides factors that depend only on $K$ and $p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2607.22892, 'Mirror Langevin diffusions: Convergence rates and Markov chain approximations'] Let $e^{-F}= (\nabla u)_{\#e^{-V}}$, as before. Suppose the following assumptions hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
     \item $e^{-F}$ satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality. 
     \item $F$ is $L$-smooth, i.e., $\norm{\nabla F(y) - \nabla F(x)}\le L \norm{y-x}$, for all $x,y$.
     \item The convex function $u$ satisfies Assumption \ref{asmp:MCconv} (i) and (ii). 
     \item The initial variable $X^\eps_0$ has a density $p^\eps_0$ such that $\chi^2(p^\eps_0 \mid \mu) < \infty$. 
 \end{enumerate}
 Then, there exists a constant $c_0>0$ such that for all $\eps \in (0,1)$, if $p^\eps_k$ is the density of $X^\eps_k$ then 
 \[
 \chi^2\left( p^\eps_k  \mid \mu\right) \le (1 - c_0 \eps)^k \chi^2(p^\eps_0 \mid \mu), \quad \forall\; k \in \mathbb{N}. 
 \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 6 (Aldous' criterion for tightness {\cite[Theorem~16.10) of arXiv:2604.21143, 'Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model'] {Billingsley1999}}]
		Let $T > 0$, and let $\{X^n\}$ be a sequence of c\`adl\`ag $\Rd$-valued processes on $[0,T]$.
		If the following two conditions hold, then $\{X^n\}$ is tight in $D([0,T]; \Rd)$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every $t \in [0,T]$, the family of laws of $\{X^n_t\}$ is tight in $\Rd$.
			\item For every $\eta > 0$ and every sequence of stopping times $\{\tau_n\}$ bounded by $T$,
			\[
			\lim_{\delta \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le \theta \le \delta} \P\left( |X^n_{(\tau_n + \theta) \wedge T} - X^n_{\tau_n}| \ge \eta \right) = 0\,.
			\]
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix any $\delta\in(0,1)$, and set
$
\tilde{\varepsilon}:=\frac{\delta}{20\tau},
\bar\varepsilon:=\frac{\tilde{\varepsilon}}{4.4\tau},
\varepsilon:=\frac{\bar\varepsilon}{4\tau}
$.
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\bm d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)
$
denote its degree sequence. Suppose that $v_1,\dots,v_{\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil}$ are vertices with degrees greater than $n^{2\tilde\varepsilon}$. Let $\tilde A$ denote the event that, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$, the vertex $v_a$ has at least $\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$ pairwise distinct neighbors
$
u_1^{(a)},\dots,u_{\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil}^{(a)}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{u_b^{(a)}:1\le a\le \lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil ,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct, and have degrees between $n^{\bar\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\bar\varepsilon}
$. Moreover, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$ and each $b=1,\dots, \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$, the vertex $u_b^{(a)}$ has at least $ \lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil$ distinct neighbors
$
w_{a,b,1},\dots,w_{a,b,\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{w_{a,b,m}:1\le a\le\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil,\ 1\le m\le\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct and have degrees between
$n^{\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\varepsilon}$. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\tilde A\mid \bm d)\ge 1-\exp(-n^{\bar\varepsilon(\tau-2)/2})-\exp(-n^{\varepsilon/2}), \qquad \text{on the event $D_{\varepsilon}$ defined in \eqref{eq_D}. }
\end{equation}

[Defi 41 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Let $\cG/k$ be a finite gerbe whose geometric inertia has order invertible in
$k$.  Its \emph{quotient-compression dimension} is
\[
\operatorname{qcdim}_k(\cG)
=
\min\left\{\dim S:\
\begin{array}{l}
(S,s)\text{ is a tame quotient singularity over }k,\\
\cG_{(S,s)}\simeq\cG
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
If no such realization exists, we set $\operatorname{qcdim}_k(\cG)=\infty$.

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that the hypotheses in Theorem \ref{Theorem: Main}
hold, and that $\msf T_0(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion in \eqref{Equation: Smooth Heat Trace}.
Let $t_1>t_2>\cdots>0$ be a vanishing sequence of positive numbers.
The following holds for any fixed $\ka>0$:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1/2-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}2\pi t_n\,\msf T_\ka(t_n)=\msf{A}(D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}4\sqrt{2\pi t_n}\left(\tfrac{\msf{A}(D)}{2\pi}t_n^{-1}-\msf T_\ka(t_n)\right)=\msf{L}(\partial D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]

[Theorem thm:ub of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] In the setting of (thm:1 of the paper), fix $n\geq 1$ and $K>0$, let $\rho_n(x)$ be the maximum vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ above $x+(\frac{L}2,0)$ for $-N_n^{2/3} \leq x\leq N_n^{2/3}$,
and set $\sigma^2>0$ as per (def:sigma of the paper). 
Then every weak limit point $\mathbf{Y}_n(t)$ of the process $Y_n(t):=N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$ ($t\in[-K,K]$), as $L\to\infty$, satisfies
\[ \mathbf{Y}_n \preceq \mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,. \]
Moreover, for every fixed $m$, every weak limit point $({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ of the processes $(Y_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ satisfies
\[ ({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n)_{n\leq m} \preceq \bigotimes_{n\leq m}\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.10051, 'Ergodicity of the voter model with dynamic anti-voter bonds'] Consider a Markov chain with a countable state space~$\mathcal{S}$ and~$Q$-matrix~$\{q(x,y): x,y \in \mathcal S\}$ that satisfy~\eqref{eq_q_finite}. [Theorem maincvlawera of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $\mathbf m, \mathbf m',\mathbf m_n$, $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, be $\mathbb{T}^*$-valued r.v.s. 
Let $(h_p)_{p\in \mathbb{N}}$ be an $\mathbb{R}^*_+$-valued sequence strictly decreasing to $0$. Then the following holds true.
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] $\mathbf m$ and $\mathbf m'$ have the same law iff for all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, ${\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m$ and ${\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m'$ have the same law. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$]  Let us assume that ${\cal E}_{h_n-h_{n+1}}\mathbf m_{n+1}$ has the same law as $\mathbf m_n$. 
Then, there exists a $\mathbb{T}^*\! $-valued r.v.~$\mathbf m''$, unique in law and such that ${\cal E}_{h_n}  \mathbf m''$ has the same law as $\mathbf m_n$, for all $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$.  

\item[$(iii)$] $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ iff for all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, 
${\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m_n \! \to \! {\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iv)$] The laws of $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight in $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ iff the laws of 
$(\langle \mathbf m_n \rangle)_{n\in \mathbb{N}} $ are tight in $\mathbb{R}_+$ and for all fixed $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, 
the laws of $(\mathtt{Ht} ({\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m_n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$  are tight in $\mathbb{R}_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(v)$] Let us assume that $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is 
$\mathbb{T}$-valued and that $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. Then, the following assertions are equivalent.
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(a)$] ${\bf P}$-a.s.~$\mathbf m\! \in \!  \mathbb{T}$, and $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(b)$] ${\bf P}$-a.s.~${\boldsymbol{\lambda}}_{\mathbf m} \! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f(\mathbb{R}_+)$, and the random finite measures 
$({\boldsymbol{\lambda}}_{\mathbf m_n})_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$  on $\mathbb{R}_+$ converge to $ {\boldsymbol{\lambda}}_{\mathbf m}$ in law in $\mathcal{M}_f(\mathbb{R}_+)$. 
\smallskip
\end{compactenum}

\item[$(vi)$] For all $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, let us assume that 
a.s.~$(\mathbf T^{ n}, \mathbf d_n, \rho_n, \mathtt m_n)\! \equiv\! \mathbf m_n \! \in \!  \mathbb{T}$.  
Then the laws of $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$ iff they are tight in $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ and 
\begin{equation}

\forall \varepsilon, \eta \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+, \quad \lim_{h\to 0} \, \sup_{n\in \mathbb{N}} {\bf P} \Big( \mathtt m_n \big( \mathbf T^{n} \backslash (\mathbf T^n_{\! \mathtt m_n , h})^{(\varepsilon)}\big) \! > \!  \eta \Big) = 0\; .
\end{equation}
where $(\mathbf T^n_{\! \mathtt m_n , h})^{(\varepsilon)}\! :=\! \{ \sigma \! \in \!  \mathbf T^{n}: \mathbf d_n ( \sigma , \mathbf T^n_{\! \mathtt m_n , h})\! \leq \!  \varepsilon\}$. 
\smallskip
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem maincvlawera of arXiv:2608.09856

[Theorem thm:compregime of arXiv:2606.01866, 'Phase Transition of a Semiflexible Membrane in Two Dimensions'] For $d=2$, let $\{\phi_x\}_{x\in V_N}$ be the centered Gaussian interface, zero outside $V_N$, whose covariance is $G_N$. For each fixed $\lambda\in[0,2]$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, the following holds for $x,y\in V_N^\delta\coloneq V_{\lfloor (1-\delta)N\rfloor}$: As $N\to\infty$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item(Long-range covariance) If $\|x-y\|\gtrsim N^{\lambda/2}$, then
        \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=\operatorname{Cov}^\nabla_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(1).\]
        Here, $\operatorname{Cov}^\nabla_N$ denotes the covariance of the two-dimensional DGFF on $V_N$, with zero boundary condition.
        \item(Short-range covariance) If $\|x-y\|\ll N^{\lambda/2}$, then 
        \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=\frac{2-\lambda}{\pi}\log N+O(1).\]
    \end{enumerate}
    The asymptotic notation such as $\gtrsim$ or $\ll$ is defined later; see (ch:notation of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covariance calculation for competition regime

[Theorem Theorem1.1 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Let $\zeta$ be a mean 0, variance 1 random variable with a subgaussian tail. We also assume that $\zeta$ has a finite Log-Sobolev constant.

Let $A_n$ be an $n\times n$ symmetric random matrix with upper-diagonal entries $\{A_{i,j}\}_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n}$ being independent and identically distributed with distribution $\zeta$, and $A_{ij}=A_{ji}.$

Fix two positive numbers $\kappa>0$ and $\Delta>0$, and consider two locations $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in[-(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n},(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n}]$ such that $|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|\geq \Delta n^{1/2}$. 

Then there exist constants $C>0,c>0$ depending only on the random variable $\zeta$ and the constants $\kappa,\Delta$ such that for any $\delta_1,\delta_2\geq 0$, we have the following singular value estimate jointly at $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$:
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbb{P}\left(\sigma_{min}(A_n-\lambda_1 I_n)\leq\delta_1 n^{-1/2},\sigma_{min}(A_n-\lambda_2 I_n)\leq\delta_2 n^{-1/2}\right)\leq C\delta_1\delta_2+2e^{-cn}. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Theorem1.1 of arXiv:2504.15992

An elementary probability control, not an FPP counterexample. If J is uniform on {1,...,m} and A_i={J=i}, each deterministic event has probability 1/m, while P(union_i A_i)=1. Equivalently, each threshold indicator has mean 1/m and their maximum is always one. Therefore an estimate for every deterministic pair of endpoints does not automatically control a pair chosen after observing the environment. For the square boundary S_n in Z^2 there are 8n sites and at most 64n^2 ordered endpoint pairs; a raw union bound needs a per-pair bound o(n^-2) to vanish. Qualitative midpoint decay supplies no such conclusion. Independence of the resampled edge from its outside environment is valid; multiplying success probabilities for correlated endpoint capacities or selected corridors needs an additional justified filtration or independence argument.

[Definition def:sc-dressing of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We say that $K \colon \mathcal{V} \to \mathrm{End}(H)$ is
\emph{dressing compatible} with $(\Psi, \Phi)$ if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item For every $u \in \mathcal{V}$ and $j \geq 2$,
\begin{align}
K(Tu) - K(u) &= \Psi(Tu)\Phi(Tu),
   \\
\partial_1 K(u) &= \Psi(Tu)C_1(u)\Phi(u),
   \\
K(S_j u) - K(u)
  &= \Psi(Tu)C_j(u)\Phi(S_j u).
  
\end{align}
\item There exists $z \in \mathbb{F}$ such that the resolvent
exists at every vertex:
\[
R(u) \vcentcolon= (I - zK(u))^{-1} \in \mathrm{End}(H),
\qquad u \in \mathcal{V}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 17 of arXiv:2608.26618, 'A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs'] Let $\eta_n=\log n$ and
\[
C_S
=
g\log m+s\log d+2\log(g+1)
+2\sum_{k\in G}\log(t_k+1).
\]
Assume that $g^*\le d^\gamma$ for some constant $\gamma\ge0$.
For every
$
\lambda\ge
\lambda_{\mathrm{sel}}\vee
c_{\alpha,\zeta}(1+\gamma)^{2/\alpha},
$
with $c_{\alpha,\zeta}>0$ sufficiently large, if the following
conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(\romannumeral 1)]
    There exists a sufficiently large constant $c_1>1$ such that,
    for every $S\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sub}}$,
    \[
    \mathrm{APP}(S)\ge
    c_1\left\{
    (s^*-s)\log n
    +\lambda\left(C_{S^*}^{2/\alpha}-C_S^{2/\alpha}\right)
    +\log^{2/\alpha}N\bigl(\Delta^-(S)\bigr)
    \right\}.
    \]

    \item[(\romannumeral 2)]
    For every $S\in\mathcal M_w$ satisfying $2B_S>u_S$,
    \[
    \mathrm{APP}(S)\ge2(2B_S-u_S).
    \]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\Pr\left\{
\min_{\substack{S\in\mathcal M_n\\S\neq S^*}}
\mathrm{DCIC}(S)>\mathrm{DCIC}(S^*)
\right\}
\to1
\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 17 of arXiv:2608.26618

    \item  We have

    \]
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 3 (Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] Let \(f\in C(\mathbb R^n)\).

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\le\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has \(u(x_0)\le0\) or
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\le0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if \(u\ge0\) in \(\mathbb R^n\) and, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\ge\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\ge0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity solution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.
title: Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem
Finite-time blow-up

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify gamma and v from known exponents and locate the missing joint convergence. Result: gamma = 1: the intrinsic one-arm probability is of order 1/n (Kozma-Nachmias), so n P_{p_c}(intrinsic radius >= n) is bounded, matching the canonical measure normalisation; v is the variance per intrinsic step of the spatial displacement, given by the lace expansion two-point function through the intrinsic-distance two-point function (C0079). The finite-dimensional distributions of the process in t are the intrinsic r-point functions with fixed intrinsic distances, which are the objects of C0079 (Open Problem 15.5) at the level of r = 2; the source's Theorem 15.4 handles the number-of-pivotals two-point function, and the intrinsic distance version is the missing step. Given the intrinsic r-point functions, convergence of finite-dimensional distributions to SBM follows as in the oriented case (Hofstad-Slade), and tightness follows from the one-arm bound and a modulus-of-continuity estimate for the intrinsic exploration. So the problem reduces to Open Problem 15.5 extended to r-point functions. Obstruction: Intrinsic-distance r-point functions not lace-expanded for unoriented percolation.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.30400, 'What to Expect When You're Expecting'] Let \(n\ge2\). For \(1\le k\le n\), say that the extended expectation of the sum is determined by \(k\)-marginals if the following holds: whenever \(X=\left(X_1,\ldots,X_n\right)\) and \(Y=\left(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\right)\) are random vectors in \(\R^n\) such that \(\left(X_i\right)_{i\in S}\stackrel{d}=\left(Y_i\right)_{i\in S}\) for every \(S\subseteq\left[n\right]\) with \(\lvert S\rvert\le k\), and both \(\E\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\) and \(\E\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\) are defined, then
\[
\E\sum_{i=1}^nX_i=\E\sum_{i=1}^nY_i.
\]
We term the least such \(k\) the marginal degree of sums in dimension \(n\) and denote it by \(\sigma\left(n\right)\).
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.30400

[Proposition pro: Wasserstein-$p$ bound without exchangeability final version of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Let $X\in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a random vector, and $T: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function. Suppose $T(X)$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[|T(X)|^p] < \infty$ for some $p > 1$. We assume Assumptions (assumption: Stein identity final version of the paper), (assumption: Kramers-Moyal expansion final version of the paper) and (assumption: integrability of Kramers-Moyal coefficients final version of the paper)
     hold for $X$ with operator $\mathcal{A}$ and mapping $T$. Then for any $t_0 > 0$, we have the following upper bound for Wasserstein-$p$ distance between $\mathcal{L}(T(X))$ and $\mathcal{L}(Z')$, 
    \begin{align}
        W_p(\mathcal{L}(T(X)), \mathcal{L}(Z')) &\leq g_0(t_0,p) + \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - a_{k}^{\mathcal{L}_{OU}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &= g_0(t_0,p) + g_1(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[| a_{1}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) + T(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &+ g_2(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{2}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - 1|^p]^{1/p} + \sum_{k=3}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p}, 
    \end{align}
    where $Z'\sim N(0,1)$ and the coefficients $g_k(t_0,p)$ for $k\ge 0$
are continuous in $(t_0,p)$ and are given explicitly in (equation eq: W-p bound final of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wasserstein-$p$ bound via generator comparison

[Corollary cor:ev_continuity of arXiv:2511.22162, 'Landau Hamiltonian with Gaussian white noise potential and the asymptotics of its bottom o'] For all $n \ge 1$, the eigenvalue $\lambda^B_n = \lambda^B_n(\bA, q)$ of $\Phi^B(\bA, q)$ is a locally Lipschitz function of $(\bA, q) \in \ccM$. Namely, for all $R>0$ and $\bA, q, \bar\bA, \bar q$ with norms bounded by $R$, one has
	\[|\lambda^B_n(\bA, q) - \lambda^B_n(\bar\bA, \bar q)| \leq C_R \left(\left\| q - \bar q \right\|_{\ccM(B)} + \left\| \bA - \bar \bA \right\|_{\ccA(B)}\right),\]
	for some $C_R > 0$.

[Proposition prop:basic-facts-zero of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let gamble space $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be given.
  Then we have
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}\, 0 \geq 0$ if and only if $\mathcal{Z}$ is arbitrage-free.
  \item $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}\, 0 \leq 0$ when $\mathcal{Z}$ contains zero.
  \end{enumerate}
  In particular, $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}\, c = c$ for all $c\in\mathbb{R}$ when both conditions hold ($\mathcal{Z}$ is normalized).

[Proposition propE3 of arXiv:2411.04238, 'Holomorphic jump-diffusions'] (Theorem 2.4.1, Theorem 6.2.14, Theorem 6.2.4 and Theorem 11.1.2 in [B:11] and  Theorem 19.3 in [Rudin:86])
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Order and type of an entire function do not change under differentiation. 
    \item  Non-constant entire functions of order strictly smaller than 1 are unbounded on lines.
    \item Let $\tau\in (0,\infty)$ and let
$B_\tau$ be the set of  
 all entire functions of exponential type  $\tau$, which are bounded on the real axis.  Then  $h\in B_\tau$ implies 
 $$|h(z)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)| \exp(\tau |\Im(z)|).$$
 Moreover, in this case we also have that $h'\in B_\tau$, 
$\sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h'(x)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)|\tau$
for all $z\in \mathbb C$, and thus in particular 
 $$|h'(z)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)| \tau \exp(\tau |\Im(z)|).$$
 \item {\textbf{Paley--Wiener theorem}} Let $h\in H(\mathbb C)$ be an entire function of exponential type $\tau$ such that 
 $$\int_{\mathbb R}|h(x)|^2dx<\infty.$$
 Then there exists $g\in L^2(-\tau,\tau)$ such that
 $h(z)=\int_{-\tau}^\tau g(t)e^{itz}dt$ for each $z\in \mathbb C$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition propE3 of arXiv:2411.04238

body: [Proposition 4.5 of arXiv:2510.05566, 'Domain-Shift-Aware Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models'] relates the conservativeness term πn+1 to the effective sample size neff. When the estimated weights are reasonably balanced, neff is large and the upper bound shows that the extra mass placed on ∞is small, so the upper bound in Theorem 4.4 stays close to the target level. Conversely, when only a few calibration points receive most of the weight, neff becomes small.

[Corollary 42 (Self-improvement) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A} and put
$\XX^{(n)} := \{ x \in \XX : T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi \}$ for $n \in \N$. Then
$\XX^{(n)} \subseteq \XX^{(n+1)}$ for every $n \in \N$. Hence the condition
``for every $x \in \XX$ there is a number $n \in \N$ with
$T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi$'' already implies ``for every $x \in \XX$ there is a
number $n_{0}(x) \in \N$ such that $T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi$ for \emph{every}
$n \ge n_{0}(x)$''.

[Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Let $a_n$ be a sequence such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$. Let $(\xi^{n,k})_{k\in{\mathbb N}}$ be a sequence of  $i.i.d.$ random vectors in  ${\mathbb R}^d$. Suppose that their moments satisfy:
  $${\mathbb E} \xi^{n,1}=m+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  and $${\mathbb E}(\xi^{n,1}_i-m_i)(\xi^{n,1}_j-m_j)=\sigma_{ij}+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  for some $m\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and some covariance matrix $C=(\sigma_{ij})_{d\times d}$. Let $b_n\in{\mathbb R}^d$ be a sequence such that $|b_{n}|=O\left(\sqrt{n}+a_n^2\right)$.
  Suppose that there exists $R>0$ such that for all $\eta\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and $|\eta|<R$, $\sup_n\log {\mathbb E}\exp(\eta\cdot \xi^n)<\infty$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item   Let $N(\lambda_n n)$ be an independent Poisson process with $\lambda_n=\lambda+O(\frac{1}{n})$. The sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N(\lambda_n n)}\xi^{n,k}-\lambda m n+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, (C+mm^T)l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C+mm^T$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals  
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,(C+mm^T)^{-1}x\>.}$$
    \item For any $\lambda>0$ and $u\in{\mathbb R}$, the sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\xi^{n,k}-(\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n})m+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, C l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,C^{-1}x\>.}$$
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471

[Prop Meromorphic continuation and difference equation of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] The function $\widehat \pi_1$ admits a meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ and satisfies the difference equation
\[
\widehat \pi_1(y(s+(\mu_1+\mu_2)))=\widehat G(s)\,\widehat \pi_1(y(s)),

\widehat G(s):=\frac{k_1(s)\,k_2(\zeta s)}{k_2(s)\,k_1(\zeta s)}
=\frac{(s-s_1)(s+s_2+\mu_2)}{(s-s_2)(s+s_1+\mu_2)}.
\]
Moreover, the functional equation and the invariance properties by $\widehat\eta$ and $\widehat\zeta$ extend to the whole complex plane $\mathbb{C}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
